sections.title: 2. Who the exam is for
sections.html:
As a candidate for this Microsoft Certification, you’re an Azure AI engineer who builds, manages, and deploys agents and AI solutions that take advantage of Microsoft Foundry.

For this exam, you should have experience developing apps by using Python, and you need to be familiar with the capabilities of general AI, generative AI, and Azure services.

Your responsibilities include:

  • Planning and managing Azure AI solutions.
  • Implementing generative AI and agentic solutions.
  • Implementing computer vision solutions.
  • Implementing text analysis solutions.
  • Implementing information extraction solutions.

In this role, you collaborate with business stakeholders, solution architects, data scientists, DevOps engineers, and cloud security engineers to design, implement, and maintain AI solutions.

Source: Official study guide (audience profile), updated 2026-10-15.

sections.title: 4. How to read the skills measured
sections.html:
• The bullets illustrate how a skill is assessed; related topics may appear (Microsoft's own note in the study guide). Treat each bullet as a heading for everything around it.
  • Most questions cover generally available (GA) features, but Preview features can appear when they are commonly used. Where the documentation labels something preview, retired or renamed, this guide says so.
  • Expect code and syntax questions (read the code once for what it does, then check names, signatures and order) next to scenario and decision questions. Exact names matter.
  • Case studies present a business scenario followed by several questions. Read the requirements and constraints once, then answer every question against them. Microsoft's break rules differ inside case-study and problem/solution sets.

sections.title: Overview and official dates
sections.html:
Microsoft's Skills Hub announcement (published 3 March 2026, timeline updated 28 May 2026) lists Azure AI Engineer Associate (Exam AI-102) as a retiring certification and names Azure AI Apps and Agents Developer Associate (Exam AI-103) as its replacement certification. Candidates who had not yet registered for AI-102 are told to prepare for and take AI-103 instead. AI-103 is a new certification with a new exam rather than a renamed AI-102, and the announcement describes no bridge or upgrade path.

Other differences on the Learn pages

  • Exam time: 100 minutes (AI-102) → 120 minutes (AI-103).

AI-102 had six skill areas and AI-103 has five. Planning and management now weighs more, generative AI and agents are merged into the largest area, and the language and knowledge-mining areas each lose five points. Weights are published as ranges.

Inside the areas, AI-103 splits planning into model and service choice, Foundry set-up, management and monitoring, and responsible AI for agentic systems. The vision area is rebuilt around image and video generation, multimodal understanding and multimodal safety.

How this comparison was made

The AI-103 study guide has no change log, so the lists in this section are this app's own bullet-by-bullet comparison of the last AI-102 outline (skills as of 23 December 2025) with the AI-103 outline (skills as of 16 April 2026).

Sources: AI-102 study guide · AI-103 study guide

sections.title: What is new or expanded
sections.html:
These AI-103 outline bullets have no equivalent in the last AI-102 outline, or they widen a topic that AI-102 only touched.

Planning, security and responsible AI (area 1)

  • New “Manage quotas, scaling, rate limits, and cost footprints for model and agent workloads”.
  • New “Monitor model performance, drift, safety events, and grounding quality” and “Monitor data ingestion quality, search index health, and relevance performance”.
  • New “Configure security, including managed identity, private networking, keyless credentials, and role policies” (AI-102 asked about protecting account keys and managing authentication).
  • New Responsible AI for agentic systems: evaluators, safety evaluations and explanation tooling; auditing through trace logging, provenance metadata and approval workflows; agent oversight modes, constraints and tool-access controls.

Generative AI and agents (area 2, 30–35%)

  • New Agents move from a separate 5–10% area into the largest area. The AI-103 group is more design-oriented than AI-102's six bullets: define agent roles, goals, conversation-tracking approach and tool schemas; retrieval, function-calling and conversation memory; agent tools (APIs, knowledge stores, search, content understanding, custom functions); orchestrated multi-agent solutions; autonomous or semiautonomous workflows with safeguards and approval flow controls; monitoring, behavior evaluation and error analysis. Agent workloads also appear in areas 1 and 2 (infrastructure, deployments, quotas, governance).
  • New “Design workflows, tool-augmented flows, and multistep reasoning pipelines”, and evaluation that detects fabrications, relevance, quality and safety.
  • New Chain-of-thought evaluations and self-critique loops (AI-102 had “Implement model reflection”); observability that adds token analytics, safety signals and latency breakdowns to tracing (AI-102 had “Enable tracing and collect feedback”); “hybrid LLM and rules engines” (AI-102 had “Implement orchestration of multiple generative AI models”).

Vision, text and extraction (areas 3 to 5)

  • New Image and video generation: text prompts plus reference media, inpainting and mask-based edits, editing generated videos, generation and editing controls (AI-102 only had “Use the DALL-E model to generate images”).
  • New Multimodal understanding: captions, question answering grounded in visual evidence, alt text aligned to accessibility guidelines, single-task and pro-mode Content Understanding pipelines, video segments, objects and regions.
  • New Multimodal safety: classify unsafe visual content, detect and mitigate indirect prompt injection through embedded text in images, enforce visual policy rules (watermarks, prohibited symbols, brand usage).
  • New Text and speech: structured JSON outputs through generative prompting, domain outputs such as compliance summarization, LLM-powered translation flows, speech as an agent modality, multimodal reasoning from audio inputs.
  • New Retrieval: ingest and index documents, images, audio and video; hybrid search next to semantic and vector search; connect retrieval pipelines directly to workflows and agent tools; analyzers that output structured or markdown content.

Sources: AI-103 study guide · AI-102 study guide

sections.title: What was removed or is no longer named
sections.html:
None of the items below is named as such in the AI-103 skills outline. The study guide says its bullets illustrate how skills are assessed and that related topics may be covered, so treat these as lower priority rather than excluded.

  • Removed Custom vision models (7 AI-102 bullets): choose between image classification and object detection, label images, train, evaluate, publish and consume a custom image model, build one code-first.
  • Removed Custom language models (12 bullets): intents, entities and utterances; train, evaluate, deploy, optimize and back up a language understanding model; custom question answering (knowledge base, multi-turn conversations, chit-chat, export, multi-language); custom translation.
  • Removed Azure AI Document Intelligence (5 bullets): provision, prebuilt, custom, train and publish, and composed models. The outline does not name it, but the study guide's documentation list still links Azure AI Document Intelligence and the learning path “Extract insights from visual data on Azure” has a module “Extract data with Azure Document Intelligence”.
  • Removed Azure AI Search administration: provision a resource, create an index and define a skillset; create data sources and indexers and run an indexer; query syntax, sorting, filtering and wildcards; Knowledge Store projections. AI-103 keeps ingestion and indexing, custom or built-in enrichment skills, semantic, hybrid and vector search, and RAG ingestion at a higher level.
  • Removed Classic image and video analysis: select visual features, tags and object detection, interpret responses, Azure Vision text and handwriting extraction, Azure AI Video Indexer and Spatial Analysis.
  • Removed Classic text and speech APIs: key phrase extraction, language detection, PII detection, SSML, intent and keyword recognition. AI-103 frames text analysis as generative prompting plus Foundry Tools and mentions “sensitive content”.
  • Removed Set-up and platform bullets: separate service-selection bullets for vision, language, speech, information extraction and knowledge mining; create an Azure AI resource; provision an Azure OpenAI resource and submit prompts; install SDKs and APIs; determine a default endpoint; plan and implement a container deployment; deploy containers for local and edge devices; deploy a hub and project; prompt flow; prompt templates; fine-tune a generative model; “Plan for a solution that meets Responsible AI principles” and “Design a responsible AI governance framework”.
  • Removed Product names in the agent bullets: AI-102 named the Microsoft Foundry Agent Service and Microsoft Agent Framework, AI-103 says “by using Foundry”. The learning path “Develop AI agents on Azure” still teaches both.

Sources: AI-102 study guide · AI-103 study guide · Learning path: Extract insights from visual data on Azure · Learning path: Develop AI agents on Azure

sections.title: 1.1 Choose the appropriate Foundry services for generative AI and agents
sections.html:
Skills measured: choose a model for each task (LLMs, small language models, multimodal models, Foundry Tools) • choose Foundry services for generative tasks, grounding, vector search, agent workflows or multimodal processing • choose a retrieval and indexing method • choose memory, tool and knowledge integration services for agent solutions. Practise by deploying GPT-4.1 and a model router in one Foundry project, then grounding one prompt agent three ways (file search, Azure AI Search tool, Foundry IQ knowledge base) and comparing the answers. Implementation details are in §5.1 (retrieval and grounding pipelines) and §2.2 (building agents).

Names to expectThe exam mixes old and new wording. Azure AI Foundry is now Microsoft Foundry; Azure AI Services is now Foundry Tools; a hub plus Azure OpenAI and AI Services resources is now one Foundry resource with projects; the Assistants API (threads, runs) is now the Responses API (conversations, responses, agent versions); the roles Azure AI User, Owner, Account Owner and Project Manager are now Foundry User, Owner, Account Owner and Project Manager (same role IDs).

Choose an appropriate model for each task (LLMs, small language models, multimodal models, Foundry Tools)

The catalog has two groups. Foundry Models sold by Azure are hosted by Azure with guaranteed support and enterprise SLAs (all Azure OpenAI models plus selected Cohere, DeepSeek, Meta, Mistral AI and xAI models); some offer fungible provisioned throughput, so PTU quota and reservations can be shared across them. Models from partners and community (for example Anthropic Claude and Hugging Face models) are developed and generally supported by their providers, who decide whether a model deploys as serverless API (pay per token) or on managed compute (dedicated VMs billed per VM core hour; Preview deployment type).

NeedChooseWhy the tempting alternative fails
Live support chat: low latency, high volume, very long inputsGPT-4.1 family (-mini or -nano to cut cost)Non-reasoning and fast: 128K tokens, up to 1M with long context. GPT-5 adds latency and takes 272K input.
Multi-step planning, agentic tool use, code review, research reportsGPT-5 family (-mini, -nano variants) at medium (default) or high reasoning_effortGPT-4.1 has no adjustable reasoning depth.
Bulk transforms or triage where speed and cost dominateGPT-5 family at minimal or low efforthigh is slowest and costliest; minimal has no parallel tool calls.
Mixed-difficulty traffic behind one endpointModel router (Balanced mode)A fixed model overpays or underdelivers.
The model itself must reason over an image or diagram together with textA multimodal chat model such as GPT-4oText-only models take no image input; Vision and Content Understanding return analysis or extracted fields, not free reasoning.
Offline use, data must stay on the device, no per-token costFoundry Local with a small language model such as PhiCloud deployments need a network and bill per token.
Narrow task: OCR, forms, speech, translation, PII detectionA Foundry Tool (Document Intelligence, Vision, Speech, Translator, Language)Purpose-built, no prompt design needed.
Documents, images, audio and video into one user-defined schema with confidence scores and groundingContent UnderstandingDocument Intelligence, Vision and Speech each specialise in one input type, with no shared schema.
Change tone, format or task skill, not factsFine-tuningIt changes behaviour, not knowledge; use retrieval for private or changing data.
  • Model router is a trained language model you deploy like any Foundry model; it picks an underlying LLM for each prompt. Routing mode: Balanced (default; models within about 1–2% of the best quality, cheapest wins), Cost (about 5–6% band), Quality (best model, ignores cost). An optional model subset restricts the pool. Only Global Standard and Data Zone Standard deployments are supported, the effective context window is that of the smallest underlying model, and Claude models must be deployed from the catalog first.
  • Foundry Local runs on the user's device (ONNX Runtime): offline, no Azure subscription, no per-token cost; built for one user on constrained hardware, not as a multi-user server.
  • Model leaderboards Preview compare quality, safety (a lower attack success rate is better), performance and cost; shortlist there, then evaluate on your own data.
  • Foundry Tools (formerly Azure AI Services) include Speech, Translator, Language, Content Understanding, Document Intelligence, Vision and Azure AI Search. Anomaly Detector, Content Moderator, Language understanding, Metrics Advisor, Personalizer and QnA Maker are retired: don't use them in new apps.
Exam traps
  • A router deployment is limited to the smallest underlying model's context window, and Quality mode ignores cost entirely.
  • minimal reasoning effort blocks parallel tool calls; medium is the default, not low.
  • Foundry Local is single-user and on-device; concurrent users need a cloud deployment or a server stack such as vLLM or Triton.

Choose the appropriate Foundry services for generative tasks, grounding, vector search, agent workflows or multimodal processing

Foundry Agent Service gives three agent types plus a no-agent option. The choice sets how much you build and how much Foundry runs.

RequirementUseNotes
Fastest tool-using agent, nothing to hostPrompt agentDeclarative: instructions, model and tools, defined in the portal, SDK or REST. Foundry runs it; no containers.
Real-time spoken conversationVoice-based prompt agentWebSocket connection; Voice Live handles speech in and out. Parts are Preview. Text-only needs a plain prompt agent.
Your own code or framework (Agent Framework, LangGraph) run by FoundryHosted agentYour container with a managed endpoint, scaling and identity. If instructions and tools are enough, use a prompt agent.
Agent code already runs elsewhere; you only want Foundry models and toolsResponses API called directlyNo agent resource to manage.
New multi-agent orchestrationMicrosoft Agent FrameworkFoundry Workflows (UI builder) is Preview and retiring December 1, 2026.
Ground answers in a few uploaded filesFile search with a vector storeManaged; lighter than Foundry IQ.
Vector or hybrid search over your own indexAzure AI Search (tool or custom RAG)You keep schema, scoring and security control.
Several enterprise sources, permission-aware, shared by agentsFoundry IQ knowledge baseAgentic retrieval; API-level GA, portal access still Preview.
Documents, images, audio, video into structured outputContent UnderstandingUser-defined schema, confidence scores, grounding, prebuilt industry analyzers; part of the Foundry resource.
project = AIProjectClient(endpoint=PROJECT_ENDPOINT, credential=DefaultAzureCredential())
openai = project.get_openai_client()

# Prompt agent: a persisted, versioned definition that Foundry runs
agent = project.agents.create_version(
    agent_name="MyAgent",
    definition=PromptAgentDefinition(model="gpt-4.1-mini", instructions="Be concise.", tools=[search_tool]),
)
reply = openai.responses.create(
    input="Hello",
    extra_body={"agent_reference": {"name": agent.name, "type": "agent_reference"}},
)

# No agent resource: call the model deployment directly
reply = openai.responses.create(model="gpt-4.1-mini", input="Hello")

The runtime has three objects: agents (reusable definition), conversations (persisted history) and responses (one generation). Start with a response for a single interaction; add an agent for reusable behaviour and a conversation for history. Multimodal work splits by input: Document Intelligence for documents, Vision for images and video, Speech for audio, and Content Understanding when one schema must cover several modalities.

Exam traps
  • The capability map still lists Workflows, but the workflow page says it retires on December 1, 2026: pick Microsoft Agent Framework for new work.
  • A hosted agent moves your container runtime into Foundry. If the agent already runs in your own host, the Responses API is enough.
  • A prompt agent cannot run custom orchestration code such as LangGraph.

Choose an appropriate method for retrieval and indexing

SituationUseWhy not the others
A few uploaded files, quick proof of conceptFile search tool plus vector storeNo index to manage.
Existing index; you control schema, scoring and securityAzure AI Search tool (or custom RAG code)File search cannot bind your own index.
Many sources, per-user permissions, one knowledge base reused by agents, multi-part questionsFoundry IQ knowledge base (agentic retrieval)One query over one index misses sub-questions and other sources.
Exact part numbers plus natural-language descriptionsHybrid query, plus the semantic ranker for best relevanceVector-only misses exact tokens; keyword-only misses synonyms.
Simple RAG, GA features only, lowest latency and costClassic hybrid with semantic rankingAgentic retrieval adds latency, and its LLM query planning is Preview.
  • Hybrid search is one request with both search and vectorQueries. Text (BM25) and vector queries run in parallel and are merged with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF).
  • Semantic ranker re-ranks only the top 50 results (L2), adds captions and answers, and is a premium feature billed by usage with a free allowance. Query rewrite (up to 10 variants) is Preview. Set k to 50 when you combine vectors with semantic ranking.
  • Agentic retrieval is a multi-query pipeline: a knowledge base with at least one knowledge source (indexed or remote) plans subqueries with an LLM, runs them in parallel, semantically reranks each and merges the results (optional references and activity log). Reasoning effort is minimal (no LLM planning), low (default) or medium. REST 2026-04-01 is GA for minimal, extractive retrieval; 2026-08-01-preview adds LLM planning, answer synthesis, non-minimal effort and multi-turn. It bills AI Search retrieval tokens plus Azure OpenAI tokens.
POST https://contoso-search.search.windows.net/indexes/parts/docs/search?api-version=2026-04-01
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "search": "quiet cooling fan for a small enclosure",
  "queryType": "semantic",
  "semanticConfiguration": "my-semantic-config",
  "vectorQueries": [
    { "kind": "text", "text": "quiet cooling fan for a small enclosure", "fields": "contentVector", "k": 50 }
  ]
}

"kind": "text" makes the index's vectorizer turn the string into a vector at query time; "kind": "vector" expects you to send the numeric vector yourself.

Indexing with integrated vectorization, in order: (1) create a data source; (2) create a skillset with the Text Split skill (chunking) and the AzureOpenAIEmbedding skill or another embedding skill; (3) create an index with a vectorizer assigned through a vector profile to the vector field; (4) create an indexer and run it on a schedule. The vectorizer must use the same embedding model that produced the stored vectors. The alternative is to generate embeddings yourself and push them into vector fields.

SettingAI Search guidanceFoundry file search defaults
Chunk sizestart at 512 tokens (about 2,000 characters)800 tokens
Overlap25% (128 tokens)400 tokens
OtherText Split skill settings maximumPageLength and pageOverlapLengthtext-embedding-3-large at 256 dimensions; at most 20 chunks go to the model

File search: up to 10,000 files per vector store, one vector store per agent and one per conversation, asynchronous ingestion (in_progress then completed). Basic agent setup uses Microsoft-managed storage and search; standard setup uses your Blob Storage and Azure AI Search. The Azure AI Search tool takes project_connection_id, index_name, top_k (default 5), query_type (default vector_semantic_hybrid; also simple, semantic, vector, vector_simple_hybrid) and filter. In the Python SDK these are the fields of AISearchIndexResource and the values come from AzureAISearchQueryType (for example VECTOR_SEMANTIC_HYBRID). Behind private networking use the project's Entra managed identity; key-based auth isn't supported. Keyless roles differ by page: Search Index Data Contributor plus Search Service Contributor on the tool page, Search Index Data Reader (read-only) on the Foundry IQ page.

Exam traps
  • A mismatched vectorizer (different embedding model than the indexer used) returns poor matches without any error.
  • Agentic retrieval has two API versions: GA 2026-04-01 (minimal effort) and 2026-08-01-preview (LLM planning, which the default effort low uses).
  • Chunk defaults differ: 512 tokens with 25% overlap in AI Search guidance, 800 with 400 in file search.

Choose appropriate memory, tool and knowledge integration services for agent solutions

Memory Preview is managed long-term memory in Agent Service: short-term memory is the current conversation, long-term memory is knowledge distilled across sessions (extraction, consolidation, retrieval). A store keeps user profile, chat summary and procedural memory and needs a chat model and an embedding model deployment. Limits: 100 scopes per store, 10,000 memories per scope, 1,000 search and 1,000 update requests per minute; no VNet integration. Memory = user-specific context learned over time; Foundry IQ = curated organisational content; file search = documents the user supplies in a conversation.

options = MemoryStoreDefaultOptions(user_profile_enabled=True, chat_summary_enabled=True)
definition = MemoryStoreDefaultDefinition(
    chat_model="gpt-5.2", embedding_model="text-embedding-3-small", options=options)
store = project_client.beta.memory_stores.create(name="shopper_memory", definition=definition)

tool = MemorySearchPreviewTool(memory_store_name="shopper_memory", scope="{{$userId}}", update_delay=300)
agent = project_client.agents.create_version(
    agent_name="ShopperAgent",
    definition=PromptAgentDefinition(model="gpt-5.2", instructions="Use memory.", tools=[tool]),
)

With the memory search tool, scope="{{$userId}}" resolves the end user from the x-memory-user-id request header, or from the caller's Entra tenant and object IDs if the header is missing. The low-level Memory Store APIs need an explicit scope. The SDK is azure-ai-projects>=2.3.0.

NeedChoose
Remember a shopper's preferences across sessionsMemory store plus memory search tool
Many agents reuse the same tools with central auth, governance and versioningToolbox GA: one MCP-compatible endpoint; promote a new default version without redeploying agents
Your own backend logic must run in the client appFunction calling: the model asks, your app executes and returns function_call_output
Existing REST API with a specOpenAPI tool: OpenAPI 3.0 or 3.1, every operation needs an operationId; auth is anonymous, API key (project connection) or managed identity
Public web freshness, simplest optionWeb Search tool (GA, no Bing resource, Azure OpenAI models)
Bing parameters or non-OpenAI models sold by AzureGrounding with Bing Search (GA; you create the Bing resource); Bing Custom Search is Preview
Curated enterprise knowledge for agentsFoundry IQ: MCPTool with allowed_tools=["knowledge_base_retrieve"] (the only knowledge base tool Agent Service supports) over a RemoteTool project connection (Preview)

A toolbox accepts MCP, web search, Azure AI Search, code interpreter, file search, OpenAPI and A2A tools, plus tool search and skills Preview. Function calling, Grounding with Bing, computer use, image generation, SharePoint, the Fabric data agent and Azure Functions tools are direct-integration only. An agent can register at most 128 tools.

Exam traps
  • Without the x-memory-user-id header, {{$userId}} falls back to the caller's Entra identity. For a backend service that is the backend itself, so all users would share one scope.
  • Memory is Preview and doesn't support VNet integration; the Foundry IQ RemoteTool connection is Preview too.
  • Function calling executes in your app, so it isn't a toolbox tool; Azure Functions tools aren't either.
  • Web Search needs no Bing resource and supports Azure OpenAI models; Grounding with Bing needs your resource. Both send data outside the Azure compliance boundary, and the Microsoft DPA doesn't apply to Bing grounding.
