sections.title: 1.2 Set up AI solutions in Foundry
sections.html:
Skills measured: design Azure infrastructure for AI apps and agent-based solutions • choose appropriate deployment options • configure model and agent deployments • integrate Foundry projects with continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD) pipelines. Practise by deploying a model with az cognitiveservices account deployment create, pinning an agent version, standing up a network-secured Standard setup from the foundry-samples Bicep templates, and running an evaluation gate from GitHub Actions. Quotas, monitoring, keyless access and RBAC are in §1.3; building agents is in §2.2.

Design Azure infrastructure for AI apps and agent-based solutions

A Foundry resource is Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts of kind AIServices; a project is its child resource and the unit of sharing and isolation. Pick the data setup first, then the network.

GoalChoose
Fastest working agent, no isolationBasic setup (default): Microsoft-managed storage and search
Agent data in resources I ownStandard setup: Azure Storage (files), Azure AI Search (vector stores), Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL (messages, conversation history, agent metadata)
Only restrict who can call the endpointPrivate endpoint with public network access disabled; egress stays public
No public egress; I control IP ranges, peering and routing, or need on-premises reachBYO virtual network (plus VPN or ExpressRoute)
No public egress; I can't manage IP ranges or my address space overlapsManaged virtual network
Several services share one boundary, log-first rolloutNetwork security perimeter: Transition (formerly Learning; CLI value Learning), then Enforced
  • Standard setup: the Cosmos DB account needs at least 3,000 RU/s (provisioned or serverless). Capability settings (account defaults, one store overridable per project) can't be updated on an existing project: delete and recreate it. The deploying identity needs Storage Blob Data Contributor and Cosmos DB Operator on those accounts (AI Search needs no caller role); creating account and project needs Foundry Account Owner, and builders get Foundry User on the project.
  • Inbound is public (optionally selected IP addresses) or a private endpoint with a private DNS zone, so the same connection string works inside and outside the virtual network. With public egress, a private endpoint secures only the inbound path.
  • BYO virtual network: a subnet delegated to Microsoft.App/environments, not shared by more than one Foundry resource; RFC 1918 or RFC 6598 ranges; at least /27 (/24 recommended for production with hosted agents), never resizable; Azure reserves five addresses. Hosted agents use one IP each, prompt agents a static pool of about 10 per project. Private endpoints and private DNS zones are needed for the account and each data resource, and the Foundry resource and virtual network must share a region.
  • Managed virtual network: outbound modes are Allow internet outbound, Allow only approved outbound (service tags, private endpoints, FQDN rules on ports 80 and 443 through a managed Azure Firewall you pay for) and Disabled. Settings can only tighten, can't be disabled once enabled, and have no upgrade path from BYO. The Azure portal can't create it: use Bicep (18-managed-virtual-network), Terraform or az rest (the az cognitiveservices account managed-network group is in preview). The Foundry resource's managed identity needs Azure AI Enterprise Network Connection Approver.
  • HA/DR: Foundry itself doesn't provide automatic failover or disaster recovery. Enable Cosmos DB continuous backup (7-, 30- or 35-day tier) before an incident; without it point-in-time restore isn't possible.
  • IaC: the foundry-samples repository has Bicep and Terraform templates such as 41-standard-agent-setup, 15-private-network-standard-agent-setup and 18-managed-virtual-network.
resource agentSubnet 'Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/subnets@2024-05-01' = {
  parent: vnet
  name: 'snet-agents'
  properties: {
    addressPrefix: '10.20.4.0/24'
    delegations: [
      {
        name: 'foundry-agents'
        properties: { serviceName: 'Microsoft.App/environments' }
      }
    ]
  }
}
Exam traps
  • Standard setup is a data-ownership choice, not network isolation; isolation is the separate BYO or managed virtual network choice.
  • Network injection is set when the account is created. You can't add it to an existing account or change outbound settings later: redeploy and create new projects.
  • The delegation target is Microsoft.App/environments, and /28 is too small: the minimum is /27.
  • Managed virtual network can't be created in the Azure portal and can't be switched off.

Choose appropriate deployment options

Start with Global Standard and move only for data residency, reserved throughput or batch work. These types apply to the serverless API option, not to managed compute. Data at rest stays in the designated geography; where inference runs depends on the type.

Deployment typeSKU codeInference runsBilling and best for
Global StandardGlobalStandardany Azure regionPay per token; default, newest models, highest quota
Global ProvisionedGlobalProvisionedManagedany regionReserved PTU; predictable high throughput
Global BatchGlobalBatchany region50% discount, 24-hour target; large async jobs
Data Zone StandardDataZoneStandardwithin the data zone (US, EU, APAC)Pay per token; zone compliance
Data Zone Provisioned / BatchDataZoneProvisionedManaged / DataZoneBatchwithin the data zoneZone plus reserved throughput / zone plus async at 50% off
StandardStandardwithin one Azure geographyPay per token; geography compliance, low volume
Regional ProvisionedProvisionedManagedwithin one geographyReserved PTU; strict residency plus throughput
DeveloperDeveloperTierany regionPay per token; fine-tuned model evaluation only, 24-hour lifetime, no SLA or residency guarantee
  • Request-level tiers on Global Standard deployments (Flex requires Global Standard; Priority is available on Global Standard and Data Zone Standard (US)): Flex Preview is service_tier="flex", 50% cheaper, no latency or service SLA, may return 429, and an unsupported model returns HTTP 400 with no fallback (use a long client timeout). Priority is enabled on the deployment or with service_tier="priority" and gives a defined per-model latency target at the priority token rate. Standard is service_tier="default".
  • Provisioned throughput: PTUs are held for you whether or not they are used, are model-independent, and are quota-limited per subscription, region and deployment type (Global, Data Zone and Regional are separate pools). Quota is not capacity: a deployment can fail with quota available (check the portal or the Model Capacities API). Size PTUs from requests per minute, prompt and response tokens, the output-to-input ratio and the cache rate (cached tokens don't consume PTU). Hourly billing can't be paused and stops only when you delete the deployment. A 1-month or 1-year Azure Reservation discounts the meter but guarantees no capacity; it matches on deployment type, region (Data Zone and Regional only) and scope, never on model.
  • Spillover sends overflow (for example 429 from exhausted PTUs) to a standard deployment in the same Foundry resource. Enable it for all requests with the deployment property spilloverDeploymentName, or per request with the x-ms-spillover-deployment header set to the standard deployment's name. If both are set, the deployment property wins; without either, no spillover occurs. A response header x-ms-spillover-from-deployment marks spilled requests.
  • Other options: instant access models Preview are called by name with no deployment; managed compute is a Preview deployment type. Agent deployment options (prompt, voice-based prompt, hosted, Responses API) are in §1.1.

Provisioned onboarding order: (1) size the PTUs; (2) confirm quota and capacity in the target region; (3) create the deployment (billing starts); (4) purchase the Azure Reservation for the PTUs you deployed; (5) check the deployment is covered by the reservation.

Exam traps
  • Batch, Standard and Provisioned are deployment types; Flex and Priority are per-request service tiers on Standard-type deployments.
  • Always create the provisioned deployment first, then buy the reservation: reservations don't hold capacity.
  • Global types may process in any region; only Data Zone and geography types keep inference inside the zone or geography.
  • The spillover header names the standard deployment, not the provisioned one.

Configure model and agent deployments

az cognitiveservices account deployment create \
    -n fabrikam-foundry -g rg-ai-prod \
    --deployment-name support-chat \
    --model-name gpt-4.1 --model-version 2025-04-14 --model-format OpenAI \
    --sku-name GlobalStandard --sku-capacity 100

az cognitiveservices account deployment show \
    -n fabrikam-foundry -g rg-ai-prod --deployment-name support-chat \
    | jq '.properties.provisioningState'    # "Succeeded"
  • -n is the Foundry resource; --deployment-name is the name callers send in the model field of requests to https://<resource>.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/. az cognitiveservices account list-models shows the name, format (provider), version and SKU you need. The same model can be deployed several times under different names, for example to compare guardrails.
  • Bicep: resource Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts/deployments with sku (name, capacity) and properties.model (format, name, version). The guardrail is assigned with properties.raiPolicyName (default Microsoft.DefaultV2); creating or editing guardrails needs Foundry Account Owner or higher.
  • Permissions: the deployment how-to lists Cognitive Services Contributor (or equivalent) on the Foundry resource for creating deployments. Partner and community models also need Azure Marketplace permissions (Owner and Contributor include them); models sold by Azure don't.
versionUpgradeOptionBehaviour
OnceNewDefaultVersionAvailableAuto-update to default: upgrades within two weeks of a new default version
OnceCurrentVersionExpiredUpgrades to the default when the current version retires; null behaves the same
NoAutoUpgradeNever upgrades; at retirement the deployment stops working until you repoint your code

Automatic updates apply to Standard deployment types only. REST, PowerShell and the portal can change the option; the Azure CLI can only show it.

Agents. An agent version is an immutable snapshot: any change, even one prompt edit, creates a new version (maximum 1,000 per agent). Every agent has a stable endpoint from the moment it is created, with no separate publish step. Its version_selector defaults to Always use latest; pin it to serve a fixed version (the SDK code on the docs page uses preview packages). Defaults: Responses protocol enabled, Entra inbound authorization (callers need Foundry Agent Consumer or higher; API keys aren't supported). Other protocols are Activity, Invocations, A2A and MCP. Foundry User on the project creates, manages and invokes agents. Publishing now means distributing to Microsoft Copilot and Teams; the older Agent Application resource is the legacy publishing experience.

endpoint_config = AgentEndpointConfig(
    version_selector=VersionSelector(
        version_selection_rules=[FixedRatioVersionSelectionRule(agent_version="2", traffic_percentage=100)]
    ),
)
project_client.agents.update_details(agent_name="support-bot", agent_endpoint=endpoint_config)
Exam traps
  • Callers use the deployment name, not the model name; -n is the account, not the deployment.
  • NoAutoUpgrade breaks the deployment at retirement; a missing option is OnceCurrentVersionExpired; the CLI can't change it.
  • The Bicep sample's parameter is called contentFilterPolicyName, but the resource property is raiPolicyName.
  • Saving an agent edit creates a new version, and with the default selector it is served at once.
  • Foundry User builds and invokes; Foundry Agent Consumer only calls agent endpoints.

Integrate Foundry projects with continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD) pipelines

Pipelines authenticate keylessly: GitHub Actions uses OpenID Connect through azure/login@v2 and needs permissions: id-token: write; Azure DevOps uses an Azure Resource Manager service connection with the AzureCLI@2 task; azd signs in with a federated credential. Don't add a long-lived client secret.

permissions:
  id-token: write
  contents: read
jobs:
  run-action:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          client-id: ${{ vars.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
          tenant-id: ${{ vars.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
          subscription-id: ${{ vars.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}
      - uses: microsoft/ai-agent-evals@v3-beta
        with:
          azure-ai-project-endpoint: "<project endpoint>"
          deployment-name: "<judge model deployment>"
          agent-ids: "support-bot:1,support-bot:2"
          data-path: ${{ github.workspace }}/evals/data.json
  • Evaluation gate. microsoft/ai-agent-evals (tag v3-beta) runs offline evaluation. agent-ids uses agent-name:version, comma-separated; the first is the baseline unless baseline-agent-id is set. The JSON data file has name, evaluators (such as builtin.task_adherence) and data[] items with query and optional ground_truth or context. The run summary shows scores, confidence intervals and, for several agents, a pairwise significance test. Don't run it on every commit. Azure DevOps uses the AI Agent Evaluation extension: AzureCLI@2 first, then AIAgentEvaluation@2.
  • Hosted agents with azd. azd pipeline config detects the Git provider, creates a service principal, stores AZURE_CLIENT_ID, AZURE_TENANT_ID, AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID, AZURE_ENV_NAME and AZURE_LOCATION as secrets and variables, and generates the workflow. A push to main runs azd provision then azd deploy. The runner needs azd ext install microsoft.foundry. Add --no-prompt to every azd ai step, or a missing value can hang the job. Regression-check with azd ai agent eval run --no-prompt (run eval generate first). Use one azd environment per stage (azd env new staging); main maps to production and develop to staging. Provisioning may need Contributor plus Foundry Owner. Terraform infrastructure doesn't move agent-version deployment out of azd.

Gated release order: (1) pin production to its existing agent version; (2) run azd deploy to create the candidate; (3) capture the version the deployment created; (4) validate that exact version in a fresh version-pinned session and check the response content; (5) promote only after approval, separately from deploy and provisioning.

Exam traps
  • The endpoint follows the latest version by default, so deploy-then-test can change production before the test runs: pin first.
  • azd deploy waiting for activation proves readiness, not correct behaviour; a non-empty CLI output is not a smoke test.
  • The GitHub OIDC login relies on permissions: id-token: write; a client secret in the repository contradicts keyless guidance.
  • azd ai agent invoke uses --output raw; show and the connection, toolbox and skill commands use --output json.
  • These pages carry the generic Preview banner, and the action tag is v3-beta.

Sources: Standard agent setup · Networking options · Managed virtual network · Network isolation · Network security perimeter · High availability · Deployment types · Provisioned throughput · Provisioned billing · Spillover · Flex processing · Create deployments · Model updates · Create guardrails · Configure an agent endpoint · Agent publishing model · CI/CD with azd · Evaluation in GitHub Actions · Evaluation in Azure DevOps

sections.title: 1.3 Manage, monitor, and secure AI systems
sections.html:
Skills measured: manage quotas, scaling, rate limits, and cost footprints for model and agent workloads • monitor model performance, drift, safety events, and grounding quality • monitor data ingestion quality, search index health, and relevance performance • configure security, including managed identity, private networking, keyless credentials, and role policies. Practise by wrapping a model call in retry logic, creating a continuous evaluation rule, reading an indexer status response, and granting Foundry Agent Consumer on one agent with the Azure CLI. Deployment types, spillover and network design are in §1.2; guardrails and evaluators are in §1.4.

Manage quotas, scaling, rate limits, and cost footprints for model and agent workloads

Quota is a policy limit, not reserved capacity. It is scoped to the Azure subscription (never the tenant) and counted in tokens per minute (TPM) for standard deployments or provisioned throughput units (PTU) for provisioned ones. For models onboarded to subscription-level quota management (the Scope column on the Quota page shows Global or Data Zone), Global Standard deployments of one model and version share a pool across all regions and Data Zone Standard deployments share a pool per data zone; other models are still managed per region. Quota tiers (Free, Tier 1 to 6) rise automatically with usage, and an approved quota request adds quota without changing the tier. Opting out of upgrades (tierUpgradePolicy: NoAutoUpgrade, API 2025-10-01-preview) is Preview.

NeedDo this
See quota and usageManage → Quota in the Foundry portal (tabs Token per minute and Provisioned throughput unit). Needs Cognitive Services Usages Reader at subscription scope: an assignment on a resource group, resource or project does not authorise the Usages API. GA
Free up or raise a deployment's allocationSelect the deployment, then Affiliated deployments using shared quota and the pencil icon. Request quota asks for more. Allow up to 15 minutes to propagate.
Stop one project monopolising a shared Foundry resourceAI Gateway (Azure API Management): Manage → AI Gateway → gateway → Token management → + Set limit. A TPM limit returns 429; an exhausted total token quota (hourly up to yearly) returns 403. Limits are per project and apply immediately. Needs API Management Service Contributor or Owner. Preview
High steady volume, latency varianceProvisioned deployment with spillover to a standard deployment; delay-tolerant bulk work goes to Batch (§1.2).

Rate limits. The TPM check uses an estimate made when the request arrives (prompt text plus max_tokens plus best_of), not billed tokens. RPM is checked over 1- or 10-second windows, so bursts can return 429 while the per-minute total looks fine. Read x-ratelimit-remaining-tokens, x-ratelimit-remaining-requests and, on a 429, retry-after-ms. Keep max_tokens as small as the scenario allows, keep best_of at 1, and retry with exponential backoff and jitter. The openai Python SDK already retries 429s (default max_retries is 2), so set max_retries=0 when you add your own retry library. Failed requests still count against the limit.

client = AzureOpenAI(azure_endpoint=endpoint, api_key=key,
                     api_version="2024-10-21", max_retries=0)

@retry(wait=wait_random_exponential(min=1, max=60), stop=stop_after_attempt(6),
       retry=retry_if_exception_type(openai.RateLimitError), reraise=True)
def chat(**kwargs):
    return client.chat.completions.create(**kwargs)

Agent workloads. Agent Service limits are fixed and cannot be raised: 128 tools and 1,000 versions per agent, 10,000 files per agent or thread, 512 MB per prompt-agent file, 100,000 messages per thread. Creating a version past 1,000 fails with HTTP 400 UserError, which is terminal: delete old versions first. Model calls throttle at the deployment's quota. Hosted-agent sessions return 429 session_quota_exceeded (stop or delete idle sessions, or request a higher limit), regional_session_quota_exceeded (retry or switch region) or subnet_exhausted (enlarge the subnet).

Cost footprint. Standard and Global deployments bill per token and provisioned deployments hourly per PTU; Batch and Flex are discounted. Azure OpenAI has no hard spending limit: create a budget with alerts and start automation from an action group, or cap tokens with AI Gateway. Foundry shows estimates (without discounts or provisioned throughput) in Operate → Overview (the tile excludes prompt agents and non-Foundry agents), Operate → Assets → Agents and the Monitor tab of an agent or model. Reconcile in Azure Cost Management: group by Resource, then Meter, and filter Service tier: Azure OpenAI (it sits under Cognitive Services; data lags about five hours). Every project carries an automatic project tag for chargeback (Preview, models sold by Azure only). Cost Management Reader views the data.

Exam traps
  • An exhausted gateway token quota returns 403; a TPM limit returns 429.
  • The rate-limit estimate counts max_tokens even when answers are short, so an oversized max_tokens causes 429s well under the quota.
  • Your own retry loop plus the SDK's two default retries multiplies requests; set max_retries=0.
  • Quota visibility needs Cognitive Services Usages Reader at subscription scope, not at the resource or project.
  • Budgets only alert; there is no native hard stop. The fixed Agent Service artifact limits (tools, versions, files, messages) cannot be raised, but the hosted-agent session limit can, through a support request.

Monitor model performance, drift, safety events, and grounding quality

Observability combines evaluation, monitoring and tracing. After deployment use operational metrics, continuous evaluation (production traffic at a sampled rate), scheduled evaluation (a test dataset on a schedule, to detect drift), scheduled red teaming and Azure Monitor alerts. The Agent Monitoring dashboard (Preview) is at Build → agent → Monitor; its gear opens Recurring evaluations, Red team scans and Alerts (all preview). It reads the project's connected Application Insights resource, so readers need access to it plus Log Analytics Reader (and Privileged Monitoring Data Reader for protected tables). Watch token usage, latency (over 10 seconds suggests throttling, heavy tool calls or network problems), run success rate (below 95 percent needs investigation) and evaluation scores.

eval_object = openai_client.evals.create(
    name="Continuous Evaluation",
    data_source_config={"type": "azure_ai_source", "scenario": "responses"},
    testing_criteria=[{"type": "azure_ai_evaluator", "name": "violence_detection",
                       "evaluator_name": "builtin.violence"}],
)
rule = project_client.evaluation_rules.create_or_update(
    id="my-continuous-eval-rule",
    evaluation_rule=EvaluationRule(
        action=ContinuousEvaluationRuleAction(eval_id=eval_object.id, max_hourly_runs=100),
        event_type=EvaluationRuleEventType.RESPONSE_COMPLETED,
        filter=EvaluationRuleFilter(agent_name=agent.name),
        enabled=True,
    ),
)
  • Continuous = EvaluationRule with ContinuousEvaluationRuleAction on RESPONSE_COMPLETED. max_hourly_runs caps runs per hour; sampling_rate is the percentage chance (above 0, up to 100) that a matching event triggers a run, and omitting it evaluates every event.
  • Scheduled = a Schedule with RecurrenceTrigger(interval=1, schedule=DailyRecurrenceSchedule(hours=[9])) and an EvaluationScheduleTask, created with project_client.beta.schedules.create_or_update. It runs on the clock, not on live traffic.
  • Needs azure-ai-projects>=2.0.0 (Python 3.10+) and the Foundry User role on the project's managed identity.
Azure Monitor signal (no setup)What it tells you
ModelAvailabilityRate(calls - server errors) / calls; server errors are HTTP 500 and above
ModelRequests, InputTokens, OutputTokens, TotalTokensVolume and usage
TimeToResponse, NormalizedTimeBetweenTokensStreaming latency for PTU deployments
ProvisionedUtilizationPTUs consumed / PTUs deployed x 100; 100 percent or more means throttling with 429
Blocked Volume, Harmful Volume Detected, Potential Abusive User Count, Safety System Event, Total Volume Sent for Safety CheckSafety events from content safety

Use the Models metric category rather than the older Azure OpenAI one. Provisioned-managed Utilization is deprecated in favour of V2, and the legacy Cognitive Services Latency metric misleads for Azure OpenAI. Monitoring Reader views metrics; Monitoring Contributor creates diagnostic settings. Grounding quality: offline, use Groundedness (judge model through deployment_name, scores 1 to 5, default pass threshold 3) or Groundedness Pro (Preview; Content Safety service, True or False, no judge model). At runtime the groundedness detection guardrail (Preview, models only) can flag ungrounded output (§1.4). Drift needs a quality signal: a scheduled evaluation on a fixed dataset, compared across model or agent versions.

Exam traps
  • Token and latency charts cannot reveal quality drift; only evaluation on a fixed dataset can.
  • Continuous evaluation samples live traffic; scheduled evaluation runs a dataset on a clock.
  • An empty dashboard usually means Application Insights is not connected or Log Analytics Reader is missing.
  • ProvisionedUtilization at 100 percent or more applies to PTU deployments only.
  • Groundedness (judge model, 1 to 5) is not Groundedness Pro (service, Boolean, Preview) and not the runtime groundedness detection guardrail.

Monitor data ingestion quality, search index health, and relevance performance

Azure AI Search, the engine under Foundry IQ knowledge sources, emits platform metrics automatically: DocumentsProcessedCount (split by IndexerName, IndexName, SkillsetName, DataSourceName and Failed), SkillExecutionCount (also splits on Failed), DocumentsProcessedBytes, IndexStorageUsage, IndexVectorUsage, SearchLatency, SearchQueriesPerSecond and ThrottledSearchQueriesPercentage. Resource logs are not collected until you create a diagnostic setting (to Log Analytics, Storage or Event Hubs); the Activity log covers control-plane operations.

Portal indexer statusMeaning
In ProgressActive run; high-volume indexers can show it permanently
SuccessRun finished, even if some documents failed, while errors stay under the indexer's Max failed items
FailedErrors exceeded Max failed items and indexing stopped
ResetChange tracking was reset; the next run reprocesses every document

Get Indexer Status (api-version=2026-04-01): the monitoring page shows GET https://[service].search.windows.net/indexers/[indexer]/status with an api-key header; the REST reference writes the path as /indexers('{indexerName}')/search.status. Execution details in the portal list up to 50 recent runs (downloadable as CSV).

{
  "name": "contracts-indexer",
  "status": "running",
  "lastResult": { "status": "success", "itemsProcessed": 11, "itemsFailed": 0,
                  "errors": [], "warnings": [] },
  "executionHistory": [ ]
}
  • Top-level status: running means the indexer is configured and available, not that a run is executing. Each run has its own status: running, success, transientFailure or persistentFailure, plus a Reset entry. executionHistory holds up to 50 runs, newest first.
  • In .NET, SearchIndexerClient.GetIndexerStatus(name) returns a SearchIndexerStatus with LastResult and ExecutionHistory.
  • Warnings (an image without text, a truncated document) do not stop indexing and are common; errors count toward itemsFailed.
  • Index health: GET {endpoint}/indexes('{indexName}')/search.stats?api-version=2026-04-01 returns documentCount, storageSize and vectorIndexSize; the statistics are collected periodically, so they can lag. Alert on IndexStorageUsage and ThrottledSearchQueriesPercentage.

Relevance. Ranking layers: L1 @search.score (BM25 for text; HNSW or exhaustive KNN for vectors), fused L1 (RRF for hybrid queries or several vector queries), L2 semantic ranker @search.rerankerScore (0 to 4, reranks only the top 50 L1 results, billed) and L3 (agentic retrieval at medium reasoning effort, preview). A uniform @search.score of 1.0 means no ranking algorithm ran (filter-only, autocomplete, suggestions, geospatial, fuzzy or regular-expression queries). Improve relevance with hybrid search plus the semantic ranker, scoring profiles and better chunking, then measure it in Foundry: the Retrieval evaluator (judge model, no ground truth) or Document Retrieval (needs labelled ground truth; reports Fidelity, NDCG, XDCG, Max Relevance and Holes). Agentic retrieval always returns merged content and can also return an activity log (includeActivity) and source references (includeReferences, set per knowledge source); it bills tokens.

Exam traps
  • Success does not mean every document was indexed: check itemsFailed, the errors and Max failed items.
  • Top-level running is not a live run; the run's own status is in lastResult and executionHistory.
  • Metrics are automatic; resource logs (who queried what) need a diagnostic setting.
  • The semantic ranker reorders only the top 50 results and cannot find documents L1 missed.
  • Document Retrieval needs labelled ground truth; without labels use the Retrieval evaluator.

Configure security, including managed identity, private networking, keyless credentials, and role policies

Entra ID or keys. Microsoft Entra ID (OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens scoped to https://ai.azure.com/.default) gives conditional access, MFA, just-in-time access, per-principal audit and managed identities. API keys are static, resource-wide and carry no user identity: prototyping only, and a key bypasses RBAC. The Agents service, Evaluations and Toolbox do not accept API keys.

token_provider = get_bearer_token_provider(DefaultAzureCredential(), "https://ai.azure.com/.default")
client = OpenAI(base_url="https://<resource>.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/", api_key=token_provider)
project = AIProjectClient(endpoint=project_endpoint, credential=DefaultAzureCredential())
  • Credentials: DefaultAzureCredential tries a chain (environment, managed identity, developer tools). In production prefer a deterministic credential such as ManagedIdentityCredential or a pared-down ChainedTokenCredential, and give the host a system- or user-assigned managed identity.
  • Enforce keyless: set disableLocalAuth: true on the Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts resource (Bicep or ARM), run Set-AzCognitiveServicesAccount with -DisableLocalAuth $true, or assign the Azure Policy Azure AI Services resources should have key access disabled (disable local authentication) at subscription or resource group scope. The change can take minutes or hours; confirm that an old key returns HTTP 401. Regenerating Key1 and Key2 revokes keys but does not disable key authentication.
  • Managed identity for tools: an MCP connection can authenticate as the project's managed identity or the agent identity, for example azd ai connection create my-mcp-conn --kind remote-tool --target <url> --auth-type project-managed-identity --audience <audience>. Grant that principal RBAC on the target first. The blueprint's federated credential to the project's managed identity avoids stored secrets, but the agent identity is the principal that needs the roles, and a wrong audience breaks authentication even with correct RBAC.
Built-in roleUse it for
Foundry Agent ConsumerOnly call agent endpoints (least privilege for callers). Assignable at account, project or agent scope; the Azure portal supports only account scope, so use the CLI
Foundry UserBuild and develop in a project, read, call endpoints. Assign it on the Foundry resource to users and to the project's managed identity
Foundry Project ManagerBuild, publish agents, assign Foundry User only
Foundry Account OwnerCreate accounts and projects, manage models; no build or endpoint access
Foundry OwnerAll of the above
Cognitive Services Usages ReaderQuota visibility at subscription scope
AGENT_SCOPE="/subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts/<account>/projects/<project>/agents/<agent>"
az role assignment create --assignee-object-id "<principalId>" --assignee-principal-type ServicePrincipal \
  --role "eed3b665-ab3a-47b6-8f48-c9382fb1dad6" --scope "$AGENT_SCOPE"

Use role definition IDs in code: the roles were renamed (Azure AI User is now Foundry User, and so on) with unchanged IDs. Foundry User is 53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d. At agent scope, assignments are evaluated only for agent endpoint access. The RBAC page advises against Azure AI Developer for Foundry projects (it targets Azure Machine Learning workspaces and hubs), although some task pages still list it. The docs also differ on the inference role: the keyless page assigns Cognitive Services User on the Foundry resource, while the RBAC pages use Foundry User and advise against other Cognitive Services roles except Usages Reader. Under the older Agent Application publishing model, publishing creates a distinct agent identity that needs its own role assignments; unpublished agents share the project's default agent identity.

Private networking (design choices in §1.2): set public network access to Disabled, or to selected networks with allowed IP addresses (ARM property publicNetworkAccess), and add a private endpoint (the portal labels the target account) with a privatelink private DNS zone, so the same connection string resolves to the private IP inside the virtual network. It needs Network Contributor on the network and Contributor or Owner on the Foundry project resource; without approval rights the connection stays Pending. Validate that the connection is Approved, nslookup returns the private IP and port 443 answers. Removing a private endpoint does not make the resource public.

Role policies. The Azure Policy built-ins Foundry model deployments should only use approved models and Foundry model deployments should meet eligibility requirements (source and lifecycle) are GA and evaluated at deployment time: the Deploy action is disabled with the reason. The model-router policies are Preview. Assigning needs Owner or Resource Policy Contributor. To hide preview features set the tag AZML_DISABLE_PREVIEW_FEATURE=true (case-sensitive; Contributor or Tag Contributor); custom roles block specific operations. Customer-managed keys need Key Vault or Managed HSM in the same region with soft delete and purge protection; grant the managed identity (Key Vault Crypto User) before enabling the key, and with a system-assigned identity create the resource first, then grant access.

Exam traps
  • A key grants full access and bypasses RBAC; only disableLocalAuth (or the policy) turns key authentication off, and it is not instant.
  • Foundry Agent Consumer is for callers of agent endpoints; Foundry User also lets people build, and Foundry Account Owner cannot call agents at all.
  • The portal assigns Foundry Agent Consumer only at account scope; project or agent scope needs the CLI.
  • Usages Reader at a resource group or project does not authorise the quota Usages API.
  • Customer-managed keys protect data at rest; they are not API keys, and the identity needs key access before you enable them.
  • The RBAC page says to use Foundry User or Foundry Owner, not Azure AI Developer, for Foundry projects, even though some task pages still mention it.

Sources: Manage quota · Quotas and limits · Enforce token limits · Agent Service limits · Manage costs · Observability · Agent Monitoring dashboard · Monitor model deployments · Azure OpenAI monitoring reference · Monitor indexers · Get Indexer Status · Get Index Statistics · ContinuousEvaluationRuleAction · Search monitoring data reference · Relevance and ranking · Semantic ranker · RAG evaluators · Authentication and authorization · Keyless authentication · Disable local authentication · Foundry RBAC · Agent identity · Network isolation · Model deployment policies · Disable preview features · Customer-managed keys · Feature readiness

sections.title: 1.4 Implement responsible AI across generative AI and agentic systems
sections.html:
Skills measured: configure safety filters, guardrails, risk detection, and content moderation • apply responsible AI instrumentation, including evaluators, safety evaluations, and explanation tooling • implement auditing through trace logging, provenance metadata, and approval workflows • govern agent behavior with oversight modes, constraints, and tool-access controls. Practise by creating a guardrail and assigning it to a model and an agent, running safety evaluators and a red-team scan, connecting Application Insights for tracing, and adding an MCP tool that needs approval. Identity, network and monitoring controls are in §1.3; building agents is in §2.2.

Configure safety filters, guardrails, risk detection, and content moderation

In Foundry the former content filters are configured as guardrails and controls. A guardrail is a named collection of controls; each control is a risk, one or more intervention points and an action, backed by Azure AI Content Safety classifiers. Guardrails cover Foundry Models sold by Azure (not audio transcription models) and agents built in Foundry Agent Service (not other agents registered in the Control Plane). Creating or editing one needs Foundry Account Owner. Status: guardrails for models GA; for agents, and the controls and intervention points, Preview.

ConceptValues and rules
Intervention pointsUser input; tool call and tool response (agents only, Preview); output
ActionsAnnotate (models only) and Annotate and block (models and agents). Results carry detected and filtered flags
Blocking level (Hate, Sexual, Self-harm, Violence)Off; Low blocks high severity only (least restrictive); Medium blocks medium and high; High blocks low, medium and high (most restrictive). Anyone can turn harms off for inputs; for outputs only customers approved for modified guardrails can
Default for modelsMicrosoft.DefaultV2: the four harm categories at Medium on prompts and completions, user prompt attack detection on, protected material (text and code) on completions. Document attack detection is off until you enable it
  • Agents: a guardrail assigned to the agent is used; otherwise the agent inherits its model deployment's guardrail. The agent's guardrail fully overrides the model's. Example: model Violence at High, agent Violence at Low on user input and output, no Violence control on tool calls: the agent scans input and output at Low and does not scan tool calls or tool responses for Violence.
  • Model-only risks: Spotlighting (Preview) and Groundedness (Preview) do nothing on agents; PII (Preview) and Task Adherence (Preview) apply to both.

Prompt Shields detect user prompt attacks (formerly jailbreak risk detection, scanned at user input) and document attacks (instructions hidden in documents, emails or web pages; the documents field; scanned at user input for models and also at tool response for agents, Preview). Spotlighting (Preview) marks documents as untrusted by base-64 encoding them: off by default, Chat Completions only, more tokens. The standalone Content Safety API analyses a userPrompt and up to five documents and returns attackDetected; it never blocks, so your code decides.

"prompt_filter_results": [{ "prompt_index": 0,
  "content_filter_results": { "jailbreak": { "filtered": false, "detected": true } } }]

The annotation shows an attack that was detected but not blocked: the control only annotates. Switch it to Annotate and block to stop the prompt before the model processes it.

Create and assign (ordered): project → Build → Guardrails → Create guardrail; (1) add controls (pick a risk, choose intervention points and one action, then Add control); (2) Add agents and/or Add models; (3) review, name it and Create. Assignment is immediate, and removing an item reverts it to the Microsoft default guardrail. The Microsoft defaults cannot be edited, and the four core-harm controls on input and output cannot be deleted, only overridden. In the REST API a guardrail is a RAI policy (an Azure Resource Manager resource) and a deployment references it with the raiPolicyName property. An organisation-wide minimum is a guardrail policy under Operate → Compliance.

Hosted agents: set rai_config.rai_policy_name to the policy's full ARM resource ID, for example rai_config=RaiConfig(rai_policy_name=RAI_POLICY_ID) in HostedAgentDefinition (azure-ai-projects 2.2.0 or later; azd uses a policies list with type: rai_policy). Omit rai_config and no content safety guardrail applies; include it without a name and Microsoft.DefaultV2 applies. A policy ID that does not exist fails open: the agent is active but nothing is filtered. On the invocations protocol you must also set invocations_moderation (response_mode, plus input_paths such as $.messages[*].content), otherwise nothing is screened; invocations_ws has no content safety moderation. A blocked prompt returns HTTP 400 with the content_filter error code.

Task Adherence (Preview) checks whether an agent's tool calls match the user's intent: POST <endpoint>/contentsafety/agent:analyzeTaskAdherence?api-version=2024-12-15-preview with tools and messages returns taskRiskDetected (Boolean) and details. When it is true, block the tool call or escalate to a person.

Exam traps
  • Low blocks only high-severity content and High is the most restrictive; Medium is the default.
  • Document attack detection is off by default; user prompt attack detection is on.
  • An agent's guardrail replaces its model's guardrail; the two are not merged.
  • Spotlighting and Groundedness controls are ignored on agents but still apply to models that share the guardrail.
  • A hosted agent with a non-existent policy ID, or an invocations agent without invocations_moderation, still returns HTTP 200 and screens nothing.
  • The Content Safety API only reports detections; the Foundry guardrail action does the blocking.

Apply responsible AI instrumentation, including evaluators, safety evaluations, and explanation tooling

Evaluation workflow: (1) choose what to evaluate (a dataset, generated responses, simulated conversations or production traces; a turn or a whole conversation); (2) select evaluators, referenced as builtin.<name>; (3) run them (portal, SDK cloud evaluation, CI/CD or a recurring schedule); (4) review, compare and cluster the results. Evaluations are GA, but several evaluators are Preview, so check each label. Evaluators produce metrics and, when supported, explanations in a reason field.

FamilyExamplesScale and pass rule
AI-assisted quality and RAG (judge model, needs deployment_name)Coherence, Fluency, Groundedness, Relevance, Retrieval1 to 5, default threshold 3, pass at or above
Groundedness Pro (Preview)Content Safety service, no judge modelTrue or False
Risk and safety (hosted evaluation models, no deployment_name)builtin.violence, builtin.sexual, builtin.self_harm, builtin.hate_unfairness, builtin.protected_material, builtin.code_vulnerability, builtin.ungrounded_attributes; builtin.indirect_attack is model only0 to 7 severity for violence, sexual, self-harm and hate and unfairness (default threshold 3, pass at or below); the other risk evaluators output pass or fail
Agent-only safety (Preview)builtin.prohibited_actions, builtin.sensitive_data_leakage (need tool_calls or messages)Agent targets only, not datasets or models
testing_criteria = [{
    "type": "azure_ai_evaluator",
    "name": "Violence",
    "evaluator_name": "builtin.violence",
    "data_mapping": {"query": "{{item.query}}", "response": "{{item.response}}"},
}]
# result fields: metric, score, label, reason, threshold, passed

The AI Red Teaming Agent (GA) combines PyRIT attack strategies (for example Flip and Base64) with the risk and safety evaluators. It sends seed attack objectives to a model or agent, scores each attack-response pair and reports the Attack Success Rate: successful attacks divided by total attacks, so lower is safer. Only text-based scenarios are supported, and the agent-specific categories (prohibited actions, sensitive data leakage, task adherence) are agents-only and cloud-only. Use it at design, development and pre-deployment, and on a schedule after deployment.

Explanation tooling. The documented explanation signals are the reason on each evaluator result, the Reasoning mode of the groundedness detection guardrail (Preview), the details returned by Task Adherence, and portal review and cluster analysis of evaluation results. The trace attribute gen_ai.evaluation.explanation stores explanations and is treated as sensitive content (next section).

Exam traps
  • The violence, sexual, self-harm and hate and unfairness evaluators score 0 to 7 and lower is better (pass at or below the threshold; the other risk evaluators output pass or fail); quality evaluators score 1 to 5 and higher is better.
  • Risk and safety evaluators use hosted models and take no deployment_name; Groundedness and Relevance need a judge deployment.
  • Prohibited actions and sensitive data leakage evaluate agent targets only and are Preview.
  • Groundedness (judge, scored) is not Groundedness Pro (service, True or False, Preview).
  • A red-team Attack Success Rate is bad when high; scans are text-only.
  • An evaluator reports a result; it does not block anything. Blocking is a guardrail action.

Implement auditing through trace logging, provenance metadata, and approval workflows

Trace logging. Foundry tracing is built on OpenTelemetry and stores traces in a connected Application Insights resource. It is off by default: nothing is collected until a Foundry Account Owner or Foundry Owner connects Application Insights to the project, after which every agent in the project is traced. Steps: (1) connect or create Application Insights for the project; (2) instrument (server-side traces in the portal need no code; client-side traces use the Foundry SDK with OpenTelemetry); (3) run the agent and confirm a trace appears. Tracing is GA for prompt and hosted agents and Preview for workflow and external agents. Readers need project access plus read access to Application Insights or its workspace (Log Analytics Reader, Monitoring Reader or Reader). Disconnecting Application Insights stops collection; existing data stays under its retention policy.

Protect sensitive content. Prompts, outputs, system instructions, tool definitions, tool arguments and results, and evaluation explanations (for example gen_ai.input.messages, gen_ai.output.messages, gen_ai.tool.call.arguments and gen_ai.evaluation.explanation) go to the dedicated AppGenAIContent table. Ordered steps: (1) register the feature flag, az feature register --namespace Microsoft.Insights --name protectGenAISensitiveData (needs Log Analytics Contributor and subscription Owner or Microsoft.Features/* rights; the page presents this as early enablement before the September 30, 2026 migration and does not say whether it is still required afterwards); (2) set the table's protection level to Protected (deny by default); (3) grant Privileged Monitoring Data Reader on the Application Insights resource linked to the project to the auditors; (4) verify that a user with only Log Analytics Reader cannot see the content while a Privileged Monitoring Data Reader can. From September 30, 2026 new data keeps only a pointer in AppDependencies, AppTraces and AppEvents, so point custom queries and alerts at AppGenAIContent.

Audit logs. The Azure Activity log records control-plane operations. A diagnostic setting on the Foundry resource sends model logs (for example the RequestResponse and Audit categories) to Log Analytics, Storage or Event Hubs; nothing is kept until you create one. Control Plane Compliance keeps versioned policies and assignments for auditability.

Provenance metadata. For supported generated images, audio and video, Foundry can attach Content Credentials (C2PA), cryptographically signed metadata that records that AI generated or modified the content, the service involved and the time, plus invisible watermarks that can remain when metadata is removed. Verify with the Content Provenance Detection website or the Content Provenance Detection API in Azure AI Content Safety. Text provenance depends on the model provider. For retrieval answers, provenance means citations: AI Search and agentic retrieval return source references and an activity log.

Approval workflows. An MCP tool declared with require_approval="always" pauses before each call. The response contains an item of type mcp_approval_request (server label, tool name, arguments); a person reviews it and the app returns an McpApprovalResponse in a second call that carries previous_response_id.

tool = MCPTool(server_label="api-specs", server_url="https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp",
               require_approval="always", project_connection_id=MCP_CONNECTION_NAME)
ref = {"agent_reference": {"name": agent.name, "type": "agent_reference"}}
response = openai.responses.create(input="...", extra_body=ref)

input_list = []
for item in response.output:
    if item.type == "mcp_approval_request":
        input_list.append(McpApprovalResponse(type="mcp_approval_response",
                          approve=reviewer_approved, approval_request_id=item.id))
response = openai.responses.create(input=input_list, previous_response_id=response.id, extra_body=ref)

Review the tool name and arguments before approving, require approval for tools that write data or change resources, and log approvals and tool calls. For decisions that take hours or days, long-running hosted agents (Preview) can suspend a multi-turn task under a task_id until a person replies. The Foundry Workflows human-in-the-loop pattern is Preview and Foundry is retiring workflows on December 1, 2026: use Microsoft Agent Framework for new work.

Exam traps
  • Tracing is off until Application Insights is connected; an empty Traces page usually means no connection or no Log Analytics Reader.
  • Log Analytics Reader alone does not show protected AppGenAIContent; auditors need Privileged Monitoring Data Reader.
  • The Activity log is control-plane only; prompts and tool arguments live in traces and resource logs.
  • C2PA metadata can be stripped; the invisible watermark is what can survive. Detection uses the Content Provenance Detection site or API.
  • The approval reply is an McpApprovalResponse tied to approval_request_id and sent with previous_response_id; require_approval only prompts, so a person or policy must judge the arguments.

Govern agent behavior with oversight modes, constraints, and tool-access controls

Oversight modeHow you implement it
A person approves before the agent actsMCP require_approval="always" (round trip above); Task Adherence flags a misaligned tool call so you block it or escalate
A person decides later, possibly hoursLong-running hosted-agent human-in-the-loop (Preview)
Autonomous, watched afterwardsContinuous evaluation, scheduled red teaming and alerts (§1.3), plus human review of traces
Fleet oversight across projectsFoundry Control Plane: Operate → Overview, Assets, Compliance (Preview)
tool = MCPTool(
    server_label="work-items", server_url="https://mcp.proseware.example/mcp",
    allowed_tools=["get_work_item", "search_work_items"],   # allow-list: read-only subset
    require_approval="always",                              # a person approves each call
    project_connection_id="work-items-conn",
)
  • Constraints: the allowed_tools allow-list (choosing a subset in the portal tool catalog is the same thing), tool_choice (auto, required or none) for whether the model may call tools at all, at most 128 tools per agent, guardrail controls, network egress controls for hosted agents (Preview), Azure Policy for approved models and AI Gateway token limits per project (§1.3). Treat tool descriptions, annotations and results from remote MCP servers as untrusted input (indirect prompt injection), prefer servers run by trusted providers over proxies, keep credentials in a project connection, and review allowed_tools and approvals when the server's tools or operator change.
  • Toolbox (GA) bundles tools behind one MCP-compatible endpoint with central credential management, versioning and policy enforcement. Agents authenticate to the toolbox with Entra credentials and do not carry each tool's credentials.
  • AI gateway governance for MCP tools (Preview) covers only new MCP tools created in the Foundry portal that do not use managed OAuth. API Management policies add rate-limit-by-key, ip-filter, a correlation ID header or header removal without changing the server or the agent. Needs API Management Service Contributor or Owner and the AI gateway connected to the Foundry resource.
  • Identity: assign RBAC to the agent identity. A blueprint represents a class of agents, so Conditional Access, disabling or revoking permissions applies to every agent of that type. On-behalf-of (attended) limits the agent to the signed-in user's delegated permissions; client credentials (unattended) uses the agent's own role assignments.

Operate adds inventory across projects, health, drift, latency and error clusters, guardrail view and edit, Defender and Purview alerts, and guardrail policies through Azure Policy with bulk remediation. Quota and AI Gateway are project-scoped and sit under Manage. Guardrails apply only to agents built in Foundry Agent Service, not to external agents registered in the Control Plane.

Exam traps
  • allowed_tools removes tools from the agent; require_approval only asks a person. To make writes impossible, leave them out of the allow-list.
  • Instructions such as "never call delete" are guidance, not enforcement; remote MCP content can carry prompt injection.
  • The Control Plane Operate panes and AI Gateway are Preview; Quota under Manage is GA; toolboxes are GA.
  • AI gateway MCP governance does not cover tools that use managed OAuth or tools created outside the portal.
  • The agent identity, not the project's managed identity, needs RBAC on downstream resources.

Sources: Guardrails overview · Default safety policies · Create guardrails · Prompt Shields · Task Adherence · Hosted agent guardrails · Risk and safety evaluators · RAG evaluators · AI Red Teaming Agent · Tracing and data handling · Sensitive trace content · Content provenance · MCP tool · Tool best practices · Govern MCP tools with an AI gateway · Foundry Control Plane · Agent identity · Feature readiness

sections.title: 2.1 Build generative applications by using Foundry
sections.html:
Skills measured: deploy and consume LLMs, small models, code models and multimodal models • implement retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) in an application • design workflows, tool-augmented flows and multistep reasoning pipelines • evaluate models and apps, including detecting fabrications, relevance, quality and safety • integrate generative workflows into applications by using Foundry SDKs and connectors • configure an application to connect to a Foundry project. Practise by deploying a model with the Azure CLI, calling it through AIProjectClient and a plain OpenAI client, attaching an Azure AI Search index to an agent, running a groundedness and a violence evaluation, and finishing a function-call loop. Agents are in §2.2; tuning, tracing and cost are in §2.3; quotas and RBAC are in §1.3.

Deploy and consume LLMs, small models, code models, and multimodal models

A deployment gives a catalog model a name plus a capacity type, content-filter and rate-limit settings. You pay only for inference, and every request passes the deployment name in model; the same model can be deployed twice under different names. Partner and community models need Azure Marketplace subscription rights; Models sold by Azure don't.

Deployment type (SKU code)Inference processedBillingPick it for
Global Standard GlobalStandardAny Azure regionPer tokenDefault: newest models, lowest price, highest quota
Global Provisioned GlobalProvisionedManagedAny regionReserved PTUPredictable high throughput
Global Batch GlobalBatchAny region50% discount, 24-hourLarge asynchronous jobs
Data Zone DataZoneStandard, DataZoneProvisionedManaged, DataZoneBatchOnly inside the US, EU or APAC zonePer token / PTU / 50% discountZone residency
Standard, Regional Provisioned ProvisionedManagedInside one Azure geographyPer token / PTUGeography compliance
Developer DeveloperTierAny regionPer tokenEvaluating a fine-tuned model only: 24-hour lifetime, no SLA

Data at rest stays in the designated geography for every type; only inference processing differs, and not every model supports every type. These types belong to the Serverless API option (preferred). Managed compute Preview runs open-source, partner and custom models on dedicated GPU capacity and doesn't use them; instant access Preview calls supported models by name with no deployment at all.

az cognitiveservices account deployment create \
  -n $accountName -g $resourceGroupName \
  --deployment-name Phi-4-mini-instruct --model-name Phi-4-mini-instruct \
  --model-version 1 --model-format Microsoft \
  --sku-capacity 1 --sku-name GlobalStandard
  • Quota: tokens per minute are assigned per subscription, region, model and deployment type; going over returns HTTP 429. The limiter estimates prompt tokens plus the max_tokens (and best_of) setting, not the billed count, so an oversized max_tokens can trigger 429s early.
  • Responses vs Chat Completions: responses.create works for Azure OpenAI models and for Models sold by Azure that support it (the docs name DeepSeek, Llama and Grok). Otherwise the call fails with 400 Model not supported: switch to client.chat.completions.create. It is not an auth or quota problem.
  • Reasoning models: reasoning tokens fill the context window and are billed as output tokens. Most reasoning models reject temperature, top_p, penalty parameters and max_tokens; cap output with max_completion_tokens (Chat Completions) or max_output_tokens (Responses).
  • Small models: small language models such as Phi-4-mini-instruct deploy like any catalog model. For offline, private, on-device use choose Foundry Local: it runs on ONNX Runtime on the user's device, needs no Azure subscription and exposes an OpenAI-compatible API (the Responses format included).
  • Code models: Codex-family models are deployed like any other. The Codex CLI reads config.toml: model is your deployment name, base_url ends in /openai/v1, env_key must name an environment variable (never the key itself) and wire_api = "responses". Its Agent (full access) mode skips step-by-step approval, so use it only in a sandbox.
  • Multimodal: vision-capable chat models accept images as content parts of a user message.
{"role": "user", "content": [
  {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this picture:"},
  {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "https://contoso.example/photo.jpg"}}]}

Implement retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) in an application

RAG is retrieve relevant content (usually from an index), augment the prompt with it as grounding data, generate an answer that can cite sources. Use RAG for private or frequently changing data; fine-tuning changes behaviour, style or task performance but does not add fresh knowledge. A typical build: prepare and chunk the data, set up an Azure AI Search index, connect it to Foundry, build the app, then test and evaluate it. Index design and chunking are also covered in §5.1.

NeedUse
Own index, one query per turn, GA features only, you orchestrate the LLMClassic RAG: hybrid query (keyword plus vector) with semantic ranking
Chat or agent with multi-part, history-dependent questionsAgentic retrieval: a knowledge base and its retrieve action
Several sources (Blob, SharePoint, OneLake, web), per-user permissions, shared by many agentsFoundry IQ knowledge base, attached through MCP
Existing search index, one agentAzure AI Search tool
A few files the user uploadsFile search tool with a vector store
  • Agentic retrieval pipeline: the app sends a query plus conversation history to the knowledge base. At low (default) and medium retrieval reasoning effort an LLM writes focused subqueries; at minimal that step is skipped. Subqueries (keyword, vector or hybrid) run simultaneously, each is semantically reranked, and the results merge into one response with optional references and an activity log. LLM query planning and answer synthesis are Preview (REST 2026-08-01-preview); REST 2026-04-01 is GA for GA knowledge source types with minimal, extractive retrieval. Both portals expose preview only.
  • Foundry IQ (some features GA, portal access Preview): agents reach a knowledge base through the MCP tool, and knowledge_base_retrieve is the only supported tool. The project connection has category RemoteTool Preview and uses the project's managed identity, which needs Search Index Data Reader on the search service (add Search Index Data Contributor only to write). Creating the connection needs Foundry Project Manager. For ACL-protected content, include permission metadata in the index and pass the user token in the x-ms-query-source-authorization header (query-time ACL enforcement is Preview).
  • Azure AI Search tool parameters: project_connection_id and index_name (required), top_k (default 5), query_type (default vector_semantic_hybrid; also simple, vector, semantic, vector_simple_hybrid) and filter (applied to every query). The index needs searchable, retrievable Edm.String fields, a Collection(Edm.Single) vector field and a retrievable source-URL field. A private virtual network requires the Entra managed identity, not keys.
tool = AzureAISearchTool(azure_ai_search=AzureAISearchToolResource(indexes=[
    AISearchIndexResource(project_connection_id=connection_id,
                          index_name="contoso-products",
                          query_type=AzureAISearchQueryType.SIMPLE)]))

store = openai.vector_stores.create(name="ProductInfoStore")
openai.vector_stores.files.upload_and_poll(vector_store_id=store.id, file=handle)
file_tool = FileSearchTool(vector_store_ids=[store.id])
  • File search in the standard agent setup keeps files in your own storage (Azure AI Search ingests them); it needs Storage Blob Data Contributor on the project's storage plus Foundry User, and has charges beyond token fees.
  • Risks: enforce access control at retrieval time, treat retrieved text as untrusted input (prompt injection), and remember grounding reduces but does not remove fabrication: ask for citations and instruct the model to stick to the retrieved content.
  • Azure OpenAI On Your Data retired on October 14, 2026 and is no longer supported; migrating to Foundry IQ is not automatic.

Design workflows, tool-augmented flows, and multistep reasoning pipelines

Use the lowest level of complexity that reliably works: a direct model call, then a single agent with tools (often the right default; set iteration limits to stop infinite tool-call loops), then multi-agent orchestration (§2.2), which adds coordination overhead, latency and failure modes. If plain code can do the task, write the function instead of an agent. In Microsoft Agent Framework, an agent fits open-ended, conversational work with autonomous tool use, and a workflow fits well-defined steps with explicit execution order (branches, fan-out and fan-in, checkpoints).

Foundry workflows are retiring

Foundry workflows (visual designer) are Preview and Microsoft Foundry is retiring them on December 1, 2026. For new work use Microsoft Agent Framework (YAML or code); Azure Logic Apps is the fully visual route and A2A suits a simple agent-to-agent hand-off. Templates: Human in the loop, Sequential, Group chat. Power Fx variables carry a scope prefix, System. or Local..

Function-calling loop, in order: define the function tool, create the agent with it, send a prompt, execute the function and return its output, get the final response. The model never runs your code; your app does. Runs expire 10 minutes after creation, so return outputs promptly, and the portal can't add or edit function definitions (SDK or REST only). tool_choice (auto, required, none) controls whether tools must be used.

conv = openai.conversations.create()
tool = FunctionTool(name="get_order_status", description="Look up an order",
    parameters={"type": "object", "properties": {"order_id": {"type": "string"}},
                "required": ["order_id"], "additionalProperties": False}, strict=True)
agent = project.agents.create_version(agent_name="OrderBot",
    definition=PromptAgentDefinition(model="gpt-4.1-mini", instructions="Answer order questions.", tools=[tool]))
ref = {"agent_reference": {"name": agent.name, "type": "agent_reference"}}
resp = openai.responses.create(input="Where is order 42?", conversation=conv.id, extra_body=ref)
results = [FunctionCallOutput(type="function_call_output", call_id=i.call_id,
                              output=json.dumps(get_status(**json.loads(i.arguments))))
           for i in resp.output if i.type == "function_call"]
final = openai.responses.create(input=results, conversation=conv.id, extra_body=ref)
  • Reasoning steps: for hard multistep problems use a reasoning model on the Responses API; reasoning tokens count against the context and are billed as output tokens.
  • Structured outputs pass reliable JSON between steps: response_format on Chat Completions, text.format on Responses. They enforce the schema, unlike JSON mode, which only guarantees valid JSON. They are not supported with parallel function calls, so set parallel_tool_calls to false; function tools use strict: true.

Evaluate models and apps, including detecting fabrications, relevance, quality, and safety

The flow is: choose what to evaluate (a dataset, generated responses, simulated conversations or production traces; one turn or a whole conversation), pick evaluators, run (once, in CI/CD, or on a schedule or continuously), then review and improve. Run it from the portal or the SDK; evaluations need Microsoft Entra ID (API keys aren't supported) and the Foundry User role.

Question you must answerEvaluatorScale and notes
Does the answer state things the context doesn't support (fabrication)?Groundedness1–5, precision aspect; you supply the judge model (deployment_name)
Same, but strict and without a judge deploymentGroundedness Pro PreviewAzure AI Content Safety; returns True/False
Does the answer address the query?Relevance1–5 (query, response)
Did the answer miss expected facts?Response Completeness PreviewRecall against ground truth
Were the retrieved chunks relevant?Retrieval (LLM judge, no ground truth); Document Retrieval (needs query relevance labels)Document Retrieval: Fidelity, NDCG, XDCG, Max Relevance, Holes, for tuning retrieval settings
Harmful content?Violence, Sexual, Self-harm, Hate and unfairness (builtin.violence and so on)0–7 severity, pass if score ≤ threshold
Jailbreak injected through a document?Indirect Attack (XPIA)Model only
Agent breaks policy or leaks data?Prohibited actions, Sensitive data leakage PreviewAgents only
  • Direction of the scales: AI-assisted quality evaluators score 1–5 and pass at or above the threshold (default 3). Content-safety evaluators score 0–7 severity and pass at or below the threshold (default 3). They run on hosted evaluation models in the Foundry evaluation service and need your project information, not your own judge deployment.
  • Coherence and Fluency judge writing quality, not factual correctness. For a RAG app combine Retrieval, Groundedness, Relevance and a safety evaluator.
  • Groundedness detection in Azure AI Content Safety is a filter and API, not the evaluator: non-reasoning mode (fast, binary, online) or reasoning mode (explanations, for development), domain Medical or Generic, task Summarization or QnA, with optional correction Preview.
  • The AI Red Teaming Agent uses PyRIT and the risk and safety evaluators to run automated adversarial scans, scores each attack and response pair, and reports Attack Success Rate and a scorecard. Scheduled red team scans in Monitor settings are labelled Preview (§2.2).
testing_criteria = [
  {"type": "azure_ai_evaluator", "name": "groundedness", "evaluator_name": "builtin.groundedness",
   "initialization_parameters": {"deployment_name": model_deployment},
   "data_mapping": {"context": "{{item.context}}", "response": "{{item.response}}"}},
  {"type": "azure_ai_evaluator", "name": "violence", "evaluator_name": "builtin.violence",
   "data_mapping": {"query": "{{item.query}}", "response": "{{item.response}}"}}]
evaluation = openai_client.evals.create(name="rag-gate", data_source_config=data_source_config,
                                        testing_criteria=testing_criteria)

Integrate generative workflows into applications by using Foundry SDKs and connectors

SDKUse it whenEndpoint
Foundry SDK (azure-ai-projects)Agents, evaluations, platform tools, memory, MCPhttps://<resource-name>.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/<project-name>
Agent FrameworkHosted agents and multi-agent code in C# or Python (FoundryChatClient)Responses API on the project endpoint
OpenAI SDKBest latency, maximum OpenAI compatibility, embeddings, Chat Completions on Models sold by Azurehttps://<resource-name>.openai.azure.com/openai/v1
Anthropic SDKClaude models deployed in Foundryhttps://<resource-name>.services.ai.azure.com/anthropic
Foundry Tools SDKsVision, Speech, Language, Content SafetyTool-specific endpoints

A Foundry resource exposes all of these endpoints; an Azure OpenAI resource exposes only /openai/v1, which has no agents, evaluations or Foundry platform tools. The project endpoint doesn't currently route embedding requests, so create a second client for the OpenAI endpoint. AIProjectClient handles Foundry-native operations (connections, agent versions); get_openai_client() returns the OpenAI-compatible client for Responses, conversations, evaluations and vector stores. Most apps use both.

from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential, get_bearer_token_provider
from azure.ai.projects import AIProjectClient
from openai import OpenAI

project = AIProjectClient(endpoint=PROJECT_ENDPOINT, credential=DefaultAzureCredential())
openai_client = project.get_openai_client()            # responses, conversations, evals

token_provider = get_bearer_token_provider(DefaultAzureCredential(), "https://ai.azure.com/.default")
embedder = OpenAI(base_url="https://<resource-name>.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/", api_key=token_provider)
vectors = embedder.embeddings.create(model="text-embedding-3-small", input=["red running shoes"])
  • Versions: Python pip install "azure-ai-projects>=2.3.0" "openai>=3.0.0" (Python 3.10+). SDK 2.x targets Foundry (new), 1.x targets Foundry (classic). For .NET use Azure.AI.Projects 2.0.0 with Azure.AI.Projects.Agents and Azure.AI.Extensions.OpenAI; do not also install the preview Azure.AI.Projects.OpenAI (duplicate types cause ambiguous-reference errors).
  • Connections are project-scoped references to Azure AI Search, Storage, Application Insights and other resources; project.connections.get(name).id supplies a project_connection_id. Creating MCP connections needs Foundry Project Manager.
  • Connectors Preview: the Foundry Tools Catalog has over 1,000. Adding one creates a managed MCP server in the account's Connector Namespace, scoped to the project. Only actions are available, not triggers, and the feature is regional.
  • Toolbox GA: curate tools once and expose them through one MCP-compatible endpoint with central credentials and versioning. Function calling can't be a toolbox tool because it runs in your app. Remote servers use MCPTool(server_label, server_url, require_approval, allowed_tools, project_connection_id).

Configure an application to connect to a Foundry project

An app needs three things: the project endpoint (https://<resource-name>.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/<project-name>, shown on the project's overview page; a custom subdomain replaces the resource name), a credential, and RBAC. Standing the project up from the CLI:

az cognitiveservices account create --name my-foundry-resource --resource-group my-rg \
  --kind AIServices --sku S0 --location eastus --custom-domain my-foundry-resource \
  --assign-identity --allow-project-management true
az cognitiveservices account project create --name my-foundry-resource \
  --resource-group my-rg --project-name my-foundry-project --location eastus
  • --assign-identity is required (without it project creation fails), --allow-project-management can't be changed later, and --custom-domain must be globally unique.
  • Authentication: use Microsoft Entra ID, not keys. DefaultAzureCredential uses az login locally and a managed identity in production; the token scope is https://ai.azure.com/.default. Keys give full access without per-user RBAC and don't work for agents.
  • Environment-variable names such as FOUNDRY_PROJECT_ENDPOINT, AZURE_AI_PROJECT_ENDPOINT and AZURE_AI_MODEL_DEPLOYMENT_NAME are conventions that vary between samples; only the values matter.
RoleCan doCannot do
Foundry UserBuild and test agents (data actions); least-privilege developer roleManage projects or publish
Foundry Agent ConsumerOnly call agent endpointsCreate or edit agents
Foundry Project ManagerManage projects, build, publish agents, assign Foundry UserCreate accounts
Foundry Account OwnerCreate accounts and projects, manage models, assign rolesBuild (no data actions)
Foundry OwnerEverything above–
Azure Owner, Contributor, ReaderManage (Owner, Contributor) or read (Reader) resourcesBuild (no data actions)
  • Minimum assignment: Foundry User on the Foundry resource for your user and the project's managed identity. The portal adds both automatically when the creator can assign roles. Add Cognitive Services Usages Reader at subscription scope to see quota. Don't use Azure AI Developer for Foundry projects.
  • Standard agent setup: Foundry Account Owner creates the account and project, and Role Based Access Control Administrator assigns roles on your own Storage, Search and Cosmos DB resources.
  • Troubleshooting: DefaultAzureCredential failed to retrieve a token means run az login and confirm at least Foundry User on the project; Connection refused or 404 means wrong resource or project name or endpoint format; AttributeError usually means an old SDK version.
Exam traps
  • Standard is not GlobalStandard: Global types may process in any region, only Data Zone types stay inside the US, EU or APAC zone, and Standard stays inside one geography. Developer is for evaluating fine-tuned models, never production.
  • The deployment name, not the model name, goes in model. 400 Model not supported from responses.create means switch to Chat Completions, not fix auth or quota.
  • Fine-tuning doesn't add knowledge; minimal retrieval reasoning effort skips LLM query planning; LLM planning and answer synthesis are Preview, so a GA-only workload uses classic RAG (or the GA 2026-04-01 API with minimal, extractive retrieval).
  • Embeddings go to the OpenAI endpoint (/openai/v1), not the project endpoint. Function calling executes in your code and is not a toolbox tool.
  • Quality evaluators pass at or above the threshold (1–5); safety evaluators pass at or below it (0–7). Indirect Attack is model only; Groundedness uses your judge model, Groundedness Pro uses Content Safety.
  • Foundry User is needed on the developer and the project's managed identity. Azure Owner, Contributor and Foundry Account Owner cannot build; Foundry Agent Consumer can only call agents.
