sections.title: 2.2 Build agents by using Foundry
sections.html:
Skills measured: define agent roles, goals, conversation-tracking approach and tool schemas • build agents that integrate retrieval, function-calling and conversation memory • integrate agent tools, including APIs, knowledge stores, search, content understanding and custom functions • implement orchestrated multi-agent solutions • build autonomous or semiautonomous workflows with safeguards and approval flow controls • integrate monitoring into deployed agents, evaluate agent behavior and perform error analysis. Practise by creating a prompt agent with create_version, giving it a memory store and an OpenAPI tool, forcing an MCP approval, calling a second agent over A2A, and creating a continuous evaluation rule. Retrieval and the function-call loop are introduced in §2.1; tuning, tracing detail and cost are in §2.3.

Define agent roles, goals, conversation-tracking approach, and tool schemas

An agent is a stored definition: model, instructions, tools and settings. Agents are identified by name and version; there is no AgentID GUID any more. A version is an immutable snapshot, so any change (even one prompt edit) creates a new version. The agent's endpoint is live as soon as the agent exists, and its version_selector routes traffic: Always use latest (default: 100% of traffic goes to the newest version, so an agent published to Teams or Microsoft 365 changes at once) or pinned to one active version. Choose a prompt agent (declarative, Foundry runs it), a voice-based prompt agent, a hosted agent (your own code) or call the Responses API from an agent you run yourself.

agent = project.agents.create_version(
    agent_name="SupportBot",
    definition=PromptAgentDefinition(
        model="gpt-4.1-mini",
        instructions="You are Contoso's order-support agent. Answer only order questions. "
                     "If data is missing ask one clarifying question, otherwise say you don't know.",
        tools=[order_tool]))
# REST: POST {project-endpoint}/agents?api-version=v1
#   {"name": "support-bot", "definition": {"kind": "prompt", "model": "gpt-4.1-mini", "instructions": "..."}}

Write the role and goal in the instructions: scope, tone, output format, safety rules and an explicit fallback; avoid conflicting rules. Instructions influence behaviour but don't guarantee it, so add filtering and evaluation. Give tools clear names and descriptions and say when each applies. The three runtime pieces are the agent, the conversation (persisted items) and the response (one execution). Invoke a named agent with extra_body={"agent_reference": {"name": ..., "type": "agent_reference"}}.

Tracking approachCodeUse when
Conversation objectopenai.conversations.create(), then responses.create(conversation=conv.id, ...)Multi-turn continuity, a user who returns later, inspecting messages, tool calls and outputs
Response chainingresponses.create(previous_response_id=resp.id, ...)Multi-turn without a conversation object; responses are stored by default
Client-carried statestore=False and resend earlier items in inputZero data retention, minimal stored data, full control
  • If a conversation outgrows the model's context, the model input is truncated automatically; the stored conversation is not. State lives in platform storage with the basic setup and in your Storage, AI Search and Cosmos DB with the standard setup.
  • Function tool schema: JSON Schema with "type": "object", properties, required, "additionalProperties": False and strict=True; your app runs it.
  • OpenAPI tool: OpenAPI 3.0 or 3.1; every operation needs an operationId (letters, - and _ only); request bodies application/json or application/json-patch+json; auth is anonymous, API key (a project connection) or managed identity.
  • MCP tool: server_label, server_url, allowed_tools, require_approval, project_connection_id.

Build agents that integrate retrieval, function-calling, and conversation memory

Attach one or more tools and the model decides when to call them from the input and the instructions. Retrieval is file search, the Azure AI Search tool or a Foundry IQ knowledge base (§2.1); function calling is a FunctionTool plus your execution loop (§2.1); memory is the memory search tool below.

Memory Preview (with the Memory Store API) keeps long-term knowledge across sessions, while conversations hold short-term context. It works in phases: extraction of key facts, consolidation (an LLM merges duplicates and resolves conflicts), then retrieval. Types, all enabled by default: user profile, chat summary and procedural. A store needs a chat model and an embedding model deployment; create one store per agent. Use the memory search tool on a prompt agent (it reads and writes) or the low-level store APIs for item CRUD.

options = MemoryStoreDefaultOptions(chat_summary_enabled=True, user_profile_enabled=True,
                                    procedural_memory_enabled=True)
definition = MemoryStoreDefaultDefinition(chat_model=chat_deployment,
                                          embedding_model=embedding_deployment, options=options)
store = project_client.beta.memory_stores.create(name="travel_memory", definition=definition)

tool = MemorySearchPreviewTool(memory_store_name="travel_memory", scope="{{$userId}}", update_delay=300)
reply = openai_client.responses.create(
    input="I prefer aisle seats", conversation=conv.id,
    extra_body={"agent_reference": {"name": agent.name, "type": "agent_reference"}},
    extra_headers={"x-memory-user-id": user_id})
  • scope partitions memory. With the tool, "{{$userId}}" resolves from the x-memory-user-id header (use it when a backend or proxy calls on behalf of users) and otherwise from the caller's Entra tenant and object IDs. The low-level APIs need an explicit scope; a static scope means no per-user isolation.
  • update_delay is the seconds of inactivity before memories are written; default 300 (5 minutes).
  • Limits: 100 scopes per store, 10,000 memories per scope, 1,000 search and 1,000 update requests per minute. VNet integration isn't supported, and memory is available only in listed regions.
The agent needsUse
Per-user preferences learned over timeMemory store plus memory search tool
Curated organisational contentFoundry IQ knowledge base or Azure AI Search
Documents the user suppliesFile search
The current dialogConversation or previous_response_id
Live data or an action in your systemFunction, OpenAPI or MCP tool

Integrate agent tools, including APIs, knowledge stores, search, content understanding, and custom functions

NeedToolKey facts
Call my REST APIOpenAPI toolAuth: anonymous, API key or managed identity. For managed identity grant the project's identity the least-privileged role on the API's resource. One API-key scheme per tool; use several tools for several schemes. FOUNDRY_PROJECT_ENDPOINT is the Foundry endpoint, not the API's.
Hosted tool server or SaaSMCP tool (or a connector, Preview)Auth through a project connection: key, Microsoft Entra identity or OAuth identity passthrough. Restrict with allowed_tools.
Search or knowledgeAI Search tool, file search, Foundry IQSee §2.1. Fabric IQ and Work IQ are separate tools, not Foundry IQ.
Code that must run in my appFunction toolClient-side execution; not available in a toolbox
Serverless logic over queuesAzure Functions toolQueue-based; standard agent setup only; Storage Queue Data Contributor for the project's and the function app's managed identities
Files, images, audio, video as inputContent Understanding context providerAgent Framework; prerelease package
Shared, governed toolsToolbox (GA)One MCP-compatible endpoint, central auth

Toolbox membership: MCP, web search, Azure AI Search, code interpreter, file search, OpenAPI, A2A, browser automation, Fabric IQ and Work IQ work in a toolbox or directly; tool search, skills and the reminder tool are toolbox only; function calling, Grounding with Bing, computer use, image generation, SharePoint, Fabric data agent and Azure Functions are direct only. Check tool support by region and model before building.

Content Understanding is attached through ContentUnderstandingContextProvider (pip install agent-framework-azure-contentunderstanding --pre). Before each model call it detects documents, images, audio and video in the input, analyses them and adds Markdown plus extracted fields to the model context. analyzer_id defaults to prebuilt-documentSearch (documents and images), prebuilt-audioSearch or prebuilt-videoSearch; max_wait is how many seconds to wait before deferring analysis to the background (default 5, None waits); file_search can send the Markdown to a vector store instead.

cu = ContentUnderstandingContextProvider(endpoint="https://my-resource.cognitiveservices.azure.com/",
                                         credential=credential, max_wait=None)
async with cu:
    agent = Agent(client=client, name="DocumentQA", instructions="You are a document analyst.",
                  context_providers=[cu])

Tool guardrails: the Tool call and Tool response intervention points only work for tools that support moderation: Azure AI Search, Azure Functions, OpenAPI, SharePoint Grounding, Fabric Data Agent, Bing Grounding, Bing Custom Search and Browser Automation. Controls on other tools don't take effect.

Implement orchestrated multi-agent solutions

Start with a direct call, then one agent with tools. A multi-agent design is justified when one agent can't reliably cope because of prompt complexity, tool overload or security requirements; it adds overhead, latency and failure modes.

PatternHow it runsUse whenAvoid when
SequentialFixed order; each agent gets the previous outputDraft, review, polish; clear dependenciesStages can run in parallel; backtracking or dynamic routing
ConcurrentAll agents work on the same task at once; results aggregatedIndependent perspectives, voting, time-sensitive workAgents must build on each other; strict order; quota limits; shared-state conflicts
Group chat (maker-checker is a variant)Chat manager and one shared thread; humans can joinBrainstorming, validation, review loops; keep to three or fewer agentsA linear pipeline is enough; loops can't be stopped
HandoffAn agent decides to transfer; full control moves; one agent at a timeThe right specialist emerges during processingRouting is deterministic (use a dispatcher); handoff loops
MagenticA manager builds a plan and delegates to tool-using agentsOpen-ended work with no predetermined pathThe path is already known
  • Microsoft Agent Framework ships all five orchestrations, with human-in-the-loop through tool approval and request info. Hosted agents running Agent Framework code are the code-first path.
  • The classic Connected Agents tool isn't available in the new Foundry Agent Service. Use the A2A tool, or Workflows (Preview, retiring December 1, 2026; migrate to Agent Framework, Azure Logic Apps or A2A).
  • A2A: a2a (A2ATool, protocol 1.0, GA) versus a2a_preview (A2APreviewTool, protocol 0.3, Preview). A Foundry agent target needs incoming A2A enabled and the caller needs Foundry Agent Consumer or higher on the target project; only text is supported and streaming isn't.
  • Responses API multi-agent Preview (GPT-5.6 models): openai.beta.responses.create(model=deployment, input=prompt, multi_agent={"enabled": True, "max_concurrent_subagents": 3}).
  • Tracing: OpenTelemetry multi-agent spans are invoke_agent (nested for agent-to-agent), plan, invoke_workflow and execute_tool.

Build autonomous or semiautonomous workflows with safeguards and approval flow controls

Autonomy is a dial: fully autonomous agents act without a person; semiautonomous agents pause for approval before consequential steps. Constrain the loop too: set iteration limits on a single agent, and give a maker-checker loop an iteration cap and a fallback (human escalation or a quality warning).

tool = MCPTool(server_label="tickets", server_url="https://tickets.contoso.example/mcp",
               require_approval="always", allowed_tools=["create_ticket"],
               project_connection_id=MCP_CONNECTION_NAME)
# ... resp = openai.responses.create(...); then answer each approval request:
inputs = [McpApprovalResponse(type="mcp_approval_response", approve=True, approval_request_id=i.id)
          for i in resp.output if i.type == "mcp_approval_request"]
resp = openai.responses.create(input=inputs, previous_response_id=resp.id, extra_body=agent_ref)
  • MCP approvals: with require_approval="always" the output holds mcp_approval_request items (server label, tool name, arguments). Review them, then send McpApprovalResponse. Use an allowed_tools allow list, require approval for write or change operations, log approvals and tool calls, and treat tool descriptions and results as untrusted (indirect prompt injection).
  • Agent Framework: @tool(approval_mode="always_require"); loop over result.user_input_requests and answer with request.to_function_approval_response(True) (False rejects); in .NET wrap the function in ApprovalRequiredAIFunction. Samples use never_require only for brevity.
  • Long waits Preview: a hosted agent's @multi_turn_task chain suspends under one task_id and resumes when the person replies (ctx.entry_mode == "resumed"), surviving restarts. A plain function turn must finish within the 10-minute run limit.
  • Guardrails: a named set of controls, each a risk + intervention point + action. Four intervention points: User input, Tool call and Tool response (both Preview, agents only) and Output. Each adds roughly 50–100 ms. For agents the action is Annotate and block. Agent guardrails are Preview, apply only to agents built in Foundry Agent Service and fully override the model's guardrail; hosted agents also get network egress controls (Preview). Creating a guardrail needs Foundry Account Owner.
  • Task Adherence Preview flags tool calls that don't match the user's intent: the response has taskRiskDetected and details; block the call or escalate to a person.
  • Least privilege: grant tool roles to the project's managed identity, minimise data sent to tools, keep secrets out of prompts and traces, validate structured outputs, and require approval before consequential actions. Test safeguards with the Prohibited actions and Sensitive data leakage evaluators (agents only, Preview) and red team scans.

Integrate monitoring into deployed agents, evaluate agent behavior, and perform error analysis

Connect an Application Insights resource to the project. Server-side tracing then starts automatically with no code (GA for prompt and hosted agents, Preview for workflow and external agents) and keeps about 90 days of traces in the portal. Reading telemetry needs Log Analytics Reader on the connected resource, plus Privileged Monitoring Data Reader if the tables are protected. Client-side instrumentation of your own code is a second step.

The Agent Monitoring Dashboard Preview is on Build → agent → Monitor: token usage, latency (above 10 seconds suggests throttling, complex tool calls or network issues), run success rate (below 95% warrants investigation), evaluation metrics and red-teaming results. Monitor settings hold Recurring evaluations, Red team scans and Alerts, all Preview.

Continuous evaluationScheduled evaluation
RunsSamples live traffic when a response completesOn a fixed schedule over test or trace data (drift)
SDK objectproject_client.evaluation_rules.create_or_update with EvaluationRuleproject_client.beta.schedules.create_or_update with Schedule
Key settingsContinuousEvaluationRuleAction(eval_id, max_hourly_runs=100)RecurrenceTrigger, EvaluationScheduleTask
rule = project_client.evaluation_rules.create_or_update(
    id="my-continuous-eval-rule",
    evaluation_rule=EvaluationRule(
        display_name="My Continuous Eval Rule",
        action=ContinuousEvaluationRuleAction(eval_id=eval_object.id, max_hourly_runs=100),
        event_type=EvaluationRuleEventType.RESPONSE_COMPLETED,
        filter=EvaluationRuleFilter(agent_name=agent.name),
        enabled=True))
  • Continuous evaluation needs the project's managed identity to have Foundry User. Runs are skipped once the hourly limit (default 100) is reached: raise max_hourly_runs. Results missing means check the rule is enabled and traffic is flowing; empty charts usually mean no recent traffic, a time range without data or ingestion delay, and authorization errors mean missing roles on Application Insights or Log Analytics.
  • Agent evaluators: system evaluators judge the end result (Task Completion, Task Adherence, Intent Resolution, Customer Satisfaction, Task Navigation Efficiency, which needs ground truth); process evaluators judge the steps (Tool Call Accuracy, Tool Selection, Tool Input Accuracy). Task Completion, Task Adherence, Intent Resolution and Customer Satisfaction are Preview. The rubric evaluator Preview (weighted criteria, LLM judge) is the recommended primary measure; set acceptance thresholds before release (for example a pass-rate target for task adherence; the docs don't prescribe a number).
  • Error analysis: read traces to step through model calls, tool calls and retries. Cluster analysis Preview groups failing evaluation samples: select completed runs, choose Cluster analysis, pick a model, Generate; the result isn't stored, so download it. Insights in Foundry Preview mines production traces for recurring behaviours; it needs a GPT-5 or newer deployment and Monitoring Reader on Application Insights for the user and the project's managed identity.
Exam traps
  • Agents are addressed by name and version; edits create immutable versions and traffic follows latest by default, so pin the version in production. Threads, runs and assistants are the old model.
  • store=False means no server-side history, so previous_response_id and conversation objects don't apply: resend the items yourself. Auto-truncation shortens the model input, not the stored conversation.
  • An OpenAPI operation without operationId fails; managed-identity auth needs a role on the target API's resource for the project's identity. A function tool runs in your app and can't be in a toolbox; the Azure Functions tool is queue-based and needs the standard setup.
  • Memory is Preview, has no VNet support and scopes to the caller's Entra identity unless x-memory-user-id is sent; low-level memory APIs never infer the scope.
  • Connected Agents is gone (use A2A); a2a is 1.0 GA and a2a_preview is 0.3 Preview; handoff passes full control to one agent at a time; Foundry workflows are Preview and retiring December 1, 2026.
  • Tool call and tool response guardrails silently skip unsupported tools; continuous evaluation samples live traffic while scheduled runs on a timetable; cluster analysis output disappears when you leave the page.

sections.title: 2.3 Optimize and operationalize generative AI systems
sections.html:
Skills measured: tune generation behavior, such as prompt engineering and adjusting model parameters • implement model reflection, chain-of-thought evaluations and self-critique loops • set up observability by implementing tracing, token analytics, safety signals and latency breakdowns • orchestrate multiple models, flows or hybrid LLM and rules engines. Practise by calling one reasoning deployment through Chat Completions and the Responses API, tracing a Python app into Application Insights, and fronting two deployments with model router and an API Management backend pool. Metric names are in §1.3, trace storage and sensitive-content protection in §1.4, agent patterns in §2.2.

Tune generation behavior, such as prompt engineering and adjusting model parameters

A prompt has up to five parts: instructions, primary content, examples, a cue and supporting content. Documented techniques: clear instructions first; repeat key instructions at the end (recency bias); prime the output with a cue such as the first bullet; clear syntax (separators like ---, headings, Markdown or XML; a separator can act as a stop condition); break the task down; an affordance such as search to curb fabricated answers; few-shot user and assistant turns; citations or a fixed output structure. Re-test on newer models (the examples used a base GPT-4 model) and always validate. A system message sets role and scope, tone, output contract, safety constraints and an explicit fallback; it influences the model but does not guarantee compliance.

SettingRule
temperature (0 to 2), top_pRandomness on non-reasoning models: higher temperature is more random, lower is more focused and deterministic; top_p 0.1 keeps only the top 10% probability mass. The docs recommend changing one, not both.
max_tokensLegacy Chat cap (deprecated). The TPM rate-limit estimate counts it, so an oversized value causes early 429s.
max_completion_tokens, max_output_tokensChat / Responses cap; on reasoning models it covers reasoning and visible tokens. A cut-off shows as finish_reason: "length" or status: "incomplete".
reasoning_effort, reasoning={"effort": ...}Thinking depth; values vary by model: none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max. none suits latency-critical work (voice, classification), low tool use and planning, medium a balanced start, high hard reasoning; o1-mini is unsupported.
n, seedn is 1 to 128 choices, all billed. seed is best-effort determinism (Beta).
response_format, text.formatStructured outputs enforce a JSON Schema; the older JSON mode only guarantees valid JSON.

Reasoning models (GPT-5 series, o-series) use max_completion_tokens, don't support temperature, top_p or the penalty parameters, and take a developer message that works like a system message. The techniques above "aren't recommended" for them: state the goal and tune reasoning_effort. Reasoning shares the context window, so reserve at least 25,000 tokens for reasoning and output while you size a workload, and check status on every response.

client.chat.completions.create(model="gpt-5-mini", messages=msgs,
    max_completion_tokens=5000, reasoning_effort="medium")     # Chat Completions
client.responses.create(model="gpt-5-mini", input=prompt, max_output_tokens=5000,
    reasoning={"effort": "medium"})                             # Responses API

The Foundry model playground compares up to three models and exports code. Prompt Optimizer rewrites the text instructions of a prompt or workflow agent: Build → Agents → agent → Instructions → pencil-and-sparkle icon → optional suggestion → Optimize → read the paragraph-level reasoning → Use prompt. Unapplied results are lost, there is no version history and tools or knowledge aren't optimized, so evaluate afterwards. PromptAgentDefinition carries instructions, temperature, top_p, reasoning and text.

Exam traps
  • max_tokens, max_completion_tokens and max_output_tokens differ: reasoning models need the second (Chat) or third (Responses).
  • Few-shot, cue and chain-of-thought tricks target non-reasoning models; for a reasoning model change reasoning_effort.
  • A bigger max_tokens is not free: the rate-limit estimate counts it even when answers are short.
  • A system message guides but does not enforce.

Implement model reflection, chain-of-thought evaluations, and self-critique loops

A reasoning model produces reasoning tokens before it answers. They never appear in the message content, occupy the context window and are billed as output tokens; read them from output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens (Responses) or completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens (Chat). To show how the model reasoned, request a reasoning summary: reasoning={"effort": "medium", "summary": "auto"} on the Responses API (auto, concise or detailed; the GPT-5 series has no concise). Summaries aren't guaranteed for every request and reasoning.summary isn't supported with multi-agent orchestration. Extracting raw reasoning any other way is unsupported, may break the Acceptable Use Policy and can lead to throttling or suspension. Chain-of-thought prompting is only for non-reasoning models. Between function calls send the reasoning items back (previous_response_id or copied output items); reasoning.context (auto, current_turn, all_turns) decides whether earlier turns' reasoning is rendered, and all_turns raises the tokens billed.

Chain-of-thought evaluations are LLM-as-judge evaluators that explain their verdict. Judges such as builtin.groundedness, builtin.relevance and builtin.coherence need a judge deployment_name and return score (1 to 5), label, reason, threshold (default 3) and passed. A reasoning or non-reasoning Azure OpenAI or OpenAI model can judge (gpt-5-mini is suggested) and every judge call costs inference. The Rubric evaluator Preview scores custom weighted criteria (0 to 1, per-dimension reasoning). Groundedness detection offers a fast Non-Reasoning mode for real time and a Reasoning mode that explains ungrounded segments, for development and debugging.

testing_criteria = [{
    "type": "azure_ai_evaluator", "name": "groundedness",
    "evaluator_name": "builtin.groundedness",
    "initialization_parameters": {"deployment_name": model_deployment},
    "data_mapping": {"query": "{{item.query}}", "context": "{{item.context}}",
                     "response": "{{item.response}}"},
}]

Self-critique = maker-checker (also called evaluator-optimizer, generator-verifier, critic or reflection loop): the maker drafts, the checker judges against defined criteria, specific feedback returns, and the cycle repeats until approval or a maximum iteration count. It needs clear acceptance criteria, an iteration cap and a fallback (escalate to a human reviewer, or return the best result with a quality warning). It is group chat orchestration driven by a chat manager; keep to three or fewer agents (§2.2).

# Illustrative loop, not a documented sample
for attempt in range(MAX_ROUNDS):                    # iteration cap
    draft = maker(task, feedback)
    verdict = checker(draft, ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA)    # pass or fail plus a reason
    if verdict.passed:
        break
    feedback = verdict.reason                        # specific feedback for the maker
else:
    escalate_to_reviewer(draft, verdict)             # fallback when the cap is reached
Exam traps
  • Reasoning tokens are invisible but billed and counted against the cap; a small cap can end with no visible answer.
  • A reasoning summary is not the raw chain of thought, and other extraction attempts risk throttling or suspension.
  • "Think step by step" is for non-reasoning models; a judge's reason explains a score, not hidden reasoning.
  • Without acceptance criteria, a cap and a fallback, a maker-checker loop can run forever or approve inconsistently.

Set up observability by implementing tracing, token analytics, safety signals, and latency breakdowns

Server-side tracing starts when Application Insights is connected (§1.4, §2.2). Client-side tracing adds spans from your own code with OpenTelemetry; the GenAI instrumentation is an experimental Preview, so span names and attributes can change. Python, in order: install azure-ai-projects, azure-identity, opentelemetry-sdk, azure-core-tracing-opentelemetry and azure-monitor-opentelemetry (azure-ai-projects 2.0.0 or later); set AZURE_EXPERIMENTAL_ENABLE_GENAI_TRACING to true before AIProjectInstrumentor().instrument(), or nothing is instrumented and a warning is logged; get the connection string; call configure_azure_monitor; pass agent_reference with both name and id so the trace links to the agent.

import os
os.environ["AZURE_EXPERIMENTAL_ENABLE_GENAI_TRACING"] = "true"             # before instrument()
os.environ["OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT"] = "true"  # content: development only

from azure.ai.projects.telemetry import AIProjectInstrumentor
from azure.monitor.opentelemetry import configure_azure_monitor

AIProjectInstrumentor().instrument()
cs = project.telemetry.get_application_insights_connection_string()  # ResourceNotFoundError if none
configure_azure_monitor(connection_string=cs)

Content recording also works as instrument(enable_content_recording=True) (a parameter beats its variable) and captures messages, tool arguments and outputs. @trace_function (from azure.ai.projects.telemetry) always records parameters and the return value. W3C traceparent and tracestate propagate by default; baggage only with enable_baggage_propagation=True. C#: AppContext.SetSwitch("Azure.Experimental.EnableGenAITracing", true); JavaScript SDK: tracingOptions: { experimental: true }.

NeedWhere to look
Tokens in one requestusage. Responses: input_tokens, output_tokens, output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens, input_tokens_details.cached_tokens. Chat: prompt_tokens, completion_tokens and matching *_details. Streamed calls may omit counts unless include_usage is true.
Tokens per deploymentAzure Monitor InputTokens, OutputTokens, TotalTokens, split by ModelDeploymentName; no per-user dimension. Cost data can take up to five hours to appear.
Tokens per app, user or teamAPI Management llm-emit-token-metric: a namespace and up to five custom dimension elements, sent to Application Insights.
Cap tokensllm-token-limit: tokens-per-minute breach gives 429, token-quota with token-quota-period gives 403. Foundry AI Gateway Preview: Manage → AI Gateway → Token management → + Set limit (project scope; enabling the gateway for a project needs API Management Service Contributor or Owner on the API Management resource).
LatencyCompare span durations (model call, execute_tool, your own spans). TimeToResponse and NormalizedTimeBetweenTokens cover streaming on PTU and PTU-managed deployments, measured at the gateway, without client-side latency. A higher reasoning_effort lengthens responses; a short preamble gets a first visible token sooner.
Safety signalscontent_filter_results (per category filtered, severity) and prompt_filter_results (including jailbreak) in each response; finish_reason content_filter means content was omitted. Metrics: §1.3. Evaluators and red-team scans: §1.4.
Exam traps
  • Setting the opt-in variable after instrument() leaves tracing off.
  • Deployment token metrics split by model and deployment, not by user; per-consumer counts need llm-emit-token-metric.
  • Content recording puts prompts and tool arguments into traces; keep it to development unless compliance allows.
  • TimeToResponse excludes client-side latency and applies to PTU and PTU-managed streaming only.
  • Token limits fail differently: rate gives 429, quota gives 403.

Orchestrate multiple models, flows, or hybrid LLM and rules engines

Use the lowest complexity that works: a direct model call, then one agent with tools, then multi-agent orchestration (more overhead, latency and failure modes). Model router is a trained language model you deploy like any model (for example named model-router); it routes each prompt by complexity, reasoning need and task type, doesn't store prompts and honors data zone boundaries. Balanced (default) picks the cheapest model within about 1 to 2% of the best quality, Cost accepts about 5 to 6%, Quality takes the best model and ignores cost. A model subset limits the pool and is the failover set (pick at least two). Version 2025-11-18 supports Global Standard and Data Zone Standard deployments; Claude models must be deployed first; the effective context window is that of the smallest underlying model. Benchmark it against your current named model.

with project.get_openai_client() as client:
    routed = client.responses.create(model="model-router", input=prompt)
    fixed = client.responses.create(model="gpt-5-mini", input=prompt)   # deterministic choice
    print(routed.model)      # the model that handled the request; log it for cost attribution
NeedUse
Mixed-difficulty traffic behind one deploymentModel router
A fixed model per task, for compliance or benchmarksA named deployment; only model changes
PTU first, overflow to pay-as-you-goAPI Management backend pool with priorities and a circuit breaker on the PTU backend
Thresholds, validation, arithmeticCode or a rules engine; the LLM only extracts and drafts

An API Management backend pool (type: 'Pool', up to 30 backends, each in pool.services with id, priority, weight) balances round-robin, weighted or priority-based, with optional session awareness. A lower priority group gets traffic only when every higher-priority backend is unavailable because a circuit breaker rule tripped. A rule (one per backend; not on the Consumption tier) has a failureCondition, a tripDuration and acceptRetryAfter; Azure OpenAI overload returns 429 with a possibly large Retry-After. Semantic caching uses llm-semantic-cache-lookup and llm-semantic-cache-store.

circuitBreaker: {
  rules: [
    {
      name: 'ptu-overload'
      failureCondition: {
        count: 1
        interval: 'PT1M'
        statusCodeRanges: [
          {
            min: 429
            max: 429
          }
        ]
      }
      tripDuration: 'PT1M'
      acceptRetryAfter: true
    }
  ]
}

Flows. Use an agent for open-ended work and a workflow for well-defined steps; "if you can write a function to handle the task, do that instead of using an AI agent". Agent Framework graph workflows join typed executors with edges (direct, conditional, switch-case, fan-out, fan-in), for example WorkflowBuilder(start_executor=classifier).add_edge(classifier, handler, condition=is_urgent). Foundry workflows (Preview, retiring December 1, 2026) and Prompt flow (classic, retiring April 20, 2027) both point to Microsoft Agent Framework. Hybrid LLM and rules: the LLM extracts or classifies into schema-valid JSON (response_format or text.format), you validate it against the expected schema and allow only known fields and operations, code or rules decide, and a person approves consequential actions. Skip handoff when routing is rule-based or the right agent is obvious from the input; use a dispatcher.

Exam traps
  • Priorities alone never spill over: without a tripped circuit breaker the PTU backend keeps receiving requests and clients see its 429s.
  • Weights split traffic only inside one priority group; session awareness pins a session to a backend.
  • Model router is not deterministic, and its current version is deployed as Global Standard or Data Zone Standard.
  • A system message or a higher reasoning_effort does not enforce a business rule; code does.
