sections.title: 3.1 Design and implement image- and video-generation solutions
sections.html:
Skills measured: generate images from text prompts and reference media • generate videos from text prompts and reference media • image-editing workflows (inpainting, mask-based edits, prompt-driven modifications) • edit generated videos • select and apply the platform's generation and editing controls. Practise by deploying gpt-image-2 and a Sora 2 model in one Foundry resource, then calling images.generate, a masked images/edits request and videos.remix from Python. Filtering unsafe visual content is covered in §3.3.

Implement a solution that generates images from text prompts and reference media

OpenAI's gpt-image models create images from a text prompt plus optional input images. dall-e-3 was Retired on March 4, 2026 and existing deployments are non-functional, so a legacy app must be redeployed on a gpt-image- series model. Choose the family by status, reference-image capacity and route:

FamilyStatus as documentedReference imagesRoute
gpt-image-2.5-sunburst, gpt-image-2.5-flare, gpt-image-2GAText + image input; the Edit API takes up to 16 images/openai/v1/images/generations and images/edits
gpt-image-1.5, gpt-image-1, gpt-image-1-miniThe how-to says limited access preview (apply for access); the retirement schedule lists 1.5 and mini as GA and gpt-image-1 as Preview, retiring 2026-10-23Same as aboveSame as above
MAI-Image-2.6, 2.6-Flash, 2.5, 2.5-Flash, 2.5-ProPreview, Global StandardUp to five JPEG or PNG images (multipart); returns one PNGhttps://<resource>.services.ai.azure.com/mai/v1/images/generations and /mai/v1/images/edits
FLUX.2-pro, FLUX.2-flex, FLUX.1-Kontext-pro, FLUX-1.1-proBlack Forest Labs models, Global StandardFLUX.2-pro up to 8, FLUX.2-flex up to 10 (API only, not the playground); Kontext edits in contextBFL provider API (.../providers/blackforestlabs/v1/<model-path>?api-version=preview); OpenAI-compatible Image API for Kontext and FLUX-1.1-pro
  • Output: gpt-image-2, 1.5, 1 and 1-mini return the image only as base64 in data[].b64_json (no URL option), and response_format is not supported for the gpt-image-1 series; the docs say only "outputs images" for the 2.5 models. Decode and store the bytes yourself.
  • Limits: n is 1–10 images per request. The default quota is 5 images per minute per deployment for the gpt-image-1 series and gpt-image-2; on a 429 retry with exponential backoff. Complex prompts can take up to 60 seconds.
  • Endpoint: POST https://<resource>.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/images/generations?api-version=preview with Content-Type: application/json and an api-key header (or an Entra token). model is the deployment name.
  • Auth: keyless calls use the scope https://ai.azure.com/.default; a managed identity needs Cognitive Services OpenAI User on the resource. Deploying MAI or FLUX models needs Cognitive Services Contributor.
import base64
from openai import OpenAI
from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential, get_bearer_token_provider

token_provider = get_bearer_token_provider(DefaultAzureCredential(), "https://ai.azure.com/.default")
client = OpenAI(base_url="https://<resource>.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/", api_key=token_provider)

result = client.images.generate(
    model="<deployment-name>",
    prompt="a close-up of a bear walking through the forest",
    n=1, size="1024x1024", quality="high", output_format="png",
)
open("bear.png", "wb").write(base64.b64decode(result.data[0].b64_json))

The how-to's quickstart builds the client with AzureOpenAI(api_version="2025-04-01-preview", ...) instead; its streaming sample uses the OpenAI(base_url=".../openai/v1/") form above. For reference media send the images to the edit endpoint (see the editing topic).

Agent route Preview: the image generation tool in Foundry Agent Service needs a gpt-image-1 deployment and a compatible orchestrator model (for example gpt-5) in the same project. Attach it with ImageGenTool(model="gpt-image-1", quality="low", size="1024x1024") inside PromptAgentDefinition(tools=[...]) (package azure-ai-projects), send the x-ms-oai-image-generation-deployment header on responses.create, and read the base64 from the output items whose type is image_generation_call.

Implement a solution that generates videos from text prompts and reference media

Sora 2 Preview turns text, an image or a previously generated video into a clip, with generated audio and a remix feature. It uses the Azure OpenAI v1 API with the OpenAI videos schema and is billed per second. Generation is asynchronous: create, poll, download. The Sora 2 API has five operations: create, get status, download, list and delete.

Parameter of videos.createValues and rules
promptRequired. Shot type, subject, action, setting, lighting, camera motion; keep it single-purpose.
modelYour Sora 2 deployment name (the docs show Sora-2 as the default).
size720x1280 (portrait, default) or 1280x720.
seconds4, 8 or 12 (typed as a string); default 4.
input_referenceOne image (image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp) used as the visual anchor of the first frame. It must match size exactly.
remix_video_idREST name for the id of a previously completed video (see the remix topic).
import time
from openai import OpenAI   # pip install openai --upgrade, or: 'OpenAI' object has no attribute 'videos'

client = OpenAI(base_url="https://<resource>.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/", api_key=token_provider)
video = client.videos.create(
    model="<sora-2 deployment>",
    prompt="A video of a cool cat on a motorcycle in the night",
    size="1280x720", seconds="8",
    input_reference=open("first-frame-1280x720.png", "rb"),   # optional: image to video
)
while video.status not in ["completed", "failed", "cancelled"]:
    time.sleep(20)                                            # the docs poll every 20 seconds
    video = client.videos.retrieve(video.id)
if video.status == "completed":
    client.videos.download_content(video.id, variant="video").write_to_file("video.mp4")
  • Status values: queued, in_progress, completed, failed; the sample loop also tests cancelled. A clip typically takes 1 to 5 minutes. The docs' synchronous sample deliberately avoids create_and_poll (in a notebook it avoids RuntimeError: asyncio.run() cannot be called from a running event loop); that helper appears only in the async samples.
  • Retention: generated videos are kept for 24 hours; download them promptly. The response carries expires_at.
  • Content rules: only content suitable for audiences under 18; copyrighted characters and music are rejected; real people (public figures included) cannot be generated; input images with human faces are rejected.
  • Errors: a 403 means the caller lacks the Cognitive Services User role; a failed job reports failure_reason.

The same page also documents a second request shape, the Azure video generation jobs REST API. Match parameter names to the call you are given:

client.videos.* (v1 schema)Jobs REST API
Createvideos.createPOST {endpoint}/openai/v1/video/generations/jobs?api-version=...
Dimensionssize: 720x1280 or 1280x720width and height (up to 1920 × 1080)
Lengthseconds: 4, 8 or 12n_seconds: 1–20
Reference inputinput_reference: one imageMultipart inpaint_items (image or video, crop_bounds, frame_index); up to two images or one video of at most five seconds
Status valuesqueued, in_progress, completedpreprocessing, running, processing, succeeded
Check availability before you buildThe Sora 2 pages are marked preview and still document the API, but the model retirement schedule (page dated 2026-09-21) lists sora-2 version 2025-10-06 with a retirement date of 2026-07-15 and version 2025-12-08 with 2026-10-15, both as Preview. Confirm the model can still be deployed in your region, and remember that preview models carry no service-level agreement.

Configure image-editing workflows: inpainting, mask-based edits and prompt-driven modifications

The Image Edit API is documented as generally available and supported for production. It modifies existing images from a prompt. Its URL is https://<resource>.openai.azure.com/openai/deployments/<deployment>/images/edits?api-version=<api_version> (for example 2025-04-01). The request is multipart/form-data with an api-key header, not JSON.

  1. Prepare the source image: PNG or JPG, under 50 MB, up to 16 images per request (image[] in cURL).
  2. For inpainting, prepare a PNG mask with the same dimensions as the image. Pixels that are fully transparent (alpha 0) mark the area to edit; opaque pixels are preserved.
  3. POST the form fields image, optional mask, prompt, model, size, n, quality, optional input_fidelity.
  4. Read data[].b64_json, as for generation.
import requests

edit_url = f"{endpoint}openai/deployments/{deployment}/images/edits?api-version=2025-04-01-preview"
files = {
    "image": ("living-room.png", open("living-room.png", "rb"), "image/png"),
    "mask":  ("mask.png", open("mask.png", "rb"), "image/png"),   # same size as the image; transparent = edit
}
data = {"prompt": "Replace the sofa with a green velvet sofa", "n": 1, "size": "1024x1024", "quality": "medium"}
response = requests.post(edit_url, headers={"Api-Key": subscription_key}, data=data, files=files).json()
image_b64 = response["data"][0]["b64_json"]
GoalConfigure
Replace or remove one regionimage + PNG mask (alpha 0 over the region) + prompt = inpainting
Restyle or change the whole sceneimage + prompt only; the model decides what changes (prompt-driven edit)
Keep faces and untouched areas stableRaise input_fidelity; it is not supported by gpt-image-1-mini
Combine several assetsRepeat image[] (up to 16)
No-code trialImages playground: Build → Models → deployment → attach image → inpainting → View Code. Inpainting with text transformation is available for gpt-image-1 and gpt-image-2.

MAI-Image edits (Preview) take repeated multipart image parts and cover object removal or replacement, attribute changes, inpainting, text updates and artifact cleanup. FLUX.1-Kontext-pro edits in context and keeps characters consistent.

Implement workflows to edit generated videos

Remix modifies specific aspects of an existing video while keeping its framework, scene transitions and visual layout. Reference the id of a successfully completed video and supply an updated prompt. Limit the prompt to one clearly articulated adjustment: narrow edits keep more fidelity and cause fewer visual defects.

video = client.videos.remix(
    video_id="<previous_video_id>",
    prompt="Shift the color palette to teal, sand, and rust, with a warm backlight.",
)
# new job: status "queued", remixed_from_video_id == "<previous_video_id>"; poll it as before
  • The workflow is create → poll until completed → videos.remix → poll → download. A remix is a new job with a new id; the original is untouched. List and delete operations manage the history.
  • Remix before the 24-hour retention window ends and download the result.
  • input_reference is a different feature: a still image that anchors the first frame. Starting over with a rewritten prompt loses the structure that a remix keeps.
  • In the jobs REST API a video can also enter through inpaint_items (one video of at most five seconds); that is not the videos.remix call.

Select and apply appropriate generation and editing controls

ControlApplies toValues and rules
sizegpt-image-1 series1024x1024, 1024x1536, 1536x1024; square generates fastest
sizegpt-image-2, 2.5 modelsBoth edges multiples of 16; long edge at most 3,840 px; ratio at most 3:1 (2.5: between 1:3 and 3:1); 655,360–8,294,400 pixels. size=auto may break these rules.
qualitygpt-imagelow, medium, high (2.5 adds xhigh, max, auto). Lower is faster. The how-to says the default is high (mini: medium); set it explicitly.
n, usergpt-image1–10 images (default 1); an end-user id for monitoring
output_format, output_compressiongpt-imagepng (default) or jpeg; WEBP is not supported per the how-to. Compression 0–100 (0 none, 100 maximum, default 100), JPEG output only.
backgroundgpt-image-1 (the docs don't say whether newer gpt-image models accept it)transparent together with PNG output
stream, partial_imagesgpt-imageStream intermediate images (image_generation.partial_image events, up to 3) for faster visual feedback
width, heightMAI-ImageAt least 768 px each; width × height at most 2,359,296 (2.6 models) or 1,048,576 (2.5 models)
guidance, stepsFLUX.2-flexExtra parameters of the BFL provider API, alongside seed, aspect_ratio, safety_tolerance, output_format
  • Guardrails (formerly content filters) wrap every image and video model. For image-generation models DefaultV2 blocks hate and fairness, violence, sexual and self-harm content at Medium on prompts and completions, and adds prompt-side controls for public figures, political candidates, protected art and studio characters, profanity and jailbreaks. A block returns error.code contentFilter with "Your task failed as a result of our safety system" (prompt) or "Generated image was filtered..." (output).
  • Photorealistic images of minors are blocked by default; customers can request access (enterprise-tier customers are approved automatically). Opting out of content filtering requires a Microsoft application.
  • Choose by goal: speed or cost → quality=low, a smaller or square size, gpt-image-1-mini; fidelity or 4K → gpt-image-2 or 2.5 with quality=high; transparent logo → PNG + background=transparent (documented for gpt-image-1); draft preview → stream with partial_images; shorter timeouts → streaming, simpler prompt, smaller size.
Exam traps
  • A mask marks the area to edit with transparent pixels, must be a PNG and must have the same dimensions as the image. Opaque pixels are kept, so an inverted mask edits everything except your target.
  • The Edit API takes multipart form data, not JSON; gpt-image-1 series output is base64 only, so do not ask for response_format="url".
  • input_fidelity does not work on gpt-image-1-mini; WEBP output is not supported per the how-to; size=auto ignores the gpt-image-2 size rules.
  • Sora 2 input_reference must match size exactly, and images with human faces are rejected. seconds is 4, 8 or 12 (not 1–20) on the videos API; n_seconds belongs to the jobs API.
  • Remix needs the id of a completed video, one change per prompt, and creates a new video id. It is not input_reference.
  • Generated videos disappear after 24 hours; the image quota is 5 images per minute by default.

Sources: Image generation how-to · Sora 2 video generation · Foundry playgrounds · MAI-Image models · FLUX models · Agent image generation tool · Default safety policies · Model retirement schedule

sections.title: 3.2 Design and implement multimodal understanding workflows
sections.html:
Skills measured: analyze visual context with multimodal models • concise or detailed captions for one or several images • question answering grounded in visual evidence • alt text and extended descriptions for accessibility • Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools for visual characteristics • video analysis and segments • single-task and pro-mode pipelines • identify objects, components or regions. Practise by sending the same photos to a vision-enabled deployment through the Responses API, then building a custom Content Understanding image analyzer and a video analyzer with segmentation from REST. Document analyzers are in §5.2, multimodal retrieval in §5.1 and visual safety in §3.3.

Build a solution that analyzes visual context by using multimodal models

Vision-enabled chat models are the o-series reasoning models except o3-mini (text-only), the GPT-5 series, the GPT-6 series, the GPT-4.1 series, GPT-4.5 and the GPT-4o series; confirm text and image input for the exact model in the model catalog. Deploy one, then send images and text together through the Chat Completions or the Responses API. The content-part names differ and code questions test exactly that.

Chat CompletionsResponses API
Text part{"type": "text", "text": "..."}{"type": "input_text", "text": "..."}
Image part{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "<URL or base64>"}}{"type": "input_image", "image_url": "<URL or data URI>"} (a plain string) or a file_id
JSON schema outputresponse_formattext.format
response = client.responses.create(
    model="<deployment>",
    input=[{"role": "user", "content": [
        {"type": "input_text", "text": "What is in this image?"},
        {"type": "input_image", "image_url": "https://example.com/photo.jpg", "detail": "high"},
    ]}],
)
print(response.output_text)
  • Supplying an image: a fully qualified URL, a Base64 data URI, or a file ID from the Files API. For a private blob with a SAS URL, enable managed identity on the Azure OpenAI resource and give it a blob read role (the quickstart calls it Storage Blob Reader).
  • Limits (Responses): PNG, JPEG, WebP or non-animated GIF; up to 50 images per request, each under 512 MB, combined under 512 MB. PDFs work too: the model gets the extracted text plus an image of each page.
  • detail: low = lower-resolution copy, fewest tokens, fastest, may miss fine detail; high = finer features, more tokens, slower; auto = the default, the model chooses.
  • Documented limitations: not for specialised medical images; weaker on non-Latin text, small text, rotated or upside-down content, graphs with varying line styles, panoramic or fisheye images; precise spatial localisation is weak and counts are approximate; file names and metadata are ignored and images are resized; CAPTCHAs are blocked; descriptions can be wrong.
  • Portal try-out: Models + endpoints → Deploy model (for example gpt-4o) → Open in playground → task-specific system message → Apply changes → attach an image → prompt.
  • Safety: the default guardrail for vision-enabled chat also covers identification of individuals and inference of sensitive attributes on prompts. A request-level x-policy-id guardrail is not available for image input; the default guardrail is used (§1.4).
NeedUse
Free-form questions or reasoning across one or several imagesVision-enabled model
A fixed schema (fields, classification, segments) from images, documents, audio or videoContent Understanding
Captions, tags, objects and people from a fixed API in an existing appImage Analysis 4.0 Deprecated, retires September 25, 2028
Cited answers over thousands of PDFs and imagesAzure AI Search multimodal retrieval (§5.1)

Configure apps to produce concise or detailed captions for single or multiple images

Model route: the caption style is yours to set. Put the length and content in the instruction ("one sentence of at most 20 words" versus "a detailed paragraph: objects, visible text, spatial relations"), use detail: "low" for cheap concise captions and "high" for detailed ones, and add several input_image parts to one user message to caption or compare multiple images (up to 50). A schema returns both lengths at once:

from pydantic import BaseModel

class Captions(BaseModel):
    caption_short: str     # one sentence
    caption_long: str      # detailed: objects, visible text, spatial relations

response = client.responses.parse(
    model="<deployment>",
    input=[{"role": "user", "content": [
        {"type": "input_text", "text": "Caption this product photo."},
        {"type": "input_image", "image_url": photo_url, "detail": "high"},
    ]}],
    text_format=Captions,
)
print(response.output_parsed.caption_short)
Service featureOutputNotes
Image Analysis 4.0 Caption DeprecatedOne sentence for the whole image (captionResult with text and confidence)Florence-based, English only, only certain Azure regions (otherwise use Image Analysis 3.2)
Dense CaptionsOne sentence for up to 10 regions plus the whole image, each with a boundingBox in pixelsRegion captions, not longer captions
Content Understanding prebuilt-imageSearchA one-paragraph description of the imageA custom analyzer's generate field description steers detail
from azure.ai.vision.imageanalysis.models import VisualFeatures   # pip install azure-ai-vision-imageanalysis

result = client.analyze_from_url(
    image_url="https://aka.ms/azsdk/image-analysis/sample.jpg",
    visual_features=[VisualFeatures.CAPTION],
    gender_neutral_caption=True,          # optional, default False
)
print(result.caption.text, result.caption.confidence)
  • Gender-neutral captions: REST gender-neutral-caption=true, Python gender_neutral_caption=True replaces "man", "woman", "boy" and "girl" with "person".
  • The GA Content Understanding analyze operation accepts a single item in inputs; to caption several images either call a multimodal model once with many image parts or call the analyzer once per image.
  • Choose: any language, tone or length, or several images in one description → vision-enabled model; coordinates per region from a fixed API → dense captions (legacy); stored, schema-bound batch output → Content Understanding custom analyzer.

Implement a solution that enables question-answering grounded in visual evidence

A typical design sends the question and the image(s) in one user turn. Instruct the model to answer only from what is visible, to say when the answer is not visible, and to cite the evidence (the object, region or quoted text). Return a schema such as answer, evidence[], answerable with structured outputs: text.format (or text_format with Pydantic in responses.parse) for Responses, response_format for Chat Completions. Structured outputs enforce the schema; the older JSON mode only guarantees valid JSON. Design around the documented limits: counts are approximate, spatial reasoning is weak, and small text needs a larger image (enlarge it, but do not crop away important detail) or detail: "high".

For many images or PDFs, build an Azure AI Search multimodal pipeline (the portal Import data wizard creates it):

  1. Extract page text, inline images and structure with the Document Extraction skill or the Azure Content Understanding skill.
  2. Chunk the text with the Text Split skill.
  3. Describe images with the GenAI Prompt skill (image verbalization by an LLM).
  4. Embed text and images (Azure OpenAI, Foundry or Azure Vision Preview models), or skip verbalization and pass images to a multimodal embedding model (AML skill or Azure Vision multimodal embeddings skill).
  5. Store the extracted images in the knowledge store, then query with hybrid search (full text + vector + semantic ranking) so answers cite the original image snippets.
CapabilityDocument Extraction skillAzure Content Understanding skill
Text location (pages and bounding polygons)NoYes
Cross-page tables, built-in chunkingNo (use the Text Split skill)Yes (default fixedSize; semantic chunking is Preview, 2026-05-01-preview)
AI-generated image descriptionsNoYes (needs modelName and modelDeployment; 2026-05-01-preview REST API)

Groundedness detection (Azure AI Content Safety) checks LLM text against text grounding sources: modes Non-Reasoning (fast, binary) and Reasoning (explanations); domain Medical or Generic; task Summarization or QnA; optional correction Preview. For images, run it on the verbalized or extracted text, not on pixels.

Configure generation of alt-text and extended image descriptions aligned to accessibility guidelines

  • Microsoft guidance: convey the content and purpose of the image; alt text should be no longer than a sentence or two, often a few chosen words; consider setting, emotions, colors and relative sizes; do not repeat the surrounding text or start with "a graphic of" or "an image of".
  • Charts and infographics: state the insight ("In July, brand A overtook brand B and kept growing"), not just "a bar chart". For flow charts describe the beginning, progress and conclusion.
  • Decorative visuals (stylistic borders) are marked decorative so that screen readers skip them. Generated alt text is approved or edited by the author.
  • W3C: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.1.1 Non-text Content (Level A) requires a text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose; complex images (charts, diagrams, maps) need a two-part alternative: a short description plus a long description of the essential information. Alternatives should match the language of the content.
class AltText(BaseModel):
    is_decorative: bool
    alt_text: str            # one or two sentences, no "image of"; empty when decorative
    long_description: str    # for charts and diagrams: values, trends, structure
    language: str            # match the page language

Pass that schema as text_format as above, use detail: "high" for text-heavy images, apply guardrails to the output and keep a human review step because vision models can produce incorrect descriptions. The Content Understanding option enableFigureDescription (default false) generates natural-language descriptions of figures "for accessibility requirements (alt text generation)"; enableFigureAnalysis (default false) extracts chart data and diagram components. Both are supported by document-based analyzers (§5.2).

ImageProduce
Product photoOne short sentence of alt text
Sales chart or infographicShort alt text with the insight, plus a long description of values and trends
Divider or borderMark decorative, no alt text
Screenshot with textTranscribe the important text in the description

Implement visual understanding by configuring Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools to extract visual characteristics

Content Understanding runs in a Microsoft Foundry resource. It is GA in API 2025-11-01 (use it for production); 2026-06-01-preview is Preview. An image analyzer returns the fields you define (for RAG, chart analysis, manufacturing defect checks, shelf analysis). It is not optimized for text-centric images: use a document analyzer for those.

  1. Create a Foundry resource (Contributor or higher on the subscription or resource group).
  2. Deploy the models and set the defaults: in Content Understanding Studio, Settings → + Add resource → select the resource → Next → Save (keep the autodeployment box ticked), or PATCH {endpoint}/contentunderstanding/defaults?api-version=2025-11-01 with {"modelDeployments": {"<modelName>": "<deploymentName>"}}. The Python SDK also needs the Cognitive Services User role to set defaults.
  3. Analyze with a prebuilt analyzer or create a custom one.
POST {endpoint}/contentunderstanding/analyzers/prebuilt-imageSearch:analyze?api-version=2025-11-01
Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key: {key}
{"inputs": [{"url": "https://example.com/pieChart.jpg"}]}
-> 202 Accepted, Operation-Location: {endpoint}/contentunderstanding/analyzerResults/{request-id}?api-version=2025-11-01
GET that URL every 1-2 seconds until "status": "Succeeded"

PUT {endpoint}/contentunderstanding/analyzers/chartAnalyzer?api-version=2025-11-01      -> 201 Created
{ "baseAnalyzerId": "prebuilt-image", "models": { "completion": "gpt-5.2" },
  "fieldSchema": { "fields": {
    "Title": { "type": "string" },
    "ChartType": { "type": "string", "method": "classify", "enum": ["bar", "line", "pie"] } } } }
  • Prebuilt: prebuilt-imageSearch (one-paragraph description). Custom analyzers derive only from the four base analyzers prebuilt-document, -image, -audio, -video. GA analyze takes one input per request, either a url or base64-encoded data; analyzeBinary uploads the raw file bytes as the request body.
  • Field method: extract is for documents only; generate and classify work for documents, images, audio and video. The method is optional. Up to 1,000 fields and 300 classify categories.
  • Image limits: .jpg .jpeg .jpe .png .bmp .heif .heic, at most 200 MB, 50 × 50 to 10,000 × 10,000 pixels; analyzer ID up to 64 characters (the service-limits page allows letters, numbers, dots and underscores; the 2025-11-01 REST reference pattern also allows a hyphen).
  • Python: pip install azure-ai-contentunderstanding; ContentUnderstandingClient(endpoint=..., credential=DefaultAzureCredential()), then client.begin_analyze(analyzer_id="prebuilt-imageSearch", inputs=[AnalysisInput(url=image_url)]).result() and read result.contents[0].markdown.
  • Where to work: Content Understanding Studio supports both API versions, all prebuilt analyzers, custom analyzers and labeling. The Foundry (new) playground uses the preview API only, offers a partial analyzer set and cannot create custom analyzers. The Foundry (classic) experience was deprecated on July 15, 2026.

Implement video analysis workflows to process and interpret video segments

prebuilt-videoSearch returns RAG-ready output: a WEBVTT transcript, key frames, scene segmentation and per-segment descriptions of people, places and actions. (The overview page names it prebuilt-videoAnalysis once; the prebuilt list and quickstart use prebuilt-videoSearch.) For custom fields derive from prebuilt-video. Processing has two stages: content extraction (transcription with diarization and multilingual support, key frames, shot detection), then field extraction (a generative model fills your fields and segments the video).

enableSegmentResultUse for
false (default)The whole video is one segmentBrand-safety checks anywhere in an ad; full-length summary
true + contentCategoriesSegments of seconds to minutes, defined by a natural-language description; video allows one contentCategories objectChapters, such as news stories
{ "baseAnalyzerId": "prebuilt-video",
  "models": { "completion": "gpt-5.2" },
  "config": {
    "locales": ["en-US", "fr-FR"],
    "returnDetails": true,
    "enableSegment": true,
    "contentCategories": { "news-story": { "description": "Segment the video into each distinct news story. Ignore ads." } } },
  "fieldSchema": { "fields": { "Summary": { "type": "string", "method": "generate" } } } }
  • Segmentation uses the generative model, so it consumes tokens even with no fields. With enableSegment: true one content object is returned per segment.
  • Output: contents[] with kind: "audioVisual", startTimeMs, endTimeMs, markdown, fields. keyFrameTimesMs needs no extra setting; transcriptPhrases and cameraShotTimesMs (shot starts after the first shot at 0 ms; gradual transitions may be missed) need "returnDetails": true. Set locales; an unsupported locale falls back to the nearest one and can be wrong.
  • Limits: .mp4 .m4v .flv .wmv .asf .avi .mkv .mov, 320 × 240 to 1920 × 1080. analyzeBinary (direct upload, used by Studio and Foundry): 200 MB and 30 minutes. analyze by URL (Blob Storage): 4 GB and two hours. About one frame per second is analyzed, frames are scaled to 512 × 512, and only speech is transcribed.
  • Alternative: Azure AI Video Indexer (cloud web app or Azure Arc extension; transcription, translation, object detection, summaries; live streams with bounding boxes on Arc).

Configure single-task and pro-mode Content Understanding pipelines

In the Foundry (classic) experience, which was deprecated on July 15, 2026, you created standard mode or pro mode tasks. The exam outline says "single-task and pro-mode" pipelines, but no live Learn page defines "single-task" any more; read it as the default standard flow (one analyzer, fields out), which is this guide's inference. Pro mode existed only in the 2025-05-01-preview API, and the REST reference says only pro mode supported multiple input files.

Standard (default)Pro (2025-05-01-preview only)
InputsDocuments, images, audio, videoDocuments only
Several input documentsNoYes
Reasoning and an external knowledge base for linking, enrichment and validationNoYes

Status: "Pro mode is only available in the 2025-05-01-preview API, which is now retired." The successor is agentic mode Preview in 2026-06-01-preview:

{ "description": "Calculate and validate totals in an invoice",
  "baseAnalyzerId": "prebuilt-document",
  "models": { "completion": "gpt-5.2" },
  "config": { "workflow": "agentic" },
  "fieldSchema": { "fields": { } } }
  • config.workflow (document analyzers, API 2026-06-01-preview): "default" or omitted lets the service pick a standard or advanced workflow; "agentic" enables agentic mode. The service returns a versioned value such as agentic.2026-06-01-preview. With 2025-11-01 or earlier the property is not available.
  • Use agentic for: multistep reasoning, calculations, validation and visual analysis, returned as schema fields. Limits: one input file per request (it may hold several logically related documents), documents only, no extract-method fields, no labeled samples; plan about 400,000 tokens per minute per analyzer job. It costs more and is slower, and it is not a drop-in replacement for pro mode.
  • Pipeline blocks today (GA): content extraction → optional segmentation (enableSegment with contentCategories: up to 200 categories for documents, one for video; an optional analyzerId per category routes to another analyzer, omit it to only split) → field extraction (extract, generate, classify) → structured JSON.

Implement solutions that identify objects, components, or regions within images or video

Image Analysis 4.0 Deprecated (retires September 25, 2028; calls then fail) is the classic detector: Objects returns each object's name, confidence and a pixel boundingBox; People returns people locations; denseCaptions returns described regions. Call Analyze Image with features=Objects (Python VisualFeatures.OBJECTS).

"objectsResult": { "values": [
  { "name": "Laptop", "confidence": 0.85, "boundingBox": { "x": 471, "y": 218, "w": 289, "h": 226 } } ] }
  • Limitations: objects smaller than about 5% of the image are generally missed, closely stacked objects (a pile of plates) are missed, and objects are not differentiated by brand or product name. Tags can include context such as "indoor" that cannot be boxed; object detection finds only objects and living things.
  • Replacements named by Microsoft: GPT models in Foundry (custom vision solutions), Content Understanding (managed generative extraction), Document Intelligence (OCR), Face API (faces), Cohere Embed or SigLIP (embeddings).
  • Custom Vision (classification and object detection with coordinates) has a planned retirement; full support runs until 9/25/2028. Azure Machine Learning AutoML trains both model types.
  • Vision-enabled models name components well but localise poorly and count approximately; verify boxes and counts with a detector.
NeedChoose
Pixel boxes for generic objects or people in an existing appImage Analysis 4.0 Objects or People (plan the migration)
Boxes for your own componentsCustom Vision (retiring) or AutoML object detection
Which parts, defects or products are present, per image or per video segmentContent Understanding custom analyzer (generate and classify fields) or a vision model with a schema
Time ranges inside a videoContent Understanding segments and cameraShotTimesMs; Video Indexer for object detection
Exam traps
  • image_url versus input_image: Chat Completions nests the URL in an object, Responses takes a string; detail defaults to auto, not low; low can miss small text.
  • Vision-enabled models are weak at precise localisation and counting, so they are not your bounding-box detector. Dense captions are region captions, not long captions, and Image Analysis captions are English only.
  • extract is documents only; image, audio and video fields use generate or classify. GA analyze takes one URL input; larger videos go by URL (4 GB, 2 hours), direct upload stops at 200 MB and 30 minutes.
  • Video segmentation needs enableSegment: true plus one contentCategories entry; shot times and transcript phrases need returnDetails: true; sampling is about one frame per second.
  • Pro mode is not a pricing tier: it lived only in the retired 2025-05-01-preview API and is replaced by preview agentic mode (config.workflow: "agentic", one input file, no extract fields).
  • Groundedness detection is text-based. Alt text is a sentence or two without "image of"; complex images also need a long description; decorative images are marked decorative.

Sources: Responses API · Vision-enabled models · Structured outputs · AI Search multimodal overview · Groundedness detection · Microsoft alt text guidance · W3C complex images · CU analyzer reference · CU limits · CU video overview · CU agentic mode · CU what's new · Image Analysis object detection

sections.title: 3.3 Implement responsible AI for multimodal content
sections.html:
Skills measured: implement filters to classify unsafe or disallowed visual content • detect and mitigate indirect prompt injection by using embedded text in images • enforce visual policy rules, such as applying watermarks, flagging prohibited symbols, upholding brand usage requirements, and detecting potentially inappropriate content. Practise by sending the same test images through the Content Safety image API and through a guardrail-protected vision deployment, then add a document-attack control and see what it does and does not catch.

Implement filters to classify unsafe or disallowed visual content

Two layers exist and the exam asks you to pick one. Azure AI Content Safety is called from your own moderation pipeline (uploads, marketplaces): it classifies and your code decides. Foundry guardrails filter prompts and completions inline on a vision-enabled chat or image-generation deployment.

OptionUse whenNames to know
Analyze imageYou moderate uploaded images and apply your own accept/reject rulePOST {endpoint}/contentsafety/image:analyze?api-version=2024-09-01; body image.content (base64) or image.blobUrl, categories, outputType
Analyze multimodal contentA meme or screenshot whose image and text must be judged togetherimageWithText:analyze (the quickstart uses api-version=2024-09-15-preview); enableOcr is required; text and the OCR output are each limited to 1,000 characters; available only in some regions
GuardrailsYou protect a model or agent without writing moderation codeDefault Microsoft.DefaultV2; a custom guardrail is an RAI policy, assigned with raiPolicyName on the deployment
  • Categories and scale: Hate, SelfHarm, Sexual, Violence. Images support only outputType: "FourSeverityLevels", so severity is 0 Safe, 2 Low, 4 Medium, 6 High. The result is multi-label: categoriesAnalysis holds one entry per requested category (all four if you omit categories). EightSeverityLevels (0–7) exists for text, not images.
  • Limits: up to 4 MB and 50×50 to 7,200×7,200 pixels, per the Content Safety limits page and the image quickstart (the 2024-09-01 Analyze Image REST reference and the Python ImageData docstring still say 2048×2048). Send content or blobUrl, never both (the request is refused). For blobUrl, turn on the resource's managed identity and give it Storage Blob Data Contributor or Owner; the quickstart says only those two roles work. Animated formats: the first frame is analysed.
  • Guardrail defaults: hate and fairness, violence, sexual and self-harm use the Medium blocking level on prompts and completions, which blocks medium and high severity. Vision chat models add a prompt control for identifying individuals and inferring sensitive attributes; image-generation models add controls such as public figures and political candidates.
  • Changing guardrails: Microsoft.DefaultV2 cannot be edited, so create a custom guardrail and assign it. Annotation-only mode on outputs for the four core-harm categories needs approval for modified guardrails.
from azure.ai.contentsafety import ContentSafetyClient
from azure.ai.contentsafety.models import AnalyzeImageOptions, ImageData
from azure.core.credentials import AzureKeyCredential

client = ContentSafetyClient(endpoint, AzureKeyCredential(key))
with open("upload.jpg", "rb") as f:
    result = client.analyze_image(AnalyzeImageOptions(image=ImageData(content=f.read())))

reject = any(item.severity >= 4 for item in result.categories_analysis)   # Medium or higher
Exam traps
  • Image severities are 0, 2, 4 and 6. A test of "> 4" misses Medium and ">= 2" rejects Low.
  • Analyze image only reports scores. Nothing is blocked until your code (or a guardrail) acts on them.
  • Harm categories are not attack detection: a violent photo is a Content Safety case, hidden instructions are a Prompt Shields case.
  • The request-time x-policy-id header is not available for chat with image input: assign the guardrail to the deployment instead.
  • The default Medium level blocks medium and high severity; Low and Safe are only annotated.

Detect and mitigate indirect prompt injection by using embedded text in images

An indirect (document) attack hides instructions in content the model reads for the user: documents, emails, web pages, or text inside an uploaded image. A user prompt attack (jailbreak) comes from the user's own input. Prompt Shields detect both, but they analyse supplied text (userPrompt and documents), so words in a picture count only after your app extracts them. Prompt Shields do not judge harm, accuracy or groundedness, and they are trained and evaluated mainly on English.

ControlDefault in FoundryNotes
User prompt attacksOnScans the user's input
Document (indirect) attacksOff: enable it in a custom guardrailScans text inside the document delimiter at the user-input point; for agents it can also scan tool responses (Preview, supported tools only)
SpotlightingOffPreview: base-64 encodes documents so the model trusts them less; Chat Completions only; more tokens; answers may mention base-64

Pattern for images (ordered):

  1. Extract the text from the image with OCR or a vision model and treat it as untrusted third-party content (Prompt Shields accept model-generated content and content from other sources as documents).
  2. In the Foundry portal choose Guardrails, then Create guardrail, pick Document attack in the risk dropdown, set the intervention point and action, optionally turn on Spotlighting, and assign the guardrail to the deployment.
  3. Put the JSON-escaped text inside the document delimiter in the user message and keep trusted instructions in the system or developer role.
{"role": "user", "content": "Summarize this note. \"\"\" <documents>\n<JSON-escaped extracted text>\n</documents> \"\"\""}

POST {endpoint}/contentsafety/text:shieldPrompt?api-version=2024-09-01
{ "userPrompt": "...", "documents": ["<extracted text>"] }
 -> userPromptAnalysis.attackDetected, documentsAnalysis[].attackDetected
  • The standalone API only reports attackDetected, for the prompt and for up to five documents; your code blocks or reviews. In Foundry, blocking mode stops flagged input before the model processes it.
  • The multimodal API's enableOcr reads the text in an image and moderates it for the four harm categories. It is a harm check, not the document-attack control.
  • Add defence in depth: least-privilege tools and human approval for high-impact actions (design practice, not a Prompt Shields feature).
Exam traps
  • Document attack detection is off by default; user prompt attack detection is on.
  • Indirect-attack detection depends on the <documents> delimiter in Chat Completions messages. Unmarked text is treated as direct user input.
  • Hate, Violence and the other harm thresholds, and image:analyze, do not detect injected instructions.
  • Spotlighting is Preview, applies only to Chat Completions and is a toggle inside the document attack control.
  • Keep trusted system and developer instructions in their own roles, and don't concatenate them into user input or document content.

Enforce visual policy rules, such as applying watermarks, flagging prohibited symbols, upholding brand usage requirements, and detecting potentially inappropriate content

No single service enforces "visual policy". Map each rule to the control that exists, and add your own check where Learn documents none.

Policy ruleMechanismNotes
Mark and trace AI-generated imagesContent Credentials (C2PA signed metadata) plus invisible watermarks, attached by FoundryFoundry can attach them for supported models (the provenance page does not call this automatic): gpt-image-1-mini, gpt-image-1.5, gpt-image-2, gpt-image-2.5-flare, gpt-image-2.5-sunburst, the MAI-Image models and selected FLUX models. The default image-generation guardrail includes a content credentials control
Check a file for provenanceContent Provenance Detection website or APIPOST {endpoint}/contentsafety/provenance:detect?api-version=2026-07-01-preview with {"content":{"uri":"<blob URI>"}}; asynchronous, poll GET /contentsafety/provenance/operations/{id} until Succeeded; images, audio and video
Prohibited symbol or a banned logo that just appearedCustom categories (rapid): create an incident, add sample images, deploy it, then call image:detectIncidents with incidentNamesLLM-based, no training, text and images (Preview). Custom categories (standard) is text-only and its page announces retirement on September 1, 2026 in favour of Language custom text classification. Blocklists match exact text, never images
Brand usage (logo, placement, colours)No managed brand-compliance feature is documented: score each image against your rubric with a vision-capable model, return structured output (see §4.1), and send doubtful cases to a personDesign pattern
Potentially inappropriate contentAnalyze image, multimodal analysis, or guardrailsFirst topic above
  • Visible watermarks: Learn describes invisible watermarks and signed metadata, not a visible overlay. If policy needs a visible mark, apply it in your own pipeline and re-check provenance afterwards.
  • Provenance is not trust. It shows origin and history, not authorship, accuracy or safety. NoProvenanceDetected does not mean a file is fake.
  • Metadata is fragile: editing or re-saving, cropping, resizing, filters, format conversion, transcoding and compression can remove it. An invisible watermark might remain after the metadata is gone.
  • For blob input the detection service uses its managed identity; the how-to assigns Storage Blob Data Reader on the storage account.
Exam traps
  • Foundry attaches Content Credentials and watermarks to supported model output; Content Safety only detects them.
  • A blocklist cannot flag a banned image. Use custom categories (rapid), which accepts image samples.
  • Custom categories (standard) works on text only.
  • Do not assume a service checks logo, colour or placement rules: that needs your own rubric and human review.

sections.title: 4.1 Apply language model text analysis
sections.html:
Skills measured: extract entities, topics, summaries and structured JSON outputs by using generative prompting and Foundry Tools • detect sentiment, tone, safety issues and sensitive content • translate text with Azure Translator in Foundry Tools or LLM-powered flows • customize model outputs for domain tasks such as compliance summarization and domain extraction. Practise by sending one supplier email through a strict-schema extraction call, Language PII redaction, Content Safety text analysis and a 2026-06-06 translate request that uses an LLM deployment.

Implement solutions to extract entities, topics, summaries, and structured JSON outputs by using generative prompting and Foundry Tools

NeedUse
Schema-exact JSON (entities, topics, a bespoke summary) from free textChat model with structured outputs
Standard entity types, no prompt, repeatable resultsAzure Language prebuilt NER (core capability)
Your own entity labels, with labeled examplesAzure Language custom NER (core capability)
Fields from PDFs, images, audio or videoAzure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools: define a field schema, get structured output
Key phrases or summaries in an existing Language workloadLegacy capabilities. Summarization (extractive: ranked source sentences; abstractive: new sentences) retires from Azure Language on March 31, 2029; direct new projects to Foundry models
  • Structured outputs make the model follow your JSON Schema: response_format with type: json_schema and strict: true in Chat Completions, text.format in the Responses API (output_parsed holds the parsed value). They work with the GA v1 API; 2024-08-01-preview was the first version.
  • JSON mode (response_format={"type": "json_object"}, first in 2023-12-01-preview) guarantees valid JSON only. The messages must contain the word "JSON" (otherwise a 400 error), and check finish_reason for length before parsing. Learn recommends structured outputs when possible.
  • Schema rules: types string, number, boolean, integer, object, array, enum and anyOf (never at the root); $defs and recursion work. Every field must be in required (optional = ["string", "null"]), additionalProperties: false on every object, at most 100 object properties and five nesting levels. Unsupported keywords include minLength, maxLength, pattern, format, minimum, maximum, multipleOf, minItems, maxItems, uniqueItems.
  • Function calling: strict: true and parallel_tool_calls=false. Not supported with bring-your-own-data, Assistants or Foundry Agent Service.
from pydantic import BaseModel
from openai import OpenAI
from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential, get_bearer_token_provider

token_provider = get_bearer_token_provider(DefaultAzureCredential(), "https://ai.azure.com/.default")
client = OpenAI(base_url="https://<resource>.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/", api_key=token_provider)

class SupplierEmail(BaseModel):
    vendor: str
    topics: list[str]
    summary: str

completion = client.beta.chat.completions.parse(
    model="<deployment-name>",
    messages=[{"role": "system", "content": "Extract the vendor, topics and a short summary."},
              {"role": "user", "content": email_text}],
    response_format=SupplierEmail,
)
facts = completion.choices[0].message.parsed
Exam traps
  • JSON mode is not structured outputs: it never enforces your schema.
  • A schema with maxItems, a field missing from required or an object without additionalProperties: false is not valid for strict mode.
  • Foundry Agent Service does not support structured outputs.
  • Prebuilt NER returns predefined entity types only; domain labels need custom NER.
  • Key phrase extraction, summarization and sentiment are legacy in Azure Language; the core capabilities are PII, language detection, NER and text analytics for health.

Configure detection of sentiment, tone, safety issues, and sensitive content

SignalUseKey settings
SentimentAzure Language sentiment analysis (legacy, retires March 31, 2029)Sentence labels positive, negative, neutral; the document label can also be mixed (at least one positive and one negative sentence); scores sum to 1. Opinion mining (targets and assessments) needs opinionMining=true on the REST request. Better on smaller text; language defaults to English
Tone (formal, angry, urgent)Chat model with an enum in a structured output schemaLearn documents no dedicated tone detector; Translator tone is an output control
Safety issues in textContent Safety text:analyzecategories, outputType (FourSeverityLevels = 0, 2, 4, 6 or EightSeverityLevels = 0–7), blocklistNames, haltOnBlocklistHit
Safety of model trafficGuardrailsMedium blocking by default for the four harm categories; user prompt attacks on, document attacks off
Sensitive content (PII, PHI)Azure Language PII detection (core)Text PII, Conversation PII and Document PII (the Foundry playground is GA)
POST {endpoint}/language/:analyze-text?api-version=<version>
{ "kind": "PiiEntityRecognition",
  "parameters": { "modelVersion": "latest",
    "piiCategories": ["Person", "PhoneNumber"],
    "confidenceScoreThreshold": { "default": 0.9, "overrides": [ { "value": 0.8, "entity": "USSocialSecurityNumber" } ] },
    "redactionPolicies": [ { "policyKind": "entityMask" } ] } }
  • redactionPolicies was added in 2025-11-15-preview and is also listed in the GA 2026-05-01 REST reference. Policy kinds: characterMask (default; keeps length and offset; optional redactionCharacter), entityMask ([PERSON_1]), noMask (no redactedText), syntheticReplacement (Preview; realistic fake values).
  • piiCategories limits the returned types (without default only the listed ones). confidenceScoreThreshold (a default plus per-entity overrides) and disableEntityValidation (default false) tune detection.
  • The guardrail PII control returns detected, filtered and redacted annotations and needs API version 2025-01-01-preview or later.
Exam traps
  • mixed appears only at document level, and opinion mining is off unless opinionMining=true is sent.
  • Content Safety rates harm; it does not redact PII or score sentiment. Prompt Shields detect attacks, not harm.
  • Translator tone chooses the output tone; it does not detect the source tone.
  • noMask returns no redactedText field; the default is characterMask.

Build solutions that translate text by using Azure Translator in Foundry Tools or LLM-powered translation flows

Text translation API 2026-06-06 is the latest GA release and is not backward compatible with v3.0. Each request chooses neural machine translation (NMT) or a supported LLM such as GPT-5.1; LLM translation needs a Microsoft Foundry resource.

POST https://api.cognitive.microsofttranslator.com/translate?api-version=2026-06-06
Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key: <key>
Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Region: <region>

{ "inputs": [ { "text": "Doctor is available next Monday.", "language": "en",
    "targets": [ { "language": "es", "deploymentName": "<your-gpt-5.1-deployment>", "tone": "formal" } ] } ] }

-> { "value": [ { "detectedLanguage": {...}, "translations": [ { "text": "...", "language": "es" } ] } ] }
targets[] fieldMeaning
languageRequired. Leave the source language out to auto-detect
deploymentNameDefault general = NMT; an LLM deployment name; or a Custom Translator <categoryID>
tone, genderformal/informal/neutral; female/male/neutral. Supported with LLM-based translation
adaptiveDatasetId, referenceTextPairsAdaptive custom translation: a dataset index or up to five reference pairs (pairs make the dataset ID ignored)
allowFallbackDefault true: use a general system if the model lacks the language pair; false returns an error
profanityActionNoAction (default), Marked, Deleted (marker Asterisk or Tag)
  • NMT: high volume, lowest cost (billed per source character), up to 1,000 array elements of up to 50,000 characters each, but a request is capped at 50,000 characters in total, counted across all target languages. LLM: tone, gender, adaptive terminology, context-rich text (billed per input and output token), up to 50 elements of 5,000 characters, and unavailable on a resource with a private endpoint.
  • From v3.0: to becomes targets[].language inside an inputs array. BreakSentence, Detect (use Azure Language language detection), Dictionary Lookup and Dictionary Examples are no longer supported.
  • Adaptive custom translation: 5–10,000 aligned segment pairs, ready in minutes, few-shot retrieval at inference, no training; the API is v1.0 Preview. Custom Translator: a dedicated NMT model, typically 10,000+ pairs, training up to about 48 hours, for high-volume stable domains.
  • Whole files: Document translation, asynchronous batch from Blob Storage or synchronous single document (up to 10 MB, one target language).
  • Own LLM flow (design guidance): call a chat deployment with a system message naming the target language, tone and glossary and telling it to keep placeholders; return segment arrays with structured outputs. Choose it for custom post-editing logic; choose Translator for managed NMT/LLM routing and per-request usage headers.
Exam traps
  • v3.0 code that uses to, BreakSentence or Detect breaks on 2026-06-06.
  • tone and gender do nothing useful without an LLM deploymentName; the default general is NMT.
  • Adaptive custom translation changes terminology without training; Custom Translator needs training and a deployment.
  • Private-endpoint resources can use NMT only.

Customize language model outputs for domain tasks, such as compliance summarization and domain extraction

Use the lightest lever that reaches the quality target, in this order:

StepLeverUse when
1Prompt: system message with role, policy definitions, required sections, tone and a citation rule; few-shot examplesAlways first. These prompt-engineering techniques are not recommended for reasoning models such as gpt-5 and the o-series
2Structured outputs (obligations[], risks[], citations[])The summary needs a fixed shape
3Grounding: retrieve the source text, then check it with groundedness detectionFacts must come from the document or from content newer than the model
4Fine-tuningPrompt and schema still miss style, structure or task quality and you hold good training data
5Purpose-built extraction: Language custom NER, Content Understanding custom analyzerA fixed set of domain entity labels or fields
  • Fine-tuning changes weights: better task accuracy, consistent tone, format or schema, tool use, smaller specialised models. It does not replace retrieval for current information or application-level safety controls; compare against a baseline on held-out data.
  • Methods: SFT learns from prompts and desired responses; DPO from preferred and rejected responses to the same input; RFT from prompts plus a grader that scores generated responses; distillation uses teacher-generated SFT data. Interactive training is Preview and needs access approval; managed fine-tuning is the beginner path.
  • Training types: Standard (regional residency), Data zone (US only), Global (cheaper; data and weights are copied to the training region), Developer (idle capacity, no SLA, may be preempted).
  • Groundedness detection (Content Safety, Preview): task Summarization or QnA, domain Medical or Generic, Non-Reasoning mode (fast, binary) or Reasoning mode (explanations); correction is Preview. It needs the document formatting described in §3.3.
  • Custom NER (core): domain entities from contracts or financial documents. Define the schema, label precisely, consistently and completely, train, evaluate, improve, deploy, extract.
Exam traps
  • Few-shot prompting advice does not carry over to reasoning models.
  • Fine-tuning is not a knowledge feed: current regulations still come from retrieval.
  • SFT needs prompt and response pairs, DPO needs preferred and rejected pairs, RFT needs a reliable grader.
  • Global training gives no data residency; Standard does.
  • Prebuilt NER cannot return domain labels such as "covenant"; custom NER can.

Sources: Structured outputs · JSON mode · Azure Language overview · Sentiment and opinion mining · PII redaction · Analyze text · Text translation · Translate 2026-06-06 · Migrate to 2026-06-06 · Adaptive custom translation · Fine-tuning · Prompt engineering · Groundedness detection · Custom NER

sections.title: 4.2 Implement speech solutions
sections.html:
Skills measured: speech to text and text to speech for agentic interactions • speech as an agent modality, including custom speech models • multimodal reasoning from audio inputs • translate speech by using language models and Foundry Tools. Practise by building one speech-to-agent-to-speech loop, one Voice Live session with a phrase list, one audio chat-completions call and one LLM Speech translation request.

Convert speech to text and text to speech for agentic interactions

NeedUse
Microphone or stream, interim resultsReal-time speech to text: Speech SDK, Speech CLI, or REST for short audio (up to 60 s)
A recorded file, result in the same HTTP call, predictable latencyFast transcription (synchronous, faster than real time)
Prompt-guided, multilingual or translated output from a fileAzure LLM Speech = fast transcription with enhancedMode
Large backlog, results can waitBatch transcription (asynchronous)
An existing Foundry agent must transcribe or synthesize files through a toolAzure Speech MCP tool
Live speech-to-speech with a model in one sessionVoice Live (next topic)
Speech longer than 10 minutes generated from textBatch synthesis API
  • Fast transcription is a multipart/form-data POST /speechtotext/transcriptions:transcribe?api-version=2025-10-15 on https://<resource>.cognitiveservices.azure.com, with an audio part and a definition JSON. Audio must be under 5 hours and 500 MB; for long files pass a public audioUrl in definition. Output is the display form only (punctuation, capitalization).
  • definition properties: locales, diarization (enabled, maxSpeakers; up to 35 speakers), phraseList, profanityFilterMode, channels (channels are merged into one unless you set it) and enhancedMode.
  • Models on the same endpoint: Azure Transcribe (default), Azure LLM Speech (enhanced mode; not a separate API; task is transcribe or translate; optional prompt, up to 20,000 characters) and MAI-Transcribe-2 (check availability and preview status first).
curl --location 'https://contoso-speech.cognitiveservices.azure.com/speechtotext/transcriptions:transcribe?api-version=2025-10-15' \
  --header 'Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key: <key>' \
  --form 'audio=@"call.wav"' \
  --form 'definition={"locales":["en-US"],"diarization":{"enabled":true,"maxSpeakers":2}}'

A speech-in, speech-out loop with the Speech SDK (Python). recognize_once_async() ends after one utterance; call start_continuous_recognition() for long or multi-utterance audio, and set speech_config.endpoint_id to use a deployed custom speech endpoint.

import azure.cognitiveservices.speech as speechsdk
cfg = speechsdk.SpeechConfig(subscription=key, region=region)
cfg.speech_recognition_language = "en-US"
cfg.speech_synthesis_voice_name = "en-US-Ava:DragonHDLatestNeural"
mic = speechsdk.audio.AudioConfig(use_default_microphone=True)
heard = speechsdk.SpeechRecognizer(speech_config=cfg, audio_config=mic).recognize_once_async().get().text
reply = ask_agent(heard)                                    # your agent call
speechsdk.SpeechSynthesizer(speech_config=cfg).speak_text_async(reply).get()
  • Text to speech: neural voices (100+ languages), HD voices such as en-US-Ava:DragonHDLatestNeural and OpenAI voices such as en-US-FableMultilingualNeural. Use SSML for pitch, rate and pronunciation (REST: POST https://<region>.tts.speech.microsoft.com/cognitiveservices/v1, Content-Type: application/ssml+xml). HD voices do not support every SSML tag.

Azure Speech MCP tool (Foundry Agent Service), in order:

  1. Use a Foundry resource on the Agent Service Enterprise tier (otherwise: Invalid tool value(s): mcp). The tool is not supported in network-secured Foundry.
  2. Create a storage account and blob container; with Storage Blob Data Contributor you can generate a container SAS URL with Read and Write.
  3. Create an agent on a tool-calling model (gpt-4o or later).
  4. Agent playground > Tools > Add > Add a new tool > Catalog > Azure Speech MCP Server.
  5. Enter foundry-resource-name, Authorization Bearer = resource KEY1 or KEY2, and X-Blob-Container-Url = the SAS URL (output audio is stored there); select Connect.
Speech roleData-plane access
Owner, Contributor, Cognitive Services ContributorNone (can list keys)
Cognitive Services UserCall APIs, edit custom projects; can list keys
Cognitive Services Speech ContributorSame data access, cannot list keys
Cognitive Services Speech UserView custom projects, call APIs

Microsoft Entra authentication needs a custom subdomain on the resource; the token scope is https://cognitiveservices.azure.com/.default.

Integrate speech as an agent modality, including custom speech models

OptionChoose it when
Voice Live API (WebSocket; managed STT + model + TTS)You keep an existing Foundry text agent and its tools and add live voice; you build telephony yourself
Foundry voice agent (kind: voice, Preview)You want speech-to-speech models, service-managed hosting, built-in telephony (Teams Phone extensibility, Twilio), opt-in transcript and audio storage
Azure Speech MCP toolThe agent handles audio files on request, not a live call
  • Voice Live endpoint: wss://<foundry-resource>.services.ai.azure.com/voice-live/realtime?api-version=2026-04-10&model=<model>. Entra ID is recommended (roles Cognitive Services User + Foundry User; scope https://ai.azure.com/.default). Agent mode does not support API keys. A plain Azure Speech resource supports neither Agent Service integration nor bring-your-own-model.
  • input_audio_transcription.model: azure-speech (works with every non-multimodal model and agent; supports phrase lists and custom speech), whisper-1, gpt-4o-transcribe and gpt-4o-mini-transcribe (only with gpt-realtime / -mini), mai-transcribe-2 (preview). Turn detection: server_vad (default), semantic_vad (only gpt-realtime / -mini), azure_semantic_vad and azure_semantic_vad_multilingual.
  • Voice agent setup: Agents page > Build an agent > Interaction mode = Voice; the mode cannot be changed later. SDK: pip install "azure-ai-projects[voice]>=2.7.0", AIProjectClient(..., allow_preview=True), VoiceAgentDefinition(model_type=VoiceModelType.MANAGED, ...); REST needs the header Foundry-Features: VoiceAgents=V1Preview. store is off by default.
NeedCustomization
A few product names or jargon, no training dataPhrase list: phrase_list in input_audio_transcription (not with whisper-1 or the gpt-4o transcribe models)
Systematic accent, noise or domain errors, labeled dataCustom speech: custom_speech map
Pronunciation of terms in the outputcustom_lexicon_url in voice
Brand voice / the user's own voice (limited access)voice.type azure-custom with endpoint_id / azure-personal with a required model
{
  "session": {
    "input_audio_transcription": {
      "model": "azure-speech",
      "language": "en",
      "custom_speech": { "zh-CN": "847cb03d-7f22-4b11-444-e1be1d77bf17" }
    }
  }
}
  • custom_speech is a dictionary locale → model ID: up to 10 languages, base and custom models can be mixed (one type per locale), the model must be on the same Foundry resource (copy it if trained elsewhere), only with azure-speech; training and hosting are billed separately.
  • Custom speech lifecycle: create project → upload data → train → test (word error rate) → deploy a custom endpoint (not needed for batch only). Plain text (1–200 MB) trains in minutes; audio takes days. Audio: RIFF WAV, 8 or 16 kHz, mono, PCM 16-bit, up to 40 s per clip.

Enable multimodal reasoning from audio inputs

Transcription turns audio into text; reasoning over audio sends the audio itself to a model that can answer about it. Audio-enabled models add the audio modality to /chat/completions (gpt-audio, gpt-audio-mini, gpt-audio-1.5; gpt-4o-audio-preview and gpt-4o-mini-audio-preview are Preview).

completion = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-audio",                                   # deployment name
    modalities=["text", "audio"],
    audio={"voice": "alloy", "format": "wav"},
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": [
        {"type": "text", "text": "Summarize this voicemail and flag any complaint."},
        {"type": "input_audio", "input_audio": {"data": b64_wav, "format": "wav"}},
    ]}],
)
NeedUse
One request: reason over a clip, answer in text and/or speechAudio chat model through Chat Completions (file up to 20 MB)
Live conversation in a browser or mobile appRealtime API over WebRTC (~100 ms)
Live conversation through your own back endRealtime API over WebSocket (~200 ms, server-to-server)
Phone or IVR integrationRealtime API over SIP
Long recording, who said whatSpeech fast or batch transcription with diarization, then a text model
Structured fields or a summary from recordingsContent Understanding audio analyzer (§5.2)
  • Chat audio output formats: wav, mp3, flac, opus, pcm16, aac; audio chat support began with API 2025-01-01-preview. The Audio playground does not support gpt-4o-mini-audio-preview; use the Chat playground.
  • Realtime models include gpt-realtime, gpt-realtime-mini, gpt-realtime-1.5, gpt-realtime-2, gpt-realtime-2.1, gpt-realtime-translate, gpt-realtime-whisper and gpt-live-transcribe; the last three are priced by duration. The WebSocket URL is wss://<resource>.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/realtime?model=<deployment>. The Realtime API does not connect directly to end-user devices; your client terminates the audio stream.
  • The /audio API transcribes files (whisper, gpt-transcribe, gpt-4o-transcribe, gpt-4o-mini-transcribe, gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize; 25 MB per file). Preview models are not recommended for production and do not follow the standard model lifecycle.

Translate speech into other languages by using language models and Foundry Tools

ScenarioUse
Live captions or voice, known source language, up to two targetsSpeech translation (Speech SDK/CLI)
Unknown or switching source languages, natural speech-to-speechLive Interpreter (part of real-time speech translation)
Recorded file, translated with a style promptLLM Speech: task: "translate"
LLM-native streaming translationgpt-realtime-translate (Azure OpenAI Realtime)
Translating text with tone, gender or custom terminologyAzure Translator (API 2026-06-06, GA; NMT or LLM)
cfg = speechsdk.translation.SpeechTranslationConfig(subscription=key, region=region)
cfg.speech_recognition_language = "en-US"
cfg.add_target_language("fr")
cfg.add_target_language("es")                             # two targets: the maximum on a Speech resource
recognizer = speechsdk.translation.TranslationRecognizer(translation_config=cfg)
result = recognizer.recognize_once()
print(result.translations["fr"], result.translations["es"])
  • Two target languages in one call are supported directly. More than two needs a Foundry (multi-service) resource or separate translation services; translation fees apply for each language beyond the second.
  • Event-based synthesis (set voice_name, handle synthesizing) works with one target language only, and the voice must match it. For several targets, synthesize each text yourself with SpeechSynthesizer and speech_synthesis_voice_name.
  • Live Interpreter: no input language is set, language switching is handled in the same session, speech output keeps the speaker's style, and a personal voice is optional (access must be approved). In Python, pass AutoDetectSourceLanguageConfig() without languages.
  • LLM Speech translate adds "task": "translate" and "targetLanguage": "ko" inside enhancedMode. Supported targets: de, en, es, fr, it, ko, ja, pt, zh. The default Azure Transcribe model cannot translate.
  • gpt-realtime-translate connects to wss://<resource>/openai/v1/realtime/translations?model=<deployment>; set the target language in session.update at session.audio.output.language and stream audio with session.input_audio_buffer.append.
  • Translator 2026-06-06 is a breaking change from v3.0 (inputs / value schema); its LLM option requires a Foundry resource.
Exam traps
  • Owner is not a Speech data role. Owner, Contributor and Cognitive Services Contributor give no data-plane access; assign Cognitive Services Speech User (or Cognitive Services User) and make sure the resource has a custom subdomain.
  • LLM Speech is not a separate API: it is enhancedMode on the fast transcription endpoint. Fast transcription is synchronous; batch is asynchronous.
  • Voice Live agent mode needs Entra ID; keys fail. custom_speech works only with azure-speech, only for a model on the same Foundry resource, and for at most 10 languages.
  • A voice agent's interaction mode is immutable and the feature is Preview; the Speech MCP tool needs the Enterprise tier and does not work in network-secured Foundry.
  • 20 MB (audio in chat completions) vs 25 MB (/audio transcription) vs 500 MB (fast transcription). WebRTC is for browsers, WebSocket for servers.
  • Speech translation stops at two targets on a Speech resource, and LLM Speech translate has a fixed list of nine target languages.

Sources: Fast transcription · Azure LLM Speech · Text to speech quickstart · Speech RBAC · Azure Speech MCP tool · Voice Live · Customize Voice Live · Configure a voice agent · Custom speech · Audio chat completions · Realtime API · Speech translation · Translator
