sections.title: 5.1 Build retrieval and grounding pipelines
sections.html:
Skills measured: ingest and index documents, images, audio and video • semantic, hybrid and vector search for grounding • enrichment with custom or built-in skills for text, images and layout • RAG ingestion flow with OCR • connect retrieval pipelines to workflows and agent tools. Build one indexer pipeline end to end (Blob data source, OCR, Text Split, embeddings, index projections), query it with a hybrid plus semantic request, then attach the index to an agent.

Ingest and index content, such as documents, images, audio, and video

Azure AI Search indexes JSON documents only. You load them by push (your code calls the API) or pull (an indexer or a logic app).

PushPull (indexer)
HowIndex Documents REST API or SDK (IndexDocumentsBatch, SearchIndexingBufferedSender); actions upload, merge, mergeOrUpload, delete; up to 1,000 documents or 16 MB per batch; not possible from the portalCrawler over a supported source (Blob Storage, ADLS Gen2, Cosmos DB, Azure SQL, OneLake) with field mappings
FrequencyAny, so near-real-time sync worksOn demand or on a schedule as often as every 5 minutes
Skillsets and integrated vectorizationNot available: skillsets are attached to indexersYes
Data sourceAnything you can turn into JSONMust be a supported source

An indexer reads one data source and writes one index; several indexers can feed the same index. Create the data source and the index before the indexer.

Images are processed by the indexer. Normalization is switched on with imageAction (default none), and enabling it is billed by Search. OCR reads JPEG, PNG, BMP and TIFF; Image Analysis reads JPEG, PNG, GIF and BMP; at most 1,000 images are extracted per document.

"parameters": { "configuration": {
  "dataToExtract": "contentAndMetadata",     // required
  "parsingMode": "default",                  // required: one blob = one search document
  "imageAction": "generateNormalizedImages"  // or generateNormalizedImagePerPage (PDF only)
} }
  • The result is the /document/normalized_images/* node (JPEG; width and height capped at 2,000 px by default, up to 10,000 with normalizedImageMaxWidth / normalizedImageMaxHeight).
  • Multimodal search ingests documents that mix text and images: extraction, chunking, image verbalization (GenAI Prompt skill) or direct multimodal embeddings, and storage of the extracted images. For extraction, the Content Understanding skill keeps layout and cross-page tables (its semantic chunking is Preview); the Document Extraction skill keeps only PDF location metadata, no tables and no chunking.
  • Audio and video are not Search document formats. Run them through Content Understanding (for example prebuilt-audioSearch: transcript, diarization, summary), then index the Markdown or segments it returns (§5.2).
  • Agentic-retrieval knowledge sources for Azure Blob and OneLake generate the data source, skillset, indexer and index for you; the Azure SQL, file and indexed SharePoint sources are Preview.

Configure semantic search, hybrid search, and vector search for grounding

Query shapeUse it for
Full-text (BM25)Exact tokens: SKUs, IDs, names
Vector: vectorQueriesConcepts, paraphrases, multilingual questions
Hybrid: search + vectorQueries in one requestGeneral RAG grounding; the lists are merged by Reciprocal Rank Fusion
Semantic ranker: queryType: "semantic"Reranking plus extractive captions and answers on top of BM25 or hybrid results
"fields": [{ "name": "contentVector", "type": "Collection(Edm.Single)", "searchable": true,
             "dimensions": 1536, "vectorSearchProfile": "vp-hnsw" }],
"vectorSearch": {
  "algorithms": [{ "name": "hnsw-1", "kind": "hnsw", "hnswParameters": { "metric": "cosine" } }],
  "profiles":   [{ "name": "vp-hnsw", "algorithm": "hnsw-1" }]
},
"semantic": { "defaultConfiguration": "sem-1", "configurations": [{ "name": "sem-1",
  "prioritizedFields": { "titleField": { "fieldName": "title" },
                         "prioritizedContentFields": [{ "fieldName": "content" }] } }] }
  • Vector field: Collection(Edm.Single), dimensions equal to the model output (ada-002 fixed at 1536; text-embedding-3-small up to 1536; -large up to 3072), a vectorSearchProfile, searchable: true; it cannot be filterable, sortable or facetable. Algorithms: hnsw (m 4, efConstruction 400, efSearch 500 by default) or exhaustiveKnn; metric cosine for Azure OpenAI. A profile combines an algorithm with optional compression (scalar or binary quantization) and vectorizer.
  • Vector query: kind vector (you send the embedding) or text (needs a vectorizer on the field's profile), fields (up to 10, same embedding model), k, exhaustive, weight. Use the same embedding model at query time as at index time.
  • Hybrid: results are merged with RRF, each list contributing 1/(rank + k) (the docs use 60; unrelated to the vector k). Do not add orderby: it overrides relevance.
  • Semantic ranker: reranks only the top 50 results, so it cannot recall documents the first stage missed; scores @search.rerankerScore run 0–4; captions and answers are extractive (verbatim, not generated). Up to 100 configurations per index, string fields that are searchable and retrievable, addable at any time with no rebuild. It is billed only when queryType=semantic and the search text is not empty (search=* is not).
POST https://<service>.search.windows.net/indexes/products/docs/search?api-version=2026-04-01
{ "search": "TX-4410 waterproof hiking boots",
  "vectorQueries": [{ "kind": "vector", "vector": [0.011, -0.027, ...], "fields": "contentVector", "k": 50 }],
  "queryType": "semantic", "semanticConfiguration": "sem-1", "top": 10 }

With a vectorizer on the field's profile you can send "kind": "text", "text": "..." instead of the embedding. Integrated vectorization pairs an indexing skill with a query-time vectorizer: Azure OpenAI Embedding skill ↔ Azure OpenAI vectorizer; custom Web API skill ↔ custom Web API vectorizer; Azure Vision multimodal skill (Preview) ↔ Azure Vision vectorizer. Vector, hybrid and semantic features are GA in REST 2026-04-01; thresholds, query rewrite and maxTextRecallSize are Preview (latest preview API 2026-08-01-preview).

Implement enrichment by using custom or built-in skills for text, images, and layout

A skillset is attached to an indexer. Skills run over an enriched document tree (nodes such as /document/normalized_images/*); output field mappings decide what reaches the index. Skills bound to Foundry Tools (OCR, Image Analysis, language skills) are free for 20 documents per indexer per day, then need an attached billable Foundry resource.

NeedSkill
Printed or handwritten text from imagesOCR (#Microsoft.Skills.Vision.OcrSkill)
Tags and captions of imagesImage Analysis
Markdown, tables and layout from PDFs and Office files in a new skillsetContent Understanding skill (#Microsoft.Skills.Util.ContentUnderstandingSkill): extraction and chunking in one; GA in 2026-04-01; no 20-document free allowance
The same, in an existing pipelineDocument Layout skill (...DocumentIntelligenceLayoutSkill): outputFormat markdown (default) or text; chunkingProperties only with text
Chunk plain textText Split: textSplitMode pages or sentences; maximumPageLength default 5,000 characters; pageOverlapLength
Vectors at indexing timeAzure OpenAI Embedding skill
Describe images or summarize with an LLMGenAI Prompt (...ChatCompletionSkill, GA in 2026-04-01); chat completions endpoints only, not the Responses API
Your own or third-party logicCustom Web API skill (or Azure Machine Learning skill)
Merge OCR text into the body textText Merge (utility)
{ "@odata.type": "#Microsoft.Skills.Vision.OcrSkill",
  "context": "/document/normalized_images/*",
  "defaultLanguageCode": null,
  "inputs":  [{ "name": "image", "source": "/document/normalized_images/*" }],
  "outputs": [{ "name": "text", "targetName": "myText" }, { "name": "layoutText", "targetName": "myLayoutText" }] }
  • OCR: outputs text and layoutText (bounding boxes); defaultLanguageCode unset means English, unk auto-detects. For images embedded in a PDF the OCR text lands at the end of the page text; use Text Merge to place it in context.
  • Custom Web API skill: HTTPS only. The body and the response both carry values[], each with a unique recordId and data; the response also needs errors and warnings (may be null). timeout defaults to 30 s (max 230 s), batchSize to 1,000, degreeOfParallelism to 5; httpMethod is PUT or POST; use authResourceId and authIdentity for a managed identity.
  • The Azure Vision multimodal embeddings skill, token-based Text Split unit, and the Content Understanding skill's image descriptions and semantic chunking are Preview.

Configure RAG ingestion flow, including documents and using optical character recognition (OCR)

Portal wizard: search service > Import data > RAG > connect to data (Blob Storage, ADLS Gen2 or OneLake, by managed identity) > Vectorize your text (Azure OpenAI, Foundry catalog or Azure Vision) > Vectorize and enrich your images (Vectorize images, Extract text from images = OCR) > Advanced settings (semantic ranking, extra fields, schedule) > review and create. It builds the data source, skillset, index and indexer. It needs Basic tier or higher; the search service's managed identity needs Storage Blob Data Reader and, for embeddings, Cognitive Services OpenAI User.

  • Wizard chunking is fixed: textSplitMode: pages, maximumPageLength: 2000, pageOverlapLength: 500 characters. Generated fields chunk_id (key), parent_id, chunk, title, text_vector cannot be edited; you can add metadata fields. Guidance: start at about 512 tokens (~2,000 characters) with 25% overlap.
  • Custom chunk size or tokenizer, tables and figures → build the pipeline in REST or the SDK: data source → index → skillset (Text Split or Content Understanding skill, embedding skill, optional OCR, index projections) → indexer on a schedule.
  • OCR flow: imageAction on the indexer → OCR skill on /document/normalized_images/* → Text Merge → output field mappings. Digital text PDFs need no OCR.
"indexProjections": {
  "selectors": [{ "targetIndexName": "my_consolidated_index", "parentKeyFieldName": "parent_id",
    "sourceContext": "/document/pages/*",
    "mappings": [ { "name": "chunk", "source": "/document/pages/*" },
                  { "name": "chunk_vector", "source": "/document/pages/*/chunk_vector" },
                  { "name": "title", "source": "/document/title" } ] }],
  "parameters": { "projectionMode": "skipIndexingParentDocuments" } }
  • Index projections turn each chunk into its own search document. The index needs a key of type Edm.String with the keyword analyzer and a parent field of type Edm.String that is filterable and not the key. Recommended: one index with repeated parent fields and skipIndexingParentDocuments; the default includeIndexingParentDocuments adds extra parent documents with null chunk fields (5 PDFs with 100 chunks give 105 documents).
Exam traps: ingestion and retrieval
  • Indexers cannot run more often than every 5 minutes; fresher data or an unsupported source means push, but push cannot run skillsets or integrated vectorization.
  • imageAction defaults to none, so OCR gets nothing; parsingMode must stay default and dataToExtract must be contentAndMetadata.
  • Semantic ranking reranks only the top 50 and cannot find documents the first stage missed; captions are extractive, not generated.
  • RRF k (60 in the docs) is not the vector k (neighbours); kind: "text" fails without a vectorizer.
  • The wizard's chunking (2,000 / 500 characters) cannot be changed; a different size means a custom skillset.

Connect retrieval pipelines directly to workflows and agent tools

NeedChoose
Agent grounded on one existing indexAzure AI Search tool
Many sources, per-user permissions, LLM query planning, reuse across agentsFoundry IQ knowledge base through an MCP tool
User-uploaded or ad hoc filesFile search with a vector store
Reuse and govern the same tools across agentsToolbox (managed MCP endpoint)
New orchestration or workflow codeMicrosoft Agent Framework
conn_id = project.connections.get("my-search-connection").id
agent = project.agents.create_version(
    agent_name="hr-agent",
    definition=PromptAgentDefinition(
        model="gpt-4.1-mini", instructions="Answer from the index and cite sources.",
        tools=[AzureAISearchTool(azure_ai_search=AzureAISearchToolResource(indexes=[
            AISearchIndexResource(project_connection_id=conn_id, index_name="hr-policies",
                                  query_type=AzureAISearchQueryType.SIMPLE)]))]))   # SIMPLE = keyword only; omit for the default
  • Azure AI Search tool (azure-ai-projects>=2.0.0): required project_connection_id and index_name; top_k defaults to 5; query_type defaults to vector_semantic_hybrid (others: simple, vector, semantic, vector_simple_hybrid); filter applies to every query. The index needs searchable, retrievable Edm.String fields, a searchable Collection(Edm.Single) field, a content field to cite and a source URL field. Keyless access: give the Foundry account's managed identity Search Index Data Contributor and Search Service Contributor. A private virtual network needs a connection that uses the Entra project managed identity; keys are not supported.
  • Foundry IQ (Preview features, depends on API version): a knowledge base groups knowledge sources and retrieval settings; agentic retrieval plans subqueries, runs them in parallel, reranks and merges. Reasoning effort is minimal (no LLM planning), low (default), medium or auto (a lightweight first pass that escalates up to medium; needs 2026-08-01-preview and a model on the knowledge base). The agent reaches it through an MCPTool whose server_url is <search>/knowledgebases/<kb>/mcp?api-version=2026-08-01-preview, with allowed_tools=["knowledge_base_retrieve"] and a RemoteTool project connection that uses ProjectManagedIdentity. Hub-based projects are not supported; the project's managed identity needs Search Index Data Reader; ACL-filtered content uses the x-ms-query-source-authorization header.
  • File search: FileSearchTool(vector_store_ids=[...]) after uploading files to a vector store. Toolbox: a versioned bundle of tools served as one MCP endpoint; each tool type can appear once without a name.
  • Workflows: Foundry workflows are Preview and scheduled to retire on December 1, 2026; build new orchestration with Microsoft Agent Framework. There, a context provider injects retrieved text before each model call (Python AzureAISearchContextProvider, mode="semantic" by default or "agentic") or search is exposed as a tool the model calls on demand.
Exam traps: agent tools
  • Different identities, different roles: AI Search tool = Foundry account identity with Contributor roles; Foundry IQ = project identity with Reader.
  • Key-based authentication fails with a private virtual network; use the Entra project managed identity.
  • Foundry IQ through MCP exposes only knowledge_base_retrieve and needs a non-hub project. The page's usage table marks only the Python SDK and REST as supported, yet the same page also has a .NET SDK section, so it contradicts itself on languages.
  • Do not start new designs on Foundry workflows (Preview, retiring); use Agent Framework.

sections.title: 5.2 Extract content from documents
sections.html:
Skills measured: multimodal pipelines that combine OCR, layout analysis, and field extraction • clean, grounded representations for agents and RAG by using Content Understanding • analyzers that generate structured or Markdown outputs by using Content Understanding. Practise by creating one custom document analyzer with a field schema, analysing a PDF through REST and through the Python SDK, and reading markdown, fields, confidence and source from the result.

Extract information by using multimodal pipelines that combine OCR, layout analysis, and field extraction

Content Understanding (CU) is a Foundry Tool that uses generative AI to turn documents, images, audio and video into Markdown or schema-defined JSON. One analyzer chains OCR and layout, optional classification, and field extraction. Generative steps run on your Foundry deployments (a chat-completion and an embeddings model). The GA API version is 2025-11-01; 2026-06-01-preview is Preview.

NeedAnalyzerModel deployment
OCR text only: words, paragraphs, formulas, barcodesprebuilt-readNo
OCR plus layout: tables, sections, figures, hyperlinksprebuilt-layoutNo
Born-digital files only; scans need read or layoutprebuilt-digitalParseNo
Ready-made fields for standard documentsprebuilt-invoice, prebuilt-receipt, prebuilt-idDocumentYes
Your own fieldsCustom analyzer, base prebuilt-documentYes
  • Document config: enableOcr, enableLayout, enableFormula and enableBarcode default to true; tableFormat is html (default) or markdown. returnDetails (default false) adds the element arrays: in the Python SDK DocumentContent.tables is filled only when enableLayout and returnDetails are both true.
  • Field method: extract returns the value as written (document analyzers only), generate infers or summarises (for example a risk level), classify picks one value from an enum. Types: string, number, integer, boolean, date, time, object, array (the Python SDK enum also lists json). Limits: 1,000 fields and 300 classify categories per analyzer. Image, audio and video analyzers support only generate and classify.

Classify and route a mixed batch with contentCategories in the parent analyzer's config:

"config": {
  "enableSegment": true,
  "contentCategories": {
    "invoice": { "description": "A commercial invoice", "analyzerId": "prebuilt-invoice" },
    "other":   { "description": "Any other document type" }
  },
  "omitContent": true
}
  • Each category needs a description (it prompts the classifier); analyzerId is optional, and without it the segment is only categorised. Add an "other" category, or every segment is forced into a listed one.
  • enableSegment true splits a bundle into segments and routes each; false (default) classifies the whole file as one. segmentPerPage forces one segment per page (needs segmentation). omitContent: true returns only the routed sub-analyzer results. Up to 200 categories for documents, 1 for video.
ScenarioUse
OCR or layout onlyCU prebuilt-read or prebuilt-layout (lower cost)
Standard forms on common templates: invoice, receipt, ID, tax, mortgageDocument Intelligence (DI) prebuilt model
Unstructured or varied documents, inferred fields, no labelsCU custom analyzer, zero-shot (contracts: prebuilt-contract)
Highly structured documents with labeled dataDI custom model (as few as 5 labeled samples)
On-premises or air-gappedDI containers: the only option

DI v4.0 (2024-11-30) is the current GA version.

Preview Agentic mode ("workflow": "agentic" in a document analyzer's config, 2026-06-01-preview) reasons over evidence for calculations and validation: one input file per request, documents only, no extract fields, no labeled samples, about 400,000 tokens per minute on the deployment. Preview Synchronous prebuilt-read:analyzeBinaryInline and prebuilt-layout:analyzeInline return the result in the same response (10 MB, 5 pages).

Produce clean, grounded representations to use with agents and RAG by using Content Understanding

Each result.contents[] item holds markdown (GitHub Flavored Markdown that keeps the layout) and fields. prebuilt-documentSearch is the analyzer recommended for RAG ingestion: layout Markdown, figure descriptions, chart and diagram analysis (Chart.js, Mermaid), handwritten annotations, a one-paragraph summary and chunked output (fixed-size or layout-aware semantic). prebuilt-audioSearch returns a transcript and summary, prebuilt-videoSearch segments with transcripts and descriptions. Images that contain text go to prebuilt-documentSearch, not prebuilt-imageSearch. In Azure AI Search the CU skill does extraction and chunking (§5.1).

ElementMarkdown representation
Title, sectionsTitle = level-1 heading; other headings keep the hierarchy
TablesHTML <table> (rowspan, colspan, <caption>) while tableFormat is html
Selection marks, formulas☒ selected, ☐ cleared; LaTeX $...$ inline, $$...$$ display
Page metadataHTML comments: <!-- PageNumber="1" -->, PageHeader, PageFooter, <!-- PageBreak -->
Figures![detected text](figures/1.1 "description"); the description needs enableFigureDescription, chart or diagram data needs enableFigureAnalysis (both default false)

Grounding and confidence. Set estimateFieldSourceAndConfidence: true on the analyzer (a field's estimateSourceAndConfidence overrides it). Each field then returns confidence (0 to 1), source (D(page,x1,y1,...,x4,y4): page plus polygon, in the content's unit, inches for PDF and pixels for images) and spans (offset and length into the Markdown). source is the visual position, spans the text position. GA 2025-11-01 and the preview API support all field types (extract, classify, generate); only document analyzers return confidence. Dates and numbers are normalised automatically. The Python SDK sets string_encoding to codePoint, so content.markdown[offset:offset + length] slices the field text. Route by threshold: the docs illustrate 0.90 for critical fields, 0.80 for important and 0.70 for non-critical; tune on your own data.

Agents. The Microsoft Agent Framework package agent-framework-azure-contentunderstanding (Preview, installed with --pre) analyzes attached files before each model call and adds Markdown and fields to the context. Without analyzer_id it uses prebuilt-documentSearch (documents, images), prebuilt-audioSearch or prebuilt-videoSearch; file_search uploads the Markdown to a vector store instead; run the agent inside async with cu:.

cu = ContentUnderstandingContextProvider(
    endpoint="https://my-resource.cognitiveservices.azure.com/",
    credential=AzureCliCredential(),
    max_wait=None,  # wait until analysis completes (default: 5 seconds, then it continues in the background)
)
agent = Agent(client=client, name="DocumentQA", instructions="You analyse documents.", context_providers=[cu])

Other routes: MarkItDown, the LangChain loader in langchain-azure-ai, Logic Apps, and the SDK helper to_llm_input() (Preview: fields as Markdown with YAML front matter). Guardrails on the connected deployment can warn, suppress generated fields or block analysis; extracted content can remain.

Implement analyzers for generating structured or markdown outputs for downstream reasoning by using Content Understanding

{
  "description": "Policy endorsement letters",
  "baseAnalyzerId": "prebuilt-document",
  "models": { "completion": "gpt-5.2", "embedding": "text-embedding-3-large" },
  "config": { "returnDetails": true, "estimateFieldSourceAndConfidence": true, "tableFormat": "html" },
  "fieldSchema": {
    "name": "EndorsementFields",
    "fields": {
      "PolicyNumber": { "type": "string", "method": "extract", "description": "Policy number, often labeled 'Policy No.'" },
      "RiskLevel": { "type": "string", "method": "classify", "enum": ["low", "medium", "high"] },
      "Items": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "object", "properties": { "Description": { "type": "string" }, "Amount": { "type": "number" } } } }
    }
  }
}
  • baseAnalyzerId must be prebuilt-document, prebuilt-image, prebuilt-audio or prebuilt-video: the only four parents. Analyzer IDs match [a-zA-Z0-9._]{1,64}.
  • models holds model names, never deployment names. Prebuilt analyzers use the aliases prebuilt-analyzer-completion, prebuilt-analyzer-completion-mini (for example prebuilt-*Search) and prebuilt-analyzer-embedding. GET .../analyzers/{id} returns supportedModels; GPT-5.2 is the recommended completion model.
  • Descriptions act as mini-prompts: add location hints, alternate labels and affirmative wording. Model repeated data as an array of object, not JSON in a string, and keep nesting to two or three levels.
  1. Create a Foundry resource in a supported region; deploy a chat-completion and an embeddings model.
  2. Map them once per resource: PATCH {endpoint}/contentunderstanding/defaults?api-version=2025-11-01 with {"modelDeployments": {"gpt-5.2": "<deployment>", "text-embedding-3-large": "<deployment>"}}. Keys are model names or aliases, values are deployment names. A modelDeployments object in an analyze request overrides the defaults for that request. Studio: Settings > Add resource.
  3. Create: PUT {endpoint}/contentunderstanding/analyzers/{analyzerId}?api-version=2025-11-01 with the JSON above returns 201 Created and an Operation-Location header (asynchronous).
  4. Analyze: POST .../analyzers/{analyzerId}:analyze?api-version=2025-11-01 with {"inputs": [{"url": "..."}]} returns 202 Accepted and an Operation-Location that points to /analyzerResults/{id}.
  5. Poll that URL every 1 to 2 seconds until status is Succeeded (Running or NotStarted before); read result.contents[].markdown and fields.
client = ContentUnderstandingClient(endpoint=endpoint, credential=DefaultAzureCredential())
client.update_defaults(model_deployments={"gpt-5.2": "tt-gpt52", "text-embedding-3-large": "tt-embed"})
client.begin_create_analyzer("endorsements", analyzer_json, allow_replace=True).result()
poller = client.begin_analyze(analyzer_id="endorsements", inputs=[AnalysisInput(url=sas_url)])
content = poller.result().contents[0]    # content.markdown, content.fields

The Python package azure-ai-contentunderstanding is GA and targets 2025-11-01. get_defaults() reads the mapping, begin_analyze(..., model_deployments=...) overrides it per call, begin_analyze_binary sends bytes, and AnalysisInput takes url or data plus an optional content_range such as 1-3,5,9-. The .NET, Java and JavaScript/TypeScript SDKs are GA too. The Python README asks you to assign Cognitive Services User, even to the resource owner, before you configure defaults.

Improve quality in this order: sharpen field descriptions, then add labeled samples, then try agentic mode (Preview) for reasoning-heavy fields. In CU Studio open an extraction result, then Label data > upload a sample > Auto label > correct the fields > save > rebuild the analyzer. Use one sample per template. Training works for document analyzers only, not for generate fields, and it cannot fix OCR errors. With 2026-06-01-preview the samples are distilled into the analyzer, with no run-time access to them.

Tools and access. Studio supports the GA and preview APIs, custom analyzers and labeling. The Foundry (new) playground uses the preview API, has a partial prebuilt set and cannot create analyzers; Foundry (classic) was deprecated on July 15, 2026. CU CLI is Preview. Built-in roles: Cognitive Services Content Understanding Reader (read, list, analyze), Contributor (adds create, update, test; no delete of analyzers) and Owner.

Exam traps
  • Names versus deployments. models takes model names (or the prebuilt-analyzer-* aliases); modelDeployments maps those names to your deployment names. Deployment names inside models, or a reversed map, are wrong.
  • Only four parents. prebuilt-layout, prebuilt-documentSearch and prebuilt-invoice cannot be a baseAnalyzerId. Read, layout and digitalParse need no model deployment (and digitalParse is not OCR); the other analyzers need mapped deployments.
  • extract comes with conditions. Document analyzers only, the field needs the source and confidence setting (field level, or the analyzer-level switch as in the receipt tutorial), and it is not supported in agentic mode (Preview). Use generate or classify for values the document does not state.
  • Segmentation is off by default. A PDF with several document types is classified as one unit until enableSegment is true; segmentPerPage applies only when segmentation is enabled.
  • Grounding is a setting. estimateFieldSourceAndConfidence defaults to false (it varies by analyzer). Confidence is 0 to 1, not a percentage; source locates the page region, spans the Markdown text.
  • Both calls are asynchronous. Creating an analyzer returns 201 and analyzing returns 202, each with Operation-Location; poll rather than reading the first response. Tables stay HTML in the Markdown unless tableFormat is markdown.

PairDifference

GAPreview

Ordered steps

Gated release:

  1. Pin production to its current agent version.
  2. azd deploy the candidate.
  3. Capture the version the deployment created.
  4. Validate that version in a fresh version-pinned session.
  5. Promote after approval.

Provisioned onboarding: size PTUs → check quota and capacity → create deployment → buy reservation → verify coverage.

Integrated vectorization: data source → skillset (Text Split + embedding skill) → index with vectorizer (same model) → indexer on a schedule.

  1. Declare MCPTool(..., allowed_tools=[...], require_approval="always", project_connection_id=...) on the agent.

  • All fields in required (optional = ["string","null"]) • additionalProperties: false on every object • ≤ 100 properties, ≤ 5 levels • root not anyOf.

  1. Prompt plus structured outputs. The prompt-engineering techniques are not recommended for reasoning models such as gpt-5 and the o-series.
  2. Ground with retrieval; check with groundedness detection (task Summarization or QnA, domain Medical or Generic; correction Preview).
  3. Fine-tune: SFT = prompt + desired response, DPO = preferred + rejected, RFT = grader, distillation = teacher data. It does not replace retrieval for current facts. Training: Standard (regional), Data zone (US only), Global (cheaper, no residency), Developer (no SLA).

sections.title: Study habits that work
sections.html:
• Build, then read. Do the task in the product first, then read the section to see what you missed.
  • Memorize exact names: menu paths, settings, limits, roles and (for code) object, method and attribute names.
  • Practise the decision, not just the definition. For every feature write "choose it when / do not choose it when".
  • Keep a trap log. Every missed question becomes one line: what I picked and why it was wrong.
  • Use the Missed filter in Quick drill until it is empty, then re-take the full exam.
  • Read documentation dated 2026. Features were renamed and moved between preview and GA recently.

parts.title: Exam-day plan
parts.subtitle: Preparation, pacing, tools allowed and break rules

sections.title: Exam-day plan
sections.html:
The week before

  • Take the full timed practice exam twice, a few days apart; fix every skill rated below 4.
  • Skim the cheat sheets and your trap log — do not start new topics.
  • Run the exam sandbox (aka.ms/examdemo) once so flagging, the review screen and the case-study layout are familiar.
  • Online exam? Run Pearson VUE's system test, clear your desk and room and have government ID ready. Test center? Confirm the address and arrival time.
  • Re-check the official study guide in case Microsoft revised the skills list.

During the exam

TopicApproach
PacingWith 40–60 questions in 120 minutes you have roughly 2.0–3.0 minutes per question. Do not spend more than about 3 minutes on one item in the first pass.
First passAnswer what you know, flag what you do not. Answer every question before time runs out — an unanswered item cannot earn credit.
EliminationCross out answers that use retired, renamed or wrong-direction features. Many questions have two plausible options — look for the deciding constraint (GA versus Preview, required role, prerequisite, order of steps).
Multi-selectCount how many answers are requested ("Select TWO"); each must be independently correct.
Code itemsRead the code once for what it does, then compare with the requirement. Check names, signatures and order before the logic.
Case studiesSkim the questions first, then read the scenario for the requirements and constraints that matter. Re-read the exhibit instead of relying on memory. Breaks are allowed in case studies, but you cannot return to questions seen before the break.
Microsoft Learn buttonOn associate and expert exams Microsoft Learn opens in a split screen (no extra time; Q&A, practice assessments and your profile are blocked). Use it only to confirm one detail with Ctrl+F; if you cannot find it in about 90 seconds, make your best choice and flag it.
BreaksThe clock keeps running during a break, and after a break you cannot go back to earlier questions. You cannot break in the middle of a lab or a problem/solution question set. Use the restroom before you start.
ReviewUse the review screen for flagged items. Change an answer only if you can name the specific fact that makes your first choice wrong.

Sources: Exam duration and experience · Retake policy.
